places.name: Andalen Plantation
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 179 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A Dres saltrice enterprise with a great house, a drying floor, a counting room and a labour row, abandoned at the secession when the people who worked it stopped and the family who owned it did not come back.
why.siteAdvantages: Prime saltrice ground on slack water with a private landing — everything an agricultural enterprise needs, and it still failed, which is the point.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies the house. The fields are worked by the people from the rows down the road, who take the crop and will not enter the buildings.
why.pressures: The house is intact and unlooted, which after two centuries means somebody is maintaining an arrangement rather than a building; nobody will say who.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be occupied within a month if the field-holders ever decided the taboo was over, and the house is worth more than the whole village.

hardConstraints: prime saltrice ground with a private landing
places.hook: A Dunmer plantation that failed with the crop still in the ground, and the house ledgers still name whose fault it was.

places.name: Bogmother
places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 2), 143 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: An ancient sacred site south-west of Stormhold, ruined for centuries and never abandoned, holding relics venerable enough that nobody moved them.
why.siteAdvantages: At the far end of a stone causeway from Stormhold — the causeway exists because the site does, not the other way round.
why.occupantsMotive: A caretaker few keep it swept and the relics in place; the city funds them because being seen not to would be intolerable.
why.pressures: Crocodiles have moved inside the town threshold and the caretakers have decided not to remove them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be robbed within a season if the caretakers left, and the city would blame itself for centuries.

hardConstraints: at the end of a stone causeway
places.hook: A stone xanmeer at the end of Stormhold's causeway that pilgrims tend from the outside and nobody tends within.

places.name: Broken Boom
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 151 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A field-owner's hired guard was stood down without pay at the end of a bad season and walked as far as the channel boom. They took the keeper's lodge, and now the boom only opens for people who have settled with them.
why.siteAdvantages: The one firm bank within two hundred metres of the boom's anchor, high enough that the keeper is not flooded out of the job.
why.occupantsMotive: They are levying what they were owed, one hull at a time, and have told themselves a story in which this is lawful.
why.pressures: Every boat crew in the district has stopped using the channel, which means the levy is falling and the crew is getting less careful about who they stop.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would break up within a month if the field-owners paid the arrears, which they will not.

hardConstraints: the one firm bank at a channel boom's anchor
above the flood, with the boom chain reachable from the door
places.hook: The boom only opens for boats that have settled with the men holding it, and they set the price on the day.

places.name: Branchmont
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 570 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: An Archein saltrice estate south-west of Thorn whose owners embezzled themselves out of existence, leaving a village and no landlord.
why.siteAdvantages: The best saltrice ground outside Thorn's own fields, level and floodable on demand.
why.occupantsMotive: The villagers work it as their own; three separate claimants say otherwise, and one of them is Dunmer.
why.pressures: The dispute is in Thorn's title court and has been for eleven years, which suits the villagers perfectly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be settled violently the first time a claimant arrived with hands rather than papers.

hardConstraints: an estate house with no occupant
places.hook: A contested estate village: two owners, one market, and both sides hiring.

places.name: Breathes-Underneath
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 314 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, hinterland.

why.founding: A chamber under the Loriasel shelf with air trapped in its crown — reached by a crawl through a slot in the rock that is a sump for two months a year and a squeeze the rest of it, and containing, as far as anyone can establish, nothing.
why.siteAdvantages: A limestone void that never drained into anything, sealed by its own roof, with one opening the width of a person.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The divers' landing knows about it and treats it as a test rather than a resource.
why.pressures: The slot floods in the monsoon and the divers argue about how long the crown's air is good for; two people have found out and one came back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become genuinely dangerous rather than merely frightening if the slot silted, and the channel above it is silting.

hardConstraints: a limestone void sealed by its own roof
one crawl in, no second exit
places.hook: Dive under the rock and surface inside it, into air older than the province's name.

places.name: Buried Blades
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 186 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: In 1E 2836 the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War overnight, and in the north that decision was made physical: an entire district's weapons were oiled, wrapped and buried in one pit, deliberately, so that stopping could not be easily undone.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry gravel lens under a low rise — chosen because it drains, which is why the contents are still there and still recognisable.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody guards it. Four villages know where it is and have known for sixteen hundred years, and the knowledge is transmitted as a warning rather than as an asset.
why.pressures: An-Xileel interest in the province's armament has made the pit's existence newly awkward, and one of the four villages has started asking what the others would do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change the north's politics in a week if it were opened, which is the reason four villages have not opened it.

hardConstraints: a dry gravel lens under a rise
places.hook: A Legion arms cache buried where the ground drains, still packed, and somebody is coming back for it.

places.name: Channel Cross
places.whySiteWon: saddle in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 307 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: Where two navigable channels cross, everything stops, so a village stands on the crossing itself.
why.siteAdvantages: The junction of the trunk channel and the Bogmother feeder — every boat in the district passes through it.
why.occupantsMotive: It lives on pilotage: the channels braid and only local people know which arm is open this season.
why.pressures: The pilots have begun charging by the season rather than the trip, which the boat crews call a toll.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be irrelevant if anyone ever dredged and marked the braids properly.

places.hook: Every boat in the district ties up here, so every rumour in the district is on the walkway.

places.name: Climbs-To-See
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 691 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: The north marsh has no rises and no sightlines, so the villages built one: a stack of platforms up a stand of trees, high enough to see the flood coming a day before it arrives.
why.siteAdvantages: Three trunks close enough to brace against each other, on root mat firm enough to take the base frame.
why.occupantsMotive: A flood-watcher through the wet season, paid by four villages; out of season, anyone who wants the view.
why.pressures: The bracing between trunks is the weak point and the trees move independently in wind; two platforms have been rebuilt after storms in a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if one of the three trunks came down, because two will not brace.

hardConstraints: three braceable trunks on firm root mat
places.hook: A lashed tower up three trunks: climb it and the channel network stops being a maze.

places.name: Crystalgate
places.whySiteWon: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 679 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal has to be cut, graded and sold somewhere that is not the city, because the city taxes what passes its gates.
why.siteAdvantages: On the road between the diggings and the Tear road, at the first spring outside Stormhold's jurisdiction.
why.occupantsMotive: The cutting houses are guild-like and hereditary; the town exists entirely downstream of one skill.
why.pressures: The vicecanons want the cutting inside the walls and have tried tariffs twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse into a road village the day the Silyanorn seams ran out — which the diggers say is a generation away.

places.hook: The cutting houses buy raw crystal and sell finished work, and they do not ask which digging it came from.

places.name: Cut-And-Stack
places.whySiteWon: box canyon in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 130 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.murkwater (+0.57).

why.founding: The north's only fuel that is not carried: peat banks cut in the dry months and stacked to dry, worked by three villages that have no timber worth burning.
why.siteAdvantages: A raised bog on the plain edge, deep enough to cut for three generations and dry enough to stack on.
why.occupantsMotive: Fuel, and the fact that a stack of turves is the closest thing a village here has to money in a bank.
why.pressures: The cut face is a wall of exposed peat that catches in a dry year and then burns underground for months, which has happened twice and is why the villages now cut in strips.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned as too dangerous if a fire ever reached a stack rather than a face.

hardConstraints: a raised bog with a cuttable face
places.hook: Cut peat, dry fuel and a crew who will trade both for news off the road.

places.name: Cut-In-The-Wall
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 795 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The Stormhold ravine system has more wall than floor, and the households the terraced city could not house cut their own dwellings into a side ravine's face — outside the city's walls, and outside its rents.
why.siteAdvantages: A soft band in the ravine wall, easy to cut and above the wet-season torrent, with the city's lights visible round the bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Rent. There is none here, and that fact organises the whole community, which describes itself as a neighbourhood and is described by the vicecanons as an encroachment.
why.pressures: The vicecanons have twice sent surveyors to establish whether the cuttings are within the city's boundary; both surveyors were treated hospitably and both reports were inconclusive.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be inside the city, and paying, within a year of a survey that came back conclusive.

hardConstraints: a soft cuttable band in a ravine wall
places.hook: Houses cut into the ravine wall below Stormhold: a bed, a fire, and the city's lights round the bend.

places.name: Draws-The-Herds
places.whySiteWon: spring head in border mountains (danger band 3), 1632 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, parent.

why.founding: When the northern floodplain dries, every animal on it walks to the same three tree-islands for water, and for two months this ground holds more meat, more predators and more people than anywhere else in the region.
why.siteAdvantages: The last standing water on the plain: three spring-fed pools under tree cover that do not fail in a normal dry year.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages hunt it under an allocation they renegotiate every year at Wolk Market, and the negotiation is the region's real political calendar.
why.pressures: A long dry year concentrates everything harder and the allocation stops holding; the last time it failed, two villages did not speak for a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the villages' year as they organise it if the springs failed, which is the thing the north actually fears.

hardConstraints: spring-fed pools that survive the dry season, out on the floodplain
tree cover on open flat ground, no hill within a kilometre
places.hook: In the dry months every animal on the plain comes to these three pools, and so does everything that eats them.

places.name: Dreams-By-The-Ash
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 385 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, route.

why.founding: A wallow and a hut on the Dunmer frontier, where an Argonian rite has acquired Dunmer clients — the holdings' people come for visions their own tradition does not offer, and pay considerably better than the villages do.
why.siteAdvantages: A warm seep in an ash-fall hollow where nothing grows tall, so the hollow is genuinely dark and genuinely quiet within twenty paces of the rim.
why.occupantsMotive: One keeper, who has become quietly wealthy and is regarded with suspicion by both cultures for exactly that reason.
why.pressures: The holdings' elders disapprove and their children come anyway; the nearest Argonian village considers the whole arrangement a sale of something that should not be sold.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be closed by the village, not the holdings, the day the keeper took a Dunmer apprentice.

hardConstraints: a warm seep in an ash hollow
dark and quiet within twenty paces
places.hook: Sleep in the warm seep and you are told something; the people here will read it back to you.

places.name: Feeds-The-North
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 268 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A deep bend where the northern river slows and the fish hold — the single most productive water in the region, worked by four villages' boats and argued over by all of them for as long as anyone has counted.
why.siteAdvantages: A scoured hole below a gravel shoulder: deep, cold, and reliably occupied, which no other water in the north is.
why.occupantsMotive: It feeds four villages and is the reason three of them are where they are; the boats work it in a rotation nobody wrote down and everybody can recite.
why.pressures: The rotation has held for generations and is now under pressure from Stormhold's market buyers, who pay for volume and do not care whose week it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be fished out in three seasons if the rotation broke, and every fisher on it knows the number.

hardConstraints: a deep scoured hole below a gravel shoulder
four villages within a morning's row
places.hook: The deepest hole in the northern water, always occupied, and the village's rotation stake says by what.

places.name: Anachronistic Library
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 1157 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, remote.

why.founding: A collection inside an Ayleid tomb that contains books written long after the tomb was sealed, and continues to acquire them.
why.siteAdvantages: The deepest dry chamber of the fenlord's complex — the only room in the north where paper survives.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing tends it and it is nonetheless catalogued, in a hand that changes every few centuries.
why.pressures: The Conclave of Baal at Stormhold reads the Elder Scrolls with an ancient tablet, and the tablet's provenance leads here.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the single most valuable room in the province if anyone could carry anything out of it.

hardConstraints: part of Gandranen Ruins, its deepest dry chamber
places.hook: The one room in the north where paper survived, and what it says about the Duskfall is in no other book.

places.name: Gandranen Ruins
places.whySiteWon: saddle in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 1197 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, remote, route.

why.founding: A Barsaebic Ayleid fenlord's tomb, undead-guarded, whose library has never stopped attracting volumes.
why.siteAdvantages: Sunk in fen on the least accessible ground within a day of Stormhold — the fenlord chose privacy.
why.occupantsMotive: The dead here still hold the office they held; nothing living has taken the place from them.
why.pressures: Books keep arriving. Nobody can say how, and the Conclave at Stormhold has views it will not share.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a Synod prize the day anyone proved the collection could be moved.

hardConstraints: a fenlord's burial complex with its lower course under water
places.hook: A fenlord's tomb sunk in the fen, guarded by its own dead, with the library still dry below it.

places.name: Greylight
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 1192 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-charge-pond (+1.22).

why.founding: A Hist stands here, so a village does; the north's Hist are fewer and further apart than the interior's, which makes each one political.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm hummock in the Shadowfen channels, the only one within half a day.
why.occupantsMotive: The village mediates for four water-villages that have no tree of their own, which gives it standing it did not seek.
why.pressures: Stormhold wants the tree's sanction for things the tree has no opinion about, and sends gifts about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not move; a Hist village does not. But its politics could change in a season.

hardConstraints: a living Hist on firm ground
places.hook: The only firm ground for half a day, and the Hist here will take a stranger's question.

places.name: Hackwing Wall
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in border mountains (danger band 3), 1290 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A cliff on the rim road where the carrion birds roost in hundreds, kept rather than merely tolerated by the village below, which puts its dead animals out for them and gets a clean bone-yard in return.
why.siteAdvantages: A south-facing wall with ledges at every height, warm in the afternoon, above ground nobody can farm anyway.
why.occupantsMotive: The village feeds the roost deliberately; the birds are a disposal system, an early-warning system and, twice, a weapon.
why.pressures: Travellers on the ridge path below who do not know the arrangement have been badly frightened and occasionally worse.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in a season if the village stopped putting carcasses out, and the village would then have to bury things.

hardConstraints: a ledged south-facing cliff above a road
places.hook: The village feeds its dead animals to the birds on this wall; walk under it unannounced and you are the offering.

places.name: Hatching Pools
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 217 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, parent, route; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-shut-village (+1.55).

why.founding: The regional hatchery: the one institution a depopulating province cannot let lapse, rebuilt after Umbriel, and after an older massacre the counting stones record but nobody now dates.
why.siteAdvantages: Warm spring-fed shallows at a constant temperature, screened on every side — the pools were found, not made.
why.occupantsMotive: The Keepers of the Shell stay because the alternative is that a generation is not born; canon shows them dying rather than leaving.
why.pressures: It has been attacked twice in living memory and is defended accordingly; outsiders are not welcome and are not always refused.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the single greatest loss the north could suffer, which is why it is the most defended non-city site in the province.

places.hook: Warm shallows the Keepers guard, where a stranger who is vouched for is safe and a stranger who is not is not.

places.name: Hissmir
places.whySiteWon: island in firm lowland (danger band 2), 450 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, danger, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.sits-above-the-flood (+0.78).

why.founding: Canon's one settlement that exists to receive comers it may not refuse: the Trials of the Burnished Scales reconnect the Hist-less, and anyone — lukiul, exile, even non-Argonian — may attempt them.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground at the head of a pilgrim water route in Shadowfen, deliberately reachable: a place whose whole function fails if it is hard to find.
why.occupantsMotive: Trial marshals and stewards who administer rather than defend; the Zaht stones of Hist amber do the defending, and the Hist no longer makes more of them.
why.pressures: The lodging is built for a traffic the town no longer has — the Mages and Fighters Guild halls that housed pilgrims were dissolved in the Fourth Era and their dormitories now hold people who came for a trial and stayed.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the An-Xileel ever declared the trials invalid, the province's only route back to a Hist would close, and every Hist-less settlement in the catalogue would have nowhere to send anyone.

hardConstraints: landing on a pilgrim water route
firm ground for a Hist and a trial ground
places.hook: The pilgrims' first firm ground: beds, a trial to sign for, and everyone here has walked the route you are about to.

places.name: Hixinoag
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 621 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, route, ring; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-whispers-dig (+1.72).

why.founding: The province's one genuinely drifting village: a jumble of huts half-sunk in mud that moves with the flood cycle along the northern caravan route.
why.siteAdvantages: It occupies two or three fixed moorings in turn, chosen because each is good at a different water level.
why.occupantsMotive: The people move because moving is cheaper than repairing, and because being hard to find has been good for them.
why.pressures: Caravans that miss the mooring lose a day; the village charges accordingly and is not sorry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would settle permanently only if one mooring became good in every season, which the hydrology forbids.

hardConstraints: two or three fixed moorings on one route
places.hook: A village that moves with the water level — find it at the right mooring and it will carry you on.

places.name: Hutan-Tzel
places.whySiteWon: spring head in firm lowland (danger band 2), 50 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: An old tribal village on the Panther River where it drains into its basin, holding the western approach to the north; canon gives it its own tribe, its own elder naheesh and a xanmeer, Xal Irasotl, close enough to be the tribe's charge rather than its neighbour.
why.siteAdvantages: The basin edge: still water for the village, running water for the trip downstream, and a rock shelf the flood never takes — the reason the Imperial maps call it Rockguard.
why.occupantsMotive: The tribe stays because the Hist speaks here and because the totem line is theirs to keep; they are, uniquely for the interior, cautiously willing to deal with outsiders, and have been since the 2E.
why.pressures: The rune-carved totems attract dangerous things if meddled with, and outsiders meddle; the old 3E rivalry with Glenbridge across the fringe has never quite ended, and Su-Zahleel survivors who fled the Xit-Xaht are still absorbed here without being made kin.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close to outsiders entirely the first time a meddled totem killed one of its own, and the western approach would close with it.

hardConstraints: a rock shelf above the flood line
a totem perimeter with clear ground inside it
places.hook: Still water on one side, running water on the other, and boats downstream every morning.

places.name: Keeps-The-Second-Hammock
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 35 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.stands-on-the-island (+0.41).

why.founding: The north marsh's second tree hammock, half the size and twice as awkward, settled by people who could not get standing room on the first and have spent three generations being defined by that.
why.siteAdvantages: Ground, of a sort: a thin cap of soil over root mat, dry most years, and out of the first hammock's line of sight, which its people consider an advantage.
why.occupantsMotive: They rent nothing and take nobody in, which is a policy rather than a shortage, and they are fiercely clear about the difference.
why.pressures: The soil cap is thin and the burials are shallow; the hammock floods about one year in seven, and when it does they have to ask.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would give up the policy the second time it floods in a decade, and the first hammock is counting too.

hardConstraints: a second, smaller hammock with marsh on every side
beside Stands-On-The-Hammock, out of its line of sight
places.hook: The smaller island takes in anyone the first island turned away, and will tell you about it at length.

places.name: The Let Upper Floor
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 17 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Canon records no Dominion presence inside Black Marsh in the Fourth Era, and the Thalmor are nonetheless one of the standing explanations for the Accession War — a post that does not exist is the only form that reconciles the two, so this one is a rented upper floor above a Velothi factor's counting room on the Tear road, taken on a three-year lease by a party the landlord has never met.
why.siteAdvantages: It overlooks the weighbridge where every cart off the Morrowind road is broken open and counted, so a tenant who never leaves the room can audit the whole northern traffic in ore, saltrice and people from a shuttered window.
why.occupantsMotive: To know what the An-Xileel are moving north before Morrowind does, and to be able to stop knowing it within an hour if anyone comes up the stair.
why.pressures: The landlord's grandson has begun to resent a tenant who pays a year in advance and burns a lamp all night, and has twice tried the door.
why.wouldChangeIf: An hour's warning empties it completely: the lease is in a dead Dunmer's name, the ledgers are in wax, and there would be nothing in the room but a cold lamp and a good chair.

hardConstraints: an existing occupied building with a separate outside stair
a sightline onto a weighbridge or toll
places.hook: A rented upper room over Stormhold's weighbridge; from its shutter you can count every cart out of Morrowind.

places.name: Sings-Under-Water
places.whySiteWon: spring head in upland hills (danger band 3), 777 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: Canon puts lamias in the flooded caverns beneath Loriasel, the Barsaebic Ayleid site raised to the Ten Ancestors; the nest is older than anyone's memory of it and the ruin above is the reason the cavern was ever opened.
why.siteAdvantages: A spring-fed system under Ayleid foundations, half-flooded, with one dry mouth and no other way in that a person can use.
why.occupantsMotive: A nest. It sings, it is not a person, and it sorts what it takes by nothing at all.
why.pressures: Antiquarians keep reaching the ruin above and keep hearing the sound come up through the floor; the count of who went down is kept at the mouth.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the nest would open the only Ayleid undercroft in Shadowfen that has never been robbed — which is exactly why nobody has cleared it.

hardConstraints: beneath or beside a Barsaebic Ayleid ruin
a flooded cavern system with a dry mouth
places.hook: A half-flooded Ayleid system with one dry mouth, and something in it that sings under the water.

places.name: Mazzatun
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 246 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The Xit-Xaht built in stone after the Duskfall said not to, under the direction of a Hist they had enslaved with sap.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep in the north-east swamp on ground nobody else contests, screened by rootland and reputation together.
why.occupantsMotive: Tsono-Xuhil's convalescent sleep is canon-indefinite; three and a half centuries on the Amber Plasm seep has resumed and the building has restarted.
why.pressures: The neighbours say only 'the Hist is crazy' and stay away — which is the only reason the building has never been stopped.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a province-wide emergency the day another tribe accepted the Xit-Xaht's invitation to help.

places.hook: The Xit-Xaht build in stone and welcome visitors, and the welcome is the part to think about.

places.name: Tsono-Xuhil
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 319 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on bound, landform, danger.

why.founding: A Hist coerced with sap into directing a city's construction, and left in a convalescent sleep that canon never ends.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands where it always stood; the city was built around it, not the other way round.
why.occupantsMotive: The Xit-Xaht tend it in the way a farmer tends a crop, and describe that as devotion.
why.pressures: The seep has resumed, slowly, which either means it is healing or that it is dreaming again.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change everything in the north if it woke — and there is a mnemic egg here that might tell you which it is doing.

hardConstraints: part of Mazzatun, at the city's centre
places.hook: A Hist that has been harmed and knows it, and will say what was done to it if you can stand to hear it.

places.name: Murkwater
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 391 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.cut-and-stack (+0.57).

why.founding: A Shadowfen village with a Shadowscale association, liberated by them in 2E 582 and the story is still told, which is not the same as the place still mattering.
why.siteAdvantages: A Hist on a firm hummock in the channel network, with water approaches on every side.
why.occupantsMotive: It stays because the Hist is here; it keeps its Shadowscale connection because the connection has twice saved it.
why.pressures: The Archon sanctuary closed in 4E 187, so the surviving ku-vastei who lives here is the last of an institution.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a pilgrimage site the day the Shadowscales were publicly ended, and the village would hate that.

places.hook: A Hist village on a hummock with water on every side, and a retired executioner who kept her tools.

places.name: Murkwater Tempering Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 467 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on bound, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: Children born under the Shadow were given up and made into something else, and the making happened on set ground, away from the village.
why.siteAdvantages: A screened hollow an hour from Murkwater — close enough to deliver a child to, far enough that nobody heard.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it now. The Archon sanctuary closed in 4E 187 and the ground has had no purpose since.
why.pressures: The equipment is still here, and the ku-vastei in the village has never come back to remove it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be destroyed the day someone decided the institution should not be reconstituted — and someone will try.

hardConstraints: screened from a village, within an hour of it
places.hook: The screened hollow where Shadowscale children were tempered, with the fittings still bolted to the trees.

places.name: Names-The-Year
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 402 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: The northern villages hold their naming-day together, on one flat, once a year, because a name given in front of four villages is a name none of them can later dispute.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry meadow equidistant from four villages with a single old tree at one end that every naming has happened under.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the ground belongs to the naming and to nothing else, and grazing it is considered rude rather than illegal.
why.pressures: The An-Xileel's registrars have begun attending, notebooks out, and the villages have not decided whether that makes a name safer or less theirs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its whole point the year the registry started issuing the names instead of recording them.

hardConstraints: a dry meadow equidistant from four villages
places.hook: Four villages meet under one tree to name the year, and this year they cannot agree what to call it.

places.name: Nine Fords
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 32 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.saltmarch-village (+1.05).

why.founding: Nine shallow crossings within a kilometre, and one family that put a gate on the only one passable in the wet — the town grew around the gate, as toll towns do, and is now larger than its reason.
why.siteAdvantages: The one crossing of the nine with a gravel bottom, which means it is the only one a loaded cart can use for four months of the year.
why.occupantsMotive: The toll, and everything that attaches to a toll: stabling, warehousing, a tradehouse, a moneylender and two people who will move goods around the gate for a price.
why.pressures: The other eight fords are usable in the dry, so the town is rich for four months and idle for eight, and its whole social order is built on that rhythm.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse into a village if anyone built a bridge, which Stormhold has proposed twice and the town has bought off twice.

hardConstraints: a gravel-bottomed ford passable in the wet
places.hook: The only ford a loaded cart can use, a toll to match, and carters who resent both.

places.name: Nine Marks
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 309 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Nine identical marks cut into nine separate boulders spread over two kilometres of plain, in a script that is not Ayleid, not Jel and not Daedric, and the locals have decided collectively not to find out what happens if you complete them.
why.siteAdvantages: Erratic boulders on open plain, visible from each other, which is presumably why whoever cut them chose these nine.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The nearest village keeps the grass down around each boulder, which they will describe as tidiness.
why.pressures: A Whispers scholar has established that one mark is unfinished and has asked to finish it; every village within a day has said no, in writing, which is remarkable in itself.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be finished within a month if the scholar could find one office-holder willing to sign, and she is still looking.

hardConstraints: nine erratic boulders inter-visible over two kilometres
places.hook: Nine cut boulders in sight of each other; read in order they are a route, and the route is still walkable.

places.name: Nine-Stone Bench
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 175 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Small diggings and a polishing bench for the stones the province is genuinely famous for — set up outside Crystalgate by a cutter who was refused a grading-house place and has been proving a point ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel terrace with garnet and jasper in the wash, and clean spring water for the polishing wheel, which Crystalgate's own water is too silty for.
why.occupantsMotive: One cutter, two apprentices, and a deliberate policy of selling ungraded to anyone at all, which is heresy in Crystalgate and popular everywhere else.
why.pressures: The grading houses have twice had the bench's output declared uncertified at Wolk Market; both times it sold anyway, and the second time for more.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bought out and closed within a year if the grading houses ever offered money instead of censure.

hardConstraints: clean water for a polishing wheel
places.hook: Garnet and jasper out of the wash, cut and polished on site, sold under Crystalgate's price.

places.name: One-House-High
places.whySiteWon: isthmus in firm lowland (danger band 3), 546 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, hinterland, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: A single household on a rise too small for a second house, which has taken in travellers for four generations because there is nowhere else between the pass and the plain to stop.
why.siteAdvantages: A pinnacle of firm ground exactly where the pass road meets the flood plain — one house's worth, and no more.
why.occupantsMotive: They are innkeepers by geography rather than by trade, and are frank that they would prefer not to be.
why.pressures: Too many travellers, one house, and a road that delivers them at the worst hours; the household has begun turning people away and the road has begun resenting it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a road station with a garrison if Stormhold ever noticed how many people sleep in that yard.

hardConstraints: a low rise on the flood plain, not a hill
on the pass road where it comes out onto the plain
places.hook: One house between the pass and the plain, and they will take you in, grudgingly, for a price.

places.name: Puts-Down-The-Cup
places.whySiteWon: island in firm lowland (danger band 2), 57 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal trade pays in coin and its dockside pays it straight back out in daril; this house on the terrace road is where the city's cutters send the ones who cannot stop.
why.siteAdvantages: Far enough up the terrace road that walking back down for a drink takes two hours, which is the entire therapeutic theory of the place.
why.occupantsMotive: Run by a former cutter with a shaking hand, funded by a levy the cutting houses pay and pretend is charity rather than insurance.
why.pressures: The cutting houses want the house to take anyone they send and the house wants to choose; the levy is renegotiated every year and is used as leverage every year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close in a season if the levy stopped, and the cutting houses know exactly how much that would cost them.

hardConstraints: two hours' walk from the nearest supply
on a road, not off it
places.hook: A withdrawal house two hours' walk above the nearest drink, which is the entire treatment.

places.name: Reedmoor
places.whySiteWon: natural harbour in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 272 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-thousand-birds (+2.12).

why.founding: Shadowfen's channels have no dry ground worth building on, so the villages stand on legs over the water.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide slow reach with a firm bed for piling — the bed matters more than the bank here.
why.occupantsMotive: It fishes, cuts reed and poles cargo for the trunk route; three trades, none of which need land.
why.pressures: The bed is silting and the piles are being driven shorter each rebuild, which the elders discuss constantly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move two hundred metres downstream, entire, in the way this province's villages always have.

places.hook: A stilt village over slow water: reed, fish, a bed on legs, and poled cargo leaving at dawn.

places.name: Rimfield
places.whySiteWon: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 773 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: On the rim shelf above the pass the marsh rules stop: the water is clean, the nights are cold, and a village can keep grain — so a village does, and sells it to a lowland that cannot.
why.siteAdvantages: A broad south-facing shelf with a spring at the back of it, above the fever line and below the snow.
why.occupantsMotive: Grain, wool and the pass trade; every party crossing the rim buys here because the alternative is carrying four days of food up a mountain.
why.pressures: The shelf is small, the village has filled it, and the young are going down to Stormhold rather than up onto worse ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become a summer grazing station within two generations at the current rate of leaving.

hardConstraints: a rim shelf above the fever line
a spring at the back of the shelf
places.hook: A terrace village above the fever line — the first night in the north where nobody wakes up sweating.

places.name: Riverwalk
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 37 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: The northern trunk's mid-point: a village strung along a channel because the channel is the street.
why.siteAdvantages: Two hours' poling from either end of the day's run — the trunk route's natural halt.
why.occupantsMotive: It lives on the ferry stage, the toll and feeding boat crews; nothing here is grown.
why.pressures: Alten Corimont's captain and Thorn's field-owners both think the toll should be theirs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bypassed if a deeper channel opened south, and the villagers watch the silt for exactly that.

hardConstraints: a navigable channel as the main street
places.hook: The trunk channel's natural halt, where the toll is argued nightly and two cities claim it.

places.name: Saltmarch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 325 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.nine-fords (+1.05).

why.founding: A field village of Argonians and Dunmer working the same crop, founded when the estates broke up and the labour stayed.
why.siteAdvantages: In the middle of the terraces, on the one rise that never floods, equidistant from four banks.
why.occupantsMotive: They farm together and marry separately, which is the arrangement and has been for three generations.
why.pressures: Thorn's title court could dissolve their common holding with one ruling and they know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would split cleanly in two along a line everyone can already see, if it ever came to that.

hardConstraints: a rise inside the terrace system
places.hook: Grass, dry beds and four banks' worth of gossip on the one rise that never floods.

places.name: Silyanorn Diggings
places.whySiteWon: ravine in firm lowland (danger band 3), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Stormhold's crystal trade comes out of a Barsaebic Ayleid undercity that the city has been quarrying for centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: The ravine walls below the city expose the Ayleid galleries directly — the diggings are the ruin, entered sideways.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons license the diggings because the crystal pays for the border offices; the diggers dig because the Owing says so.
why.pressures: Every season takes more of an Ayleid structure that the Synod would pay handsomely to study intact.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be closed by any authority that valued the ruin above the revenue, which is no authority the north has.

hardConstraints: exposed Ayleid galleries in a ravine wall
places.hook: The diggings are the Ayleid galleries, entered sideways — crystal for the taking past the licensed face.

places.name: Sings-For-The-Pipes
places.whySiteWon: a channel bank in seasonal floodplain (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'oxbow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-guar-ground (+1.40).

why.founding: The Panther basin's frogs have the chirp the vossa-satl copies, and somebody worked out three generations ago that the tone breeds true, so this is a farm that culls by ear.
why.siteAdvantages: Six spring-fed ponds at slightly different temperatures, which is what lets the farm hold six different tones on one site.
why.occupantsMotive: The pipe-makers in Thorn pay by tone, and a matched set of six is worth more than the ponds that made it.
why.pressures: The tone drifts if the pond temperature drifts, so the farm's whole craft is water management dressed up as animal husbandry; a hot year ruins a decade of selection.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its stock in one season to a spring failure, and the selection could not be redone in under thirty years.

hardConstraints: multiple spring-fed ponds at differing temperatures
places.hook: Six ponds of frogs bred by ear, and a matched set of six tones is worth more than the farm.

places.name: Sits-Above-The-Flood
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 258 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.hissmir (+0.78).

why.founding: Six houses on the only rise for a kilometre of the Stormhold flood plain — the hamlet has no other reason to exist and has never pretended otherwise.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel rise two metres above the plain, dry in every flood anyone has recorded, on the line villages walk between the terraces and the north road.
why.occupantsMotive: They farm the plain and sleep on the rise; in flood season they farm nothing and take in everyone whose ground is under water, at a price.
why.pressures: The rise is finite and the flood is not; two of the six houses now stand on made ground the households carried up themselves, basket by basket.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would double in size and halve in dryness if the flood took the next rise downstream, which it is visibly working on.

hardConstraints: a gravel rise two metres above the plain, not a hill
places.hook: Six houses on a gravel rise that take in everyone the flood turns out, at a price.

places.name: Stands-On-The-Hammock
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 85 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.keeps-the-second-island (+0.41).

why.founding: A tree hammock in the north marsh with real ground on it — an acre of soil that is never under water — and therefore a village, because in this landscape that is the whole argument.
why.siteAdvantages: Marsh on every side too soft to walk and too shallow to row, so nothing arrives in a hurry; the ground on top is dry enough to bury in and to grow on, which no floating village can say.
why.occupantsMotive: They own the only permanent ground for two kilometres and rent standing room on it during the flood, a business the whole marsh resents and uses.
why.pressures: The hammock is not getting bigger and the flood season is getting longer; the crown terrace is filling faster than the ground below it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have to stop burying its dead in the soil — the argument currently splitting the village.

hardConstraints: a hammock with standing marsh on every side in every season
a metre of permanent soil inside the tree ring
places.hook: Real soil in a marsh: a village that can bury its dead and grow its food, and knows what that is worth.

places.name: Stillrise Village
places.whySiteWon: box canyon in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 1285 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A village that took a Daedric bargain to survive the Knahaten Flu and has been technically dead ever since, sustained by a soul-gem array.
why.siteAdvantages: West of Stormhold on ground the Flu emptied around them — they are the only thing left on it.
why.occupantsMotive: They maintain the illusions because the alternative is to stop; three and a half centuries of infighting has settled nothing.
why.pressures: The array was preserved rather than destroyed in 2E 582, so the argument that started then is still running, with the same participants — who are technically dead, held in the world by Clavicus Vile's bargain, which is why the argument cannot simply outlive them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the day someone broke the array — and half the village would thank them.

hardConstraints: a village that appears normal at distance
places.hook: A village the Flu passed over, and the humming frame of soul gems in the meeting house explains why.

places.name: Stormhold
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'stormhold' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Built on ravine-severed mounds above a waterfall, over a Barsaebic Ayleid crystal undercity the city has never stopped mining.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of navigation on the northern river: everything from Morrowind stops here, and the ravines make each mound its own defensible quarter.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons — plural, and rivals — run the state's only working border offices because the river trade pays for offices.
why.pressures: The Knahaten Flu began here, and the city has never been allowed to forget it; the Silyanorn tunnels below are worked by people with no other option.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its purpose if the Morrowind trade failed, and its shape if the waterfall ever cut back past the first mound.

places.hook: The north's border city: offices, boats to everywhere, a crystal undercity underfoot, and two vicecanons who hate each other.

places.name: Bogmother Causeway
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in lake & standing water (danger band 2), 66 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Stormhold built a stone causeway to Bogmother because the pilgrimage could not wait on the season.
why.siteAdvantages: The shortest line of shallow bog between the city's south gate and the sacred ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it as a civic duty; the maintenance gang is a hereditary office with a bad reputation.
why.pressures: It is stone, which post-Duskfall is a moral compromise — and it is the only reason the compromise is tolerated.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced with timber if it ever failed completely, which the caretakers would prefer and the city would not.

hardConstraints: shallow bog between two fixed points
places.hook: A stone causeway over the bog to Bogmother — dry feet, and nothing off the edge worth landing on.

places.name: Tear Road Stage
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 83 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The Tear road is one of the province's two canon exit roads, and a road to Morrowind needs a last stage on the Argonian side.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the road leaves the marsh for the pass — the last place with fodder, water and level ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The stage is run by a family who take payment in both coin and salt and prefer salt.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans and Argonian porters use the same yard and keep to opposite sides of it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a border town if the traffic doubled, and everyone here can name the year they think that will happen.

hardConstraints: last level ground before the pass
places.hook: Last fodder, water and level ground before the road climbs to Morrowind.

places.name: Tearmouth
places.whySiteWon: headland in firm lowland (danger band 2), 635 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Where the north river meets navigable water, cargo has to change hulls; a two-culture port grew at the transfer point, Argonian on the water and Dunmer on the bank, and has been arguing about which half is the port ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of deep-draught navigation: below it a keeled hull can float, above it only shallow craft, and no engineering has ever changed that.
why.occupantsMotive: Transfer fees, warehousing, a customs presence run out of Thorn with two clerks, and a great deal of business that the two clerks are not shown.
why.pressures: Both halves of the town want the customs house on the other side of the water; the Thorn road wants a bridge; and the whole place empties for six weeks when the river runs too hard to transfer at all.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose half its trade to a deeper channel and all of it to a bridge, and has resisted both for a century.

places.hook: Where cargo changes hulls: two half-towns, one customs house, and any berth you like if you ask the right half.

places.name: Ten-Maur-Wolk
places.whySiteWon: box canyon in upland hills (danger band 3), 416 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A temple to Boethiah and Vaermina raised by Dunmer dissidents who fled the Tribunal, and abandoned by them. The Third Empire's surveyors renamed it Tenmar Wall on their maps; the north never adopted the name, and the market that carries the shortened form grew half a morning's walk away, on the road, which is as close as anyone wanted to build.
why.siteAdvantages: Off the road and out of the way, in a hollow the tracks curve around, which is why everyone in the north knows of it and nobody goes to it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The marker posts around it are maintained, which is the loudest thing about the place.
why.pressures: The market town that borrowed its name lives off the road and pretends the ruin is somebody else's business; the second atrocity on this ground is the Dres slave road that ran past the district, not anything the dissidents built.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would draw a cult within a year if the markers ever stopped being renewed.

hardConstraints: off every route, in ground that carries no track
places.hook: A Daedric shrine the north has ringed with new white posts and will not discuss, where nothing has fallen down in two thousand years.

places.name: Ten-Thousand-Nests
places.whySiteWon: islet in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 695 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A stand of dead trees in shallow water where the north's wading birds nest in numbers that make the stand uninhabitable and the ground beneath it the richest fertiliser source in the region.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead standing timber over water: no predator route in, no need for the birds to leave, and forty years of guano under it.
why.occupantsMotive: The villages take guano for the terraces in one licensed month and stay away for eleven, an arrangement enforced by the smell as much as by anyone.
why.pressures: The saltrice growers want more than one month; the villages that eat the eggs want none at all; the stand itself is rotting and falling tree by tree.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate entirely — birds do — if the stand came down, and nobody knows where to.

places.hook: Forty years of guano under dead standing timber, worth money, and the colony above will not agree to it.

places.name: Ash Causeway
places.whySiteWon: gorge in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 206 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The Dres built a stone causeway north from their frontier holdings towards the Tear road, and the Argonians who inherited it have kept it because it is the only hard ground across four kilometres of sink.
why.siteAdvantages: The line of a buried gravel ridge that the Dres surveyed and everyone since has simply followed.
why.occupantsMotive: The holdings at either end maintain it jointly under an arrangement neither of them likes and both of them keep.
why.pressures: It is Dunmer work in a province that reads stone as a moral error, so it is used constantly and spoken of badly; three sections have been let go deliberately.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be let go entirely if the northern holdings emptied, and the north would lose its only dry winter road.

hardConstraints: a buried gravel ridge across sinking ground
places.hook: A Dres-surveyed gravel line across wet ground: the fast way over the plain, if you keep to it.

places.name: Ash Holding
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 2), 54 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Dres families displaced by the Red Year settled the Argonian side of the pass, on land that was cheap because it had been theirs by force before.
why.siteAdvantages: Upland grazing and a spring, close enough to the pass to leave quickly if they ever have to.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because Morrowind has nothing left for them; they hold themselves apart because the alternative is admitting that.
why.pressures: Every Argonian household within a day of them is descended from someone this family's ancestors owned.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would leave in a generation if the border ever hardened, and would take the herds.

places.hook: A Dunmer frontier holding with grazing, a spring, and a household that keeps its carts loaded in case.

places.name: Black Stage
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: The Bogmother causeway ends at a channel too deep to bridge in stone, so the last two hundred metres are a ferry.
why.siteAdvantages: The channel's narrowest point, where the causeway was built up to and then stopped.
why.occupantsMotive: The ferry family are the causeway gang's cousins and the arrangement is inherited and resented.
why.pressures: Pilgrims arriving at dusk find the ferry on the far side more often than chance would explain.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced by a span the day Stormhold decided to spend the money, which it never has.

hardConstraints: part of the Bogmother Causeway, at its last span
places.hook: The causeway stops and a ferry family starts, and at dusk the boat is usually on the wrong bank.

places.name: Carries-Them-North
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 145 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Argonians die in Morrowind — in Tear's yards, in the Owings, on the road — and their bones come back down the pass.
why.siteAdvantages: The first stage on the Argonian side of the pass, because the carry from Tear is the longest in the world and the first rest matters most.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers meet carriers at the border post and take custody there, which was negotiated and is honoured.
why.pressures: More bones come down the pass each year, and nobody in Thorn will say publicly why.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a scandal if the border post ever refused a carrier, which it has not yet done.

places.hook: The first rest on the Argonian side of the pass, where the bone-carriers set down what they carry and count it.

places.name: Borrowed Tomb
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 87 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A Dunmer wayside tomb on the Tear road, emptied by its own family when they left, and lived in since by a road family with nowhere else.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry, stone, roofed and beside the road — the only free shelter on a three-hour stretch.
why.occupantsMotive: They live in the antechamber and have never opened the inner door, which they mention to every guest.
why.pressures: Passing Dunmer find it obscene; passing Argonians find the scruple about the inner door unnecessary.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be vacated instantly and apologetically if any Dres heir arrived.

hardConstraints: an emptied Velothi tomb on a road
places.hook: A dry Dunmer tomb with somebody living in it who would rather you did not mention it.

places.name: The Bound Urns
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 3), 91 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The dead who are denied return to the Hist are bound into urns, and the urns have to be kept somewhere nobody will break them by accident.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry rock shelter on the rim above the swamp — dry enough to keep clay, remote enough to be forgotten deliberately.
why.occupantsMotive: An officeholder from Greylight visits twice a year to check the seals and says nothing about it afterwards.
why.pressures: There are urns here from the last decade, which means the punishment is still being handed down.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be emptied by anyone who decided the sentences had run long enough — which is not a decision anyone has the standing to make.

places.hook: A sealed urn shelter on the rim, checked twice a year by an officeholder who will not say what is in them.

places.name: Causeway Hearth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 23 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A kilometre of open stone causeway in a province of storms needs one place to stop, and the obligation supplies it.
why.siteAdvantages: At the causeway's mid-point, built out sideways on its own small platform.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by rota from Stormhold's south quarter, which regards the duty as an honour and competes for it.
why.pressures: Pilgrim numbers have risen and the rota families are quietly out of pocket.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be an embarrassment to the whole city if it were ever found cold.

places.hook: A fire and a roof at the causeway's mid-point: free, no questions, no beds.

places.name: Charge Pond
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 89 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'lake-shore' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'relaxed-score'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.greylight-village (+1.22).

why.founding: A wamasu holds a deep pond and curses all the water around it to deadly convulsions, which is canon and is also a swimming rule.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep still water fed from below, with no outflow strong enough to move anything out of it.
why.occupantsMotive: The creature is here because the pond is deep and quiet; everything else is here by accident and briefly.
why.pressures: The villages' offerings have made the pond a place people approach on purpose, which is new and unwise.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change. Fixed danger means the pond stays lethal whatever the player is.

hardConstraints: deep still water fed from below, at least three metres
dead standing timber ringing the water
places.hook: Still black water with a wamasu in it, and the charge comes up through the water before the animal does.

places.name: Charge Works
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 357 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A wamasu is worth more dead than any three other animals in the province, and someone has to process one when it is taken.
why.siteAdvantages: Downwind and downstream of the village, on a spit where the water can carry the waste away.
why.occupantsMotive: The works family holds the sap-insulation technique and will not teach it, which is why the works is a family and not a trade.
why.pressures: Charge-holding bone is the north's most valuable export after crystal, and Stormhold's enchanters want the supply tied up.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end with the family, and the technique with it, unless the daughter changes her mind.

places.hook: Wamasu hide and gland worked into charged goods, the north's only source, and they buy raw stock.

places.name: Cold Holding
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 850 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The second Dres holding, abandoned when the family failed and the survivors went into Thorn's trade quarter.
why.siteAdvantages: Higher and colder than the first, on ground that turned out not to carry enough grazing.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the tomb is still sealed and the Argonian neighbours will not touch a sealed tomb of any people.
why.pressures: The compound is being taken apart for timber by everyone except its rightful heirs.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be reclaimed instantly if a Dres heir arrived — and one exists, in Thorn.

hardConstraints: a failed upland holding with a sealed tomb
places.hook: An abandoned Dunmer holding with the winter stores still sealed and the reason for leaving written on the door.

places.name: Crown Terrace
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 68 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: On a hammock the ground is precious and the crown is dry, so Stands-On-The-Hammock puts its dead up rather than in — a platform terrace in the canopy, above the houses, above the soil, above the flood.
why.siteAdvantages: The hammock's tallest stand, with three trunks close enough to carry a terrace and a canopy dense enough to hide it from the marsh.
why.occupantsMotive: The hammock's whole population, by turns; tending the terrace is a rotating duty and refusing it is the one thing that can get a household put off the hammock.
why.pressures: The terrace is full. The village is currently arguing whether to build a second, extend this one, or start burying in the soil after all — which is the fight the village cannot settle.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would force the village's hand within five years either way, and both answers cost the village something it does not want to give.

hardConstraints: three trunks close enough to carry a terrace
places.hook: The island puts its dead up in the canopy; the terrace is full, and climbing it shows you the argument.

places.name: The Jumped Claim
places.whySiteWon: ravine in border mountains (danger band 3), 1009 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A licensed party proved a garnet seam on the rim scree and was run off it by four men who had followed them up. The claim is still legally somebody else's and nobody in Crystalgate will say so out loud.
why.siteAdvantages: On the rim scree above the root gallery, where the rock is exposed and the seams would show if they were there.
why.occupantsMotive: They work the seam by day and hold the approach by night, and they have decided that anyone who climbs the scree is here for the claim.
why.pressures: The cutting houses buy their stone anyway, which is the only reason the arrangement has lasted two seasons.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty overnight if a seam were struck, and Crystalgate would move to it.

hardConstraints: on rim scree above a worked ravine, with one approach
places.hook: Claim-jumpers on the rim scree who ran the licensed party off and will try the same on you.

places.name: The Delta Byre
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 245 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The Tear road runs on guar and the delta breeds the one strain that will work wet ground without foundering.
why.siteAdvantages: Brackish delta grazing on firm islands — poor for crops, ideal for a Glowgill herd.
why.occupantsMotive: The byre breeds and sells to both provinces' caravans, which makes it the least political business in the north.
why.pressures: The strain is theirs and unpatented; a Dres factor has twice tried to buy the breeding stock outright.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bought out within a decade unless the family keeps refusing, which the daughter may not.

hardConstraints: brackish delta grazing on firm islands
places.hook: Glowgill guar on brackish islands: mounts, milk, and a herder who trades one for the right favour.

places.name: Diggings Ladder
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 159 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-thousand-birds (+2.70).

why.founding: The Silyanorn diggings run down into the ravine and the crystal comes out on ropes, so a ladder tower was built up the ravine wall to get the hands down and the stone up without either using the road.
why.siteAdvantages: A ravine wall with enough ledge to seat platforms every four metres and a working face directly below.
why.occupantsMotive: Hoist crews, paid by weight; it is the fastest way in and out of the diggings and everyone uses it despite the state of it.
why.pressures: It is a works structure treated as a works structure: repaired only when it fails, and the failures are recorded in the diggings' own ledger as lost time.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced with a proper stair the year Stormhold's vicecanons priced the lost time honestly.

hardConstraints: a ravine wall above a working face
places.hook: Platforms every four metres down a ravine wall — the fast way to the working face, if the ladders hold.

places.name: Divers' Landing
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 52 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A lake with a drowned xanmeer in it produces divers, and divers produce a landing where what they raise is sorted and sold.
why.siteAdvantages: The nearest firm bank to the drowned terrace, with deep water two boat-lengths out.
why.occupantsMotive: The divers work the terrace and argue about which chambers are permissible, in public, constantly.
why.pressures: Greylight's minders have declared parts of it off limits, and the landing has no way to enforce or ignore that cleanly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be shut by the villages together if a Hist chamber were ever stripped.

places.hook: The divers who work the drowned terrace sell what they bring up and hire anyone who can hold their breath.

places.name: The Drawdown Flats
places.whySiteWon: spring head in upland hills (danger band 3), 1139 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, submerged, hinterland.

why.founding: The northern lake drops three metres in the dry season and exposes ground that spends most of the year underwater.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow shelf on the lake's north side, the largest area exposed by the annual drawdown.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on it, by definition; everybody uses it for the eight weeks it exists.
why.pressures: What the water uncovers changes each year, and includes things people would rather stayed covered.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be permanent ground if the lake ever fell for good, and the villages consider that a nightmare, not a windfall.

hardConstraints: a shallow shelf on the lake's north side
part of the same lake basin as The Drowned Terrace
places.hook: For a few weeks a year the lake pulls back and a drain hole opens in the mud; after that it is under three metres.

places.name: Dres Rows
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 436 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A saltrice plantation's labour quarters, built by House Dres for people it owned, and occupied since the secession by the descendants of the people who were housed in them — who now own the fields and still live in the rows.
why.siteAdvantages: Between the fields and the water, exactly where a plantation puts its labour: convenient, damp, and impossible to leave quickly.
why.occupantsMotive: They stay because moving would mean building, and because the rows work; the discomfort of the arrangement is discussed constantly and acted on never.
why.pressures: The rows are Dunmer-built and every household has altered theirs, so the terrace is a two-hundred-year argument about how much of the original to keep.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down the year the field titles were finally settled, and the settlement is the thing nobody can get.

places.hook: Plantation quarters between the fields and the water, where the labour is housed and the ledger is kept badly.

places.name: Drover Camp
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 183 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-pass-station (+0.26).

why.founding: Naga range further north in the wet season than anyone admits, and a caravan road through wet ground is a hunting lane.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the Tear road's delta section runs between two channels — a place a road cannot leave.
why.occupantsMotive: They camp for the season and take what passes; this is not banditry as the road understands it.
why.pressures: Thorn's levy sweeps the section twice a year and finds an empty camp both times.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not be here at all in a dry year, and the road forgets between them.

hardConstraints: on the road's delta section, between two channels
screened from the road by reed
places.hook: Naga camped where the road cannot leave the channels; they take what passes and are gone by the dry season.

places.name: The Drowned Terrace
places.whySiteWon: gorge in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 1146 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, remote, submerged.

why.founding: A xanmeer whose ground subsided into the lake, taking a complete Merethic building down with it intact.
why.siteAdvantages: A lake basin over soft ground — the province's hydrology drowns what it does not flood.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives in it. The nearest village dives it for stone fittings and considers this different from looting a standing xanmeer.
why.pressures: The distinction is not universally accepted, and Greylight has said so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious quarrel the day someone brought up something that was clearly a Hist chamber's fitting.

places.hook: One stone step in open water, and a whole building in green light beneath it.

places.name: Empty Socket
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 66 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A small Barsaebic structure built around a single stone socket, with the stone gone — taken, by the record cut beside it, in the same generation the building went up.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock knoll clear of the flood, close enough to the Silyanorn system to be part of it and far enough to be forgotten by everyone working the diggings.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives here. The chamber has been searched exhaustively and there is nothing in it but the socket and the record.
why.pressures: The record beside the socket is legible and says who took the stone, and that name appears nowhere else in any source anyone has consulted.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the most important room in the north if the stone were ever put back, which is exactly the kind of sentence the Whispers scholars enjoy.

hardConstraints: a rock knoll above the flood
places.hook: An Ayleid keystone chamber with the keystone gone, and the diggings below have never noticed it is here.

places.name: Field-Edge Hearth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 28 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The obligation applies in field country too, and in field country the comers are mostly people who have just lost an Owing case.
why.siteAdvantages: At the edge of the terraces where the road from Thorn's court comes out into the fields.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by Saltmarch's rota; the Dunmer households take their turn, which took a generation to arrange.
why.pressures: The field-owners regard it as a shelter for runaways and have said so; the villages have declined to discuss it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a flashpoint the first time an overseer took someone out of it.

hardConstraints: at the field country's edge on the court road
places.hook: A hearth where Thorn's road comes out into the fields, open to anyone who works.

places.name: Field Gate
