places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 839 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Thorn's field-owners keep a levy, and a levy has to be quartered where the fields end and the road to Morrowind begins.
why.siteAdvantages: The gap between the terrace country and the pass road — the only line an approach from the north must cross.
why.occupantsMotive: The levy exists to protect titles, not people, and its officers are the field-owners' sons.
why.pressures: Half the levy are Dunmer, which is either sensible recruiting or a serious mistake depending on who is asked.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be disbanded within a year if Thorn's title disputes were ever settled, and nobody expects that.

hardConstraints: the gap between the fields and the pass road
places.hook: The gate everything from the north must pass: levy, inspection, and a market that grew on the waiting.

places.name: First-Counted
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: The first ground the Flu filled, in the first season, before anyone understood what was happening.
why.siteAdvantages: On the terrace below Stormhold's south gate, because at the time nobody could carry the dead further.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it because it cannot not; the maintenance is done at night and nobody says why.
why.pressures: Kothringi dead are buried here alongside Argonian dead — a mixing that neither people's rite permits and both accepted.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's central memorial if the city could bear to make it one.

hardConstraints: within sight of the city gate
places.hook: The first Flu dead, counted and stacked below Stormhold's south gate, with the count still legible.

places.name: Fish Boon Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 104 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Hissmir's Fish Boon Feast needs somewhere to happen that is not the pilgrimage xanmeer, and this river flat below the village has been that place for as long as the feast has existed.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide gravel flat where the river slows: shallow enough to net from the bank, wide enough for the whole village and its pilgrims, and scoured clean by every flood.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here and nothing is built here, because the flood takes it annually and that is understood to be part of the arrangement.
why.pressures: The pilgrim numbers have grown past what the flat can feed, and the Root Stewards will not turn anyone away, so the feast now runs three days instead of one.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move upstream if the river shifted its channel, which it does about once a century and is due.

hardConstraints: a gravel flat on slow water below Hissmir
places.hook: A netting festival on the gravel flat: a whole district in one place, with pilgrims, and drunk by dusk.

places.name: The Flu Cordon
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 1118 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, sightline, hinterland.

why.founding: The Flu began at Stormhold, and the north cordoned itself against its own city — the only such line drawn from the inside out.
why.siteAdvantages: A ring of markers at a day's walk from the city, following the ground where the channels make a natural boundary.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The vicecanons still pay a marker-walker, and she keeps the cellar swept because she sleeps in it herself four nights a month.
why.pressures: Stormhold has never formally acknowledged that the line was drawn against Stormhold.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a diplomatic incident if anyone re-marked it, which is why nobody has.

hardConstraints: a ring at a day's walk from the city
places.hook: A cordon cellar nobody will go near: dry, roofed, and the safest floor within an hour of the rootworm ground.

places.name: The Freed Rows
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 89 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: When the pens emptied, the people in them had nowhere to be; a shelter grew where they stopped walking.
why.siteAdvantages: A day south of the pen yard — precisely as far as a column of exhausted people got on the first day.
why.occupantsMotive: It persists because people still arrive: Owing runaways now, rather than freed slaves, and the distinction is thinner every year.
why.pressures: The Owing brokers regard it as a receiving house for stolen labour and say so in Thorn's court.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be closed by a court order the day the Owing were ruled property — which is exactly the case being argued.

hardConstraints: one day's walk from the pen yard
places.hook: The shelter freed people reached on the first day, where the Chainbreakers know who is still holding whom.

places.name: Gravel Six
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 265 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: A second rise, half a day north, settled two generations later by the overflow from the first — the two hamlets are related, competitive, and consider each other's flood arrangements inadequate.
why.siteAdvantages: A longer, lower rise than its neighbour's, which means more ground and less margin — a trade the founders made knowingly.
why.occupantsMotive: Saltrice on the plain and a ferry-rope across the channel that only pays in the wet months, which is when they need it.
why.pressures: In a bad year the rise goes under by a hand's depth and the hamlet moves bodily to its rival's rise for three weeks, which neither party enjoys.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would abandon the rise permanently after two consecutive bad years, and everyone has been counting since the last one.

hardConstraints: a longer, lower gravel rise on the same plain, not a hill
places.hook: Six households on a lower rise, a rope ferry that only works in the wet, and a feud with the hamlet upstream.

places.name: Guar Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 133 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'island' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.sings-for-the-pipes (+1.40).

why.founding: A second, smaller drying ground on the Thorn side, where the Dunmer holdings drive their guar in the dry months because the saltrice ground has nothing on it then.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow basin that holds a skin of water two months longer than the plain around it, with hard edges to hold a herd against.
why.occupantsMotive: Two Dunmer holdings and one Argonian village use it in rotation, which was a Dres arrangement and is now nobody's, and works anyway.
why.pressures: The guar and the wild herds want the same water in the same weeks, and the holdings deal with that by killing whatever else arrives.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would break the rotation the first year a holding brought more guar than the basin can water, which one of them is visibly building towards.

hardConstraints: a basin holding water into the dry season
hard edges to hold a herd
places.hook: A basin that holds water two months longer than the plain, and three herds' worth of marks on the same posts.

places.name: High Wrappings
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 309 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The second hammock's crown terrace, older and smaller than its neighbour's, and the reason its people will not accept charity from the first: their dead are already up, and have been longer.
why.siteAdvantages: A single enormous trunk with a natural triple fork at fourteen metres, which needed almost no building to make a terrace of.
why.occupantsMotive: The village tends it in silence; the terrace predates the village's grievance and is the argument they actually win.
why.pressures: The trunk is dying from the top and the terrace is in the dying part; nobody in the village will say this out loud.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have to come down before the tree does, and the village has not begun to plan for it.

hardConstraints: a natural high fork over the village
places.hook: The second island's dead are wrapped fourteen metres up a triple fork, and the wrappings are older than the first island's.

places.name: Last Landing
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 2), 176 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The north-eastern river is navigable to exactly one point, and everything that goes further inland is carried.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock sill across the channel: deep water below it, boulders above, and a bank on both sides.
why.occupantsMotive: The landing exists to change cargo from hull to back, and every trade here is a version of that.
why.pressures: The porters and the boat crews price against each other twice a day, in public, loudly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move upstream permanently the year anyone blasted the sill, which two generations have proposed.

places.hook: The head of navigation: boats below the sill, porters above it, and everyone changes here.

places.name: The Last Stone Course
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 569 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on hinterland, danger, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-shut-village (+0.80).

why.founding: A xanmeer whose building stopped mid-course when the Duskfall came, and which the province has kept unfinished on purpose ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise on the northern edge of the swamp, chosen when the builders still thought there would be time.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. Nearby villages bring their young here to be told why nobody builds in stone any more.
why.pressures: Mazzatun is four days east and building in stone right now, which makes this site's lesson urgent again.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be completed by the Xit-Xaht in a heartbeat if they were ever offered it.

places.hook: A xanmeer stopped mid-course by the Duskfall and kept unfinished on purpose, the lifted block still where it was dropped.

places.name: Lightning Yard
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 347 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A second wamasu works on the northern channel, taking what the Charge Works cannot handle and specialising in the organ lanterns rather than the hide — a split that happened because two brothers stopped speaking.
why.siteAdvantages: A channel bank with running water for the flushing and a rock face to work against, far enough from the first works that the smell of the two does not combine.
why.occupantsMotive: Lanterns: the luminescent organs keep for a season if they are handled right, and this yard handles them better than anyone, which is the brother's entire vindication.
why.pressures: Both yards depend on the same hunters, who play them against each other every season, and the price of a live wamasu has doubled in five years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would merge with the Charge Works within a year of either brother dying, and both families know it and nobody says it.

hardConstraints: a rock face to work against
places.hook: The second wamasu works: charged goods, a rock face to work against, and apprentices who pay to be shown.

places.name: The Monsoon Boom
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 584 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The low road out of Thorn goes under in the monsoon and Thorn closes it, because the alternative is losing caravans.
why.siteAdvantages: The lowest crossing of the terrace country, where the water backs up first.
why.occupantsMotive: The barrier is worked by the paddy gate-holders, who are already there for the gates.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans have twice ignored it and once been right, which is the whole problem.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be unnecessary if the road were embanked, and Thorn's owners will not pay for a road they do not own.

hardConstraints: on the road, at its lowest crossing of the terrace country
places.hook: A boom and a depth gauge across the road's lowest crossing; when it is down, the delta section has already gone.

places.name: Moon Court
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 205 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A roofless alchemical court where the apparatus is moved between fixed stations by moon phase — Stormhold's alchemists keep it outside the city because the work needs a clear sky and the city has lamps.
why.siteAdvantages: A dark upland flat with no light within four kilometres and a wall of rock to the north that kills the wind without blocking the sky.
why.occupantsMotive: Two resident alchemists and a rotation of Stormhold practitioners who book nights; the court's whole value is the darkness, which is a thing that can be spoiled and cannot be repaired.
why.pressures: Crystalgate's cutting sheds have begun burning lamps late and the court's northern sky is measurably worse than it was a decade ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be worthless the day anyone put a lit building on the ridge, and the alchemists have started buying land to prevent it.

hardConstraints: no artificial light within four kilometres
clear sky and a wind break
places.hook: A calcinator court under a sky with no light in it for four kilometres, and work here that cannot be done anywhere else.

places.name: Ninth Chapel
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: An Imperial mission built a stone chapel on the north road and was dead of swamp fever inside a year; it was the ninth such attempt on this road and the numbering, which was the mission's own, is the only reason anyone remembers the other eight.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands on the only stone footing the mission could find, which is the corner of something much older that they did not investigate.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing. The north road passes it, and travellers shelter in it without any sense that they are in a chapel.
why.pressures: The roof is gone and the walls are sound; the Nisswo rest-house down the road treats it as a competitor that lost, and says so.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down for its cut stone if the province had any use for cut stone, which it does not.

hardConstraints: a stone footing on the north road
places.hook: A failed Imperial chapel standing on the corner of something much older that the mission never dug up.

places.name: North Post
places.whySiteWon: saddle in firm lowland (danger band 2), 55 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Argonia checks what comes down the Tear road, and what it is checking for is people being taken north.
why.siteAdvantages: Below the pass on the Argonian side, at the first point where a caravan can be stopped without being on a slope.
why.occupantsMotive: The keepers count heads out and heads back, a practice begun after the invasion and never repealed.
why.pressures: House Dres's successors find the count insulting; the keepers find that satisfying.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if the Owing were ever abolished, because the Owing is what the count is really about.

places.hook: The head-count post below the pass: everyone crossing is written down, and the book can be read.

places.name: North Cut
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 2), 40 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ford' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: An Imperial attempt to cut a hard road north from Stormhold to the Tear road, abandoned four kilometres in when the surveyors discovered what everyone local already knew about the sink.
why.siteAdvantages: It follows a line that looks correct on a map and is wrong on the ground, which is the whole province's Imperial history in one earthwork.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it. The villages quarry the metalling for their own yards and consider this a form of restitution.
why.pressures: The cut has become a drainage channel it was never meant to be and is now actively rerouting water into ground that used to be dry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious problem within a generation if the water it collects reached the plain villages, and one of them has started to notice.

hardConstraints: a straight engineered formation ending in sink
places.hook: An Imperial road that stops mid-formation with the next pegs still in the ground and a half-bored culvert nobody finished.

places.name: The Waiting Hole
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 87 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Thorn's field-owners need somewhere to put a debtor between the field and the court, and will not build a gaol because Argonians do not.
why.siteAdvantages: In a field-owner's stock yard on the Thorn road, roofed and out of the weather, which they mention.
why.occupantsMotive: The overseers use it for a night at a time, which is legal, and sometimes for longer, which is not tested.
why.pressures: The Freed Rows keep a tally of who goes in and who comes out, and the counts do not always match.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be filled in the day Thorn's court defined waiting — a case the Chainbreakers are building.

hardConstraints: a roofed pit inside a private yard
places.hook: A roofed holding pit in a field-owner's yard, with people in it who are on no charge sheet.

places.name: North Relay
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 63 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The two northern cities do not trust each other's messengers, so a neutral relay stands between them and both pay it.
why.siteAdvantages: Exactly midway on the northern road, on ground belonging to neither city's hinterland.
why.occupantsMotive: The relay families keep neutrality as an inheritance and refuse to read, carry sealed writs unopened, and are paid twice.
why.pressures: Both cities have tried to buy an exception; the refusals are part of the family's standing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse the moment one refusal was proven to have been sold.

places.hook: The courier relay midway on the northern road: letters, remounts, and work for anyone who can carry.

places.name: The Cold Gallery
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 936 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, hinterland, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-wild-mouth (+0.35).

why.founding: The root layer reaches its northern limit here, and where it thins over cold rim ground it leaves galleries that are colder and drier than any in the south.
why.siteAdvantages: Between the swamp's edge and the rim's stone, where roots run over rock instead of mud.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing keeps it; the prospectors' camp above uses the first chamber as a store.
why.pressures: It is the only root gallery in the province with a stone floor, which makes it navigable and makes it dangerous differently.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's cave system if anyone mapped it, and the prospectors have started to.

hardConstraints: roots over rock rather than mud
places.hook: Roots running over bare rock instead of mud, and a gallery under them that stays cold.

places.name: North Vista
places.whySiteWon: summit in upland hills (danger band 3), 246 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, sightline.

why.founding: The rim is the only place in Argonia with a long view, and one ledge above the pass looks back over the whole northern marsh.
why.siteAdvantages: A ridge nose above the Tear road, high enough to clear the haze on a cold morning.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it; couriers use it to check the weather and travellers climb it for the reason anyone climbs anything.
why.pressures: It is the one place from which the province's scale is legible, and almost nobody in the province has been there.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not change, and does not need to.

hardConstraints: a ledge above the haze line
places.hook: A ridge nose above the Tear road: on a cold morning the whole north is laid out and you can pick your next week.

places.name: Northern Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 231 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: The Nisswo walk the north too, though less often, and the villages keep a house ready for a preacher who may not come this year.
why.siteAdvantages: On the Bogmother causeway road, where the pilgrim traffic already passes.
why.occupantsMotive: It is maintained by villages who would not describe themselves as devout and would be offended to be called otherwise.
why.pressures: No Nisswo has come for three years, and the house is still swept weekly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be maintained anyway. That is the whole point of the institution.

places.hook: A Sithis rest house on the pilgrim road where the nisswo will talk to anyone who sits down.

places.name: The Opened Terrace
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 307 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A xanmeer that was opened, looted and left, and has since been occupied by people with no claim to it at all.
why.siteAdvantages: On the channel network within a day of the trunk route — accessible, which is exactly why it was broken.
why.occupantsMotive: The current occupants are river thieves who like stone walls and do not care whose they are.
why.pressures: Greylight has asked twice for it to be cleared and Stormhold has not answered.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be re-tended within a season if a tribe with a claim took it back, which is a live quest.

places.hook: A xanmeer broken open because it was easy to reach; everything portable is gone, which leaves what is not.

places.name: Outer Silyanorn
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 271 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleid settlement that Stormhold was built on top of, whose outer compound lies beyond the city's ravines.
why.siteAdvantages: The same dry shelf the city occupies, continuing north where the city stopped building.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it. The city quarries the undercity and ignores the surface work entirely, which suits the surviving structures.
why.pressures: It is the only part of Silyanorn nobody is licensed to dig, purely because nobody has thought to ask.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be quarried within a year of anyone realising the licence covers only the galleries.

places.hook: Ayleid surface work standing in daylight, ignored by a city that only quarries downward.

places.name: Pass Station
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 414 m from the nearest route; no free 'saddle' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-drover-camp (+0.26).

why.founding: The Tear road crosses the rim at one saddle, and the saddle kills people in winter, so both provinces have paid for a station on it.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle's crown, where the road is at its highest and there is no lee at all.
why.occupantsMotive: Two keepers hold it under an arrangement between Thorn's field-owners and a Dres factor, which is the only functioning cross-border institution in the north.
why.pressures: Neither side will pay for the roof, so the roof is the worst part of the building.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse as an institution if either province stopped paying — and the keepers have a bad feeling.

places.hook: The crown of the saddle, no shelter from anything, and the last chance to turn back.

places.name: The Pen Yard
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 148 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Slavery ended; the buildings did not. This is where the Dres assembled and shipped people north for four centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: On the road below the pass, at the last point where a column could be held overnight.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. It is used as a cattle pen by a neighbouring holding, which is either healing or obscene depending who you ask.
why.pressures: It is structurally excellent and there is a live argument about pulling it down.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be demolished tomorrow if the district could agree, and the district cannot.

places.hook: The Dres holding yard below the pass, abandoned with the fittings intact and the manifests still nailed up.

places.name: Permit Dig
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 54 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Cyrodilic Collections keeps an alcove at Stormhold, and an alcove implies a dig somewhere it can defend as lawful.
why.siteAdvantages: On Outer Silyanorn's edge, on the one parcel the city was willing to licence.
why.occupantsMotive: The Collections dig to return; the vicecanons licence it to keep an eye on it; the diggers dig for wages.
why.pressures: The parcel they were given is deliberately the least interesting ground on the site, and both parties know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move onto the arcade the moment the licence was widened, which the city will not do.

hardConstraints: a licensed parcel beside a ruin
places.hook: The one licensed dig on Outer Silyanorn's edge, short of hands and shorter of honest ones.

places.name: The Pilots' Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 12 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Boat crews on the trunk route need a bed that is not their own hull, and the channel villages will not take strangers overnight.
why.siteAdvantages: Built out over the water at a wide bend where six boats can lie alongside at once.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper was a pilot, retired from it, and sells the knowledge she no longer sells the labour for.
why.pressures: The channel pilots at Channel Cross regard her as competition and her rates as a betrayal.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be bought out by the pilots' families if she ever agreed to sell, and she will not.

hardConstraints: a wide bend with alongside mooring
places.hook: Six boats alongside, the pilots who know the channels, and prices that depend on how the last trip went.

places.name: Rim Hermitage
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 365 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A cell above the treeline kept by a Nisswo who holds that the marsh makes death too easy to think about and the cold makes it honest — one of the province's very few religious lives lived in genuine isolation.
why.siteAdvantages: Above the snowline on the leeward side of the ridge, with meltwater and a fuel cache carried up once a year by people who will not discuss why they do it.
why.occupantsMotive: One occupant, by choice, who receives anyone who climbs to the door and says nothing to anyone who does not.
why.pressures: The annual carry is done by a village that is not sure it believes any of it, and the Nisswo is old.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would stand empty and intact for a century, because nothing up there rots and nobody would take it.

hardConstraints: meltwater and an annual fuel carry
places.hook: A hermit above the snowline whose fuel is carried up once a year by people who will not say why.

places.name: Rim Shelter
places.whySiteWon: headland in upland hills (danger band 3), 383 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Above the treeline on the northern rim the weather changes in minutes and the pass has no cover, so the Dres built a shelter and the north has kept it, which is the only piece of Dunmer work here nobody objects to.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock notch on the leeward side of the col — the one place on the crossing that is out of the wind from every direction it comes from.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. It is stocked by whoever came up last, under a rule everyone follows and nobody enforces.
why.pressures: The fuel is carried up and the stove is old; twice in a decade a party has arrived to find both gone, and the second time three people did not come down.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would kill people every year rather than every decade if the carrying-up habit lapsed.

hardConstraints: a leeward notch on the col
places.hook: A rock notch out of the wind from every direction it comes from, which on this crossing is the whole point.

places.name: The Salt and Shell
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 38 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A caravan house at the field-country crossroads, where a Dunmer trader and an Argonian porter will both find something they can eat.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the Tear road meets the terrace lanes, with room for beasts.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper cooks two cuisines badly and is loved for the attempt.
why.pressures: The levy drinks here and the smugglers drink here and the keeper seats them by shift.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close if the Tear road ever went quiet, and the district would mourn.

hardConstraints: at a road junction in the field country
places.hook: A tradehouse where the Tear road meets the terrace lanes, with stabling and an argument most nights.

places.name: The Salt Ledge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 174 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The head-count at the border post is exactly why an uncounted route over the rim exists.
why.siteAdvantages: A ledge line running parallel to the pass a kilometre east, wide enough for a person and not for a beast.
why.occupantsMotive: The carriers move salt north and, when the price is right, people — which is what the count was meant to stop.
why.pressures: Both provinces know it is there; neither wants the diplomatic cost of closing it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would close in a week if the head-count were dropped, which is the argument the smugglers make.

hardConstraints: a benched ledge line on the ravine wall, wide enough for a person and not a beast
places.hook: An uncounted ledge route past the border post — salt one way, people the other, for a fee.

places.name: Shell Ground
places.whySiteWon: saddle in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 623 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, remote, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-shut-village (+0.41).

why.founding: Armoured shell-beasts work a stretch of gravel bar for the molluscs in it, and where they work, they moult — which makes this the region's raw material source for shell plate, and one of the more dangerous places to stand in the north.
why.siteAdvantages: A long gravel bar with a mollusc bed under it, exposed for four hours either side of the drawdown and covered the rest of the time.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. Gatherers come at the drawdown, take moult plate off the bar, and are gone before the animals come back up.
why.pressures: The window is short, the plate is valuable, and every year somebody misjudges it; the gatherers' own count of the dead is kept on a post at the landing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would stop producing entirely if the mollusc bed were over-taken, which the gatherers police far more strictly than they police the timing.

hardConstraints: a gravel bar over a mollusc bed
a drawdown window that exposes it
places.hook: Furrows a metre deep ploughed through gravel tell you the size of what made them before you see it.

places.name: The Shut Village
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 8 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.hatching-pools (+1.55).

why.founding: A village that shut itself in during the Flu, survived, and never fully opened again — the practice outlived the reason by sixteen centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: On a rise in the reedbeds with one causeway across to it, which is why shutting was possible at all.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep the practice because it worked once; visitors are received at the causeway's outer end and not past it.
why.pressures: The village is inbred, dwindling and knows it; the Hatching Pools have sent word twice and been refused.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end within a generation either way — by opening, or by simply running out.

hardConstraints: a rise reached by a single causeway across the reedbeds
places.hook: A village that shut itself in behind its one causeway and has not opened, though it will talk through the gate.

places.name: Silyanorn Crown
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 496 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, sightline, hinterland.

why.founding: One block of the Outer Silyanorn stands to its full height with a stair that fails two thirds of the way up, so the last third is a climb and the top is the only place near Stormhold you can see over the ravine system.
why.siteAdvantages: The compound's high corner, on the ravine rim, with the diggings on one side and the city on the other.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The diggings' hands go up to eat their meal in the sun and leave the crumbs, and the hoist crews use it to see whether the road is clear.
why.pressures: The failed section of stair is failing further; the hold that everyone uses has visibly moved in a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be nothing at all if the last third became unclimbable — the block has no interior worth entering.

hardConstraints: part of Outer Silyanorn, its high corner on the ravine rim
places.hook: The compound's high corner on the ravine rim — the one climb that shows you the diggings and the city at once.

places.name: The Slumped Hamlet
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 69 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A hamlet built over a limestone void near the rim, which took four generations to notice and one season to leave.
why.siteAdvantages: Good dry ground with a spring — which was the void's fault too, and nobody made the connection in time.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the households moved two hundred metres and rebuilt, which is the province's standard answer.
why.pressures: The old and new hamlets are in sight of each other, and the old one is still slowly going down.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would take the new hamlet too if the void runs the way the rim's geology suggests.

hardConstraints: a rebuilt hamlet in sight of it
places.hook: Good ground with a spring that sank into the void that fed the spring, houses and all.

places.name: Behind the Falls
places.whySiteWon: gorge in border mountains (danger band 3), 321 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, bound, route.

why.founding: Stormhold's waterfall has cut back into the rock and left a chamber behind the sheet, directly below the city.
why.siteAdvantages: The undercut is at the falls' centre, reachable along a ledge from the ravine's south side only.
why.occupantsMotive: The city knows about it. The Conclave uses it, and does not book it.
why.pressures: It is the only room within Stormhold's walls that is not in any of the city's plans.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be sealed by the vicecanons the day they worked out who was using it.

hardConstraints: an undercut behind a major fall
places.hook: A ledge behind Stormhold's falls into an undercut chamber, and the city has never put a door on it.

places.name: The Stripped Village
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 89 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Umbriel passed north across the province in 4E 48 and took what it took; this village was under its shadow and is empty of bodies.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly on the recorded track, on ground that was perfectly good and is now avoided.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it. The neighbouring villages keep a vigil rather than a taboo, which is a different thing.
why.pressures: There are no graves here because there were no bodies, which the vigil-keepers find harder than a massacre.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be resettled if the Waiting Vigil ever declared the dead accounted for, and they will not.

places.hook: A village Umbriel passed over: buildings intact, stake field bare, and nothing left alive to bury.

places.name: Sump Rows
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 179 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A hamlet the Flu emptied twice, on the old Dres road, and nobody has wanted it since. The men working it now are what is left of a Dres holding-house: they take people off the road in ones and twos and write each one down, because a Dres crew that stops keeping the book stops being paid.
why.siteAdvantages: Roofs that still keep rain off, a walled stock pen, and a district that has agreed not to walk this way.
why.occupantsMotive: They are owed wages by a house that no longer exists and are collecting them in the only currency they were ever trained to handle.
why.pressures: Thorn's levy will not cross onto the old road, and the Chainbreakers at the Freed Rows know the camp is here and are two people short of doing anything about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in a night if the book were taken, because without it the crew cannot prove a claim on anybody.

hardConstraints: an emptied hamlet on the old Dres road
a walled stock pen still standing
places.hook: A Dres crew with no house left is still taking people off the old road, and still writing each one down.

places.name: The Tear Wreck
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 271 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.nine-fords (+0.59).

why.founding: A Dunmer trader out of Tear misread the delta bar in a storm and is still on it, forty years later.
why.siteAdvantages: Hard aground on the outer bar, upright, where the tide covers her to the rail twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody salvages her: the cargo went in the first month and the hull is Dres property in a court nobody will convene.
why.pressures: The delta villages use her as a navigation mark and would object to her removal.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would break up in one bad storm season, and the villages would lose their best mark.

places.hook: A hull aground upright on the outer bar, covered to the rail twice a day, with the cargo still stowed.

places.name: Terrace Watch
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 324 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A crop worth this much needs watching, and the terraces are flat enough that one tower sees all eleven banks.
why.siteAdvantages: The single knoll in the terrace country, put there by geology and used ever since.
why.occupantsMotive: The watch is set by the villages in rotation at harvest and by the field-owners the rest of the year, and the two watches watch different things.
why.pressures: In harvest the tower watches for theft; out of harvest it watches for surveyors.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down by the villages if the field-owners ever manned it year-round.

hardConstraints: a knoll with sight of the whole terrace system
places.hook: The one knoll in the terrace country, watched from for as long as anyone remembers; you can see who is coming.

places.name: Thorn Bond
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, bound, landform.

why.founding: Saltrice going north and Dunmer goods coming south both need to sit somewhere lockable while the tolls are argued.
why.siteAdvantages: On Thorn's river quay, where cargo transfers between boat and the Tear road.
why.occupantsMotive: The bond is held by the field-owners jointly, which means it is held by nobody and audited by everybody.
why.pressures: Half the north's smuggling passes through it legitimately and leaves by a different door.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be seized by whichever faction won Thorn's title court outright.

places.hook: Thorn's bonded warehouse: everything off the road sits here first, and one hand on the night watch is not on the roll.

places.name: The Thousand Birds
places.whySiteWon: gorge in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 179 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.reedmoor-stilts (+2.12).

why.founding: The north-east islands are flat, predator-free and surrounded by fishing water, so a colony has used them for as long as anyone knows.
why.siteAdvantages: A cluster of low islets in the delta, none big enough for a house and all of them white with birds.
why.occupantsMotive: The delta villages take eggs to a strict quota set by the oldest woman in each village and enforced absolutely.
why.pressures: Egging season and the fishing season overlap, and boats compete for the same water.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be stripped in three seasons if the quota ever lapsed, and every village says so about every other village.

hardConstraints: low islets in the delta, none big enough for a house
places.hook: Delta islets white with birds — the dusk lift is worth seeing and the eggs are worth more.

places.name: Tide Fair
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-firm-ground' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: Delta villages, upland holdings and Dunmer caravans can all reach one hard sand bank at low spring tide and nowhere else together.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm sand flat exposed for six hours twice a month and under two metres of water the rest of the time.
why.occupantsMotive: Everyone trades because everyone can get here; nobody builds because in six hours the sea comes back.
why.pressures: The fair ends when the tide says so, which is the only rule and is absolutely enforced.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be impossible if the delta shifted, and the delta shifts.

hardConstraints: a firm sand flat that the tide covers and uncovers
places.hook: Six hours of market on a sand flat, then two metres of water: buy now or wait a fortnight.

places.name: Turning Stone
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 283 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A cut stone disc, three paces across, set flush in the marsh floor on a rise, which is oriented differently in every record anyone has kept of it — including two within one lifetime.
why.siteAdvantages: A patch of bedrock at the surface, which in this province is remarkable on its own and probably why it was chosen.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps it. Four villages measure it, separately, and do not compare notes because they do not like each other's answers.
why.pressures: The Nisswo say it is not their business; the College of Whispers outstation has asked to lift it and been refused by everyone at once.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be lifted within a year if any one village decided to allow it, and the other three would never forgive them.

places.hook: Bare bedrock with a turn cut into it, in a province that has no other stone like it, and the cut is not weathered.

places.name: Two-Gate Bridge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 2), 226 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The Tear road crosses the north-eastern river once, and both banks belong to different interests.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock narrows with abutments on each side — the only single-span crossing on the river.
why.occupantsMotive: Each bank has built its own gate house, and a cart pays twice or argues twice.
why.pressures: The two toll-holders have not spoken directly in nine years and communicate by written notes carried across.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be one toll if either bank bought out the other, which both have refused on principle.

hardConstraints: on the Tear road at a rock narrows with abutments on both banks
places.hook: One span, two gate houses, two tolls, and two toll-holders who have not spoken in nine years.

places.name: The Two Hundred Roofs
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 190 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A large Kothringi-Argonian village that the Flu emptied in one season and nobody has since reoccupied. Sixteen centuries on it is still empty, and the reason is not fear of the disease but the naming taboo: nobody living holds a name that could lawfully claim the roofs, and the north will not let ground be taken by anyone who cannot say whose it was.
why.siteAdvantages: Good high ground on the channel network — so good that its emptiness is the most conspicuous thing in the district.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it but the taboo, which is now maintained by habit rather than fear.
why.pressures: Boat crews use its landing and will not sleep above the landing steps, a line they observe without discussing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be resettled tomorrow by anyone who did not grow up here.

places.hook: Two hundred roofs on the best ground in the district, all of them empty, which is what you notice first.

places.name: The Veterans' Ridge
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 454 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: Argonians who went north into Morrowind in 4E 5–6 and came back settled together on the ridge that looks at the pass they came home through.
why.siteAdvantages: High ground with a clear line to the pass, chosen for the view rather than the soil.
why.occupantsMotive: Their grandchildren hold it as an institution: a place where the invasion is remembered as a victory, in a province that mostly does not discuss it.
why.pressures: The Dres holding is four hours away and both households know exactly what the other is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose its meaning entirely when the last person who was told the story by a participant dies.

hardConstraints: a ridge with a line to the pass
places.hook: Morrowind veterans holding a ridge for the view of the pass, still expecting somebody.

places.name: Shrine of Haynekhtnamet
places.whySiteWon: ravine in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 75 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Canon names a wamasu of Shadowfen that received offerings to stop the seasonal flooding; the shrine is where they were left.
why.siteAdvantages: On the bank above the pond the creature is held to inhabit, at the highest point the flood reaches.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages send offerings each wet season, in rotation, and none of them will say they believe it works.
why.pressures: The offerings are increasingly practical — tools and salt rather than symbols — which the older villagers find embarrassing.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned in a dry decade and re-established within a week of the next bad flood.

hardConstraints: above a wamasu pond at flood height
places.hook: Offerings left to stop the flooding, still being left, above a pond people say holds Haynekhtnamet.

places.name: Unpermitted Cut
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 81 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.hixinoag (+1.72).

why.founding: Somebody is digging on the far side of Outer Silyanorn without a permit, at night, for something specific.
why.siteAdvantages: Behind the ruin's spoil ridge, where the licensed dig's fence blocks the line of sight from the road.
why.occupantsMotive: The diggers are hired; the person paying them is not here and communicates by written instruction.
why.pressures: The instructions name a chamber that is not on any plan the Collections holds.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned within an hour of discovery, and the instructions burned.

hardConstraints: out of sight of a licensed dig
places.hook: An unpermitted cut behind the spoil ridge, out of the licensed dig's sight, and whoever pays for it is not local.

places.name: White Pans
places.whySiteWon: cove in ocean (danger band 0), 385 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Salt is the north's second currency — the Tear road stage prefers it to coin — and the delta makes it for free given sun and time.
why.siteAdvantages: A flat tidal margin with high evaporation and a rock bar that keeps the sea out except when wanted.
why.occupantsMotive: Six families work the pans in a rotation set by tide rather than by agreement, which prevents most quarrels.
why.pressures: The salt smugglers on the rim ledge buy here, and the pans do not ask.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would flood permanently if the rock bar were breached, and the north's barter economy would notice.

hardConstraints: a flat tidal margin behind a bar
places.hook: Salt pans worked by a family that controls the rock bar, and salt is the north's second currency.

places.name: Wild Mouth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 373 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, route, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.the-north-root-gallery (+0.35).

why.founding: An untamed rootworm's tunnel mouth two kilometres off the Waykeepers' northern line — the same animal the transit network rides, with none of the harness, the handlers or the assurances.
why.siteAdvantages: Soft root-bound ground the animal can work, close enough to the tamed line that the Waykeepers worry about it and far enough that they do nothing.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies it but the animal, which is territorial, large, and demonstrably uninterested in the difference between a handler and anyone else.
why.pressures: The Waykeepers' line runs close enough that a wild worm cutting across it is a real prospect, and has happened twice in a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have to be dealt with, expensively and by somebody, the first time it took a loaded transit worm's tunnel.

hardConstraints: near but not on the Waykeepers' line
places.hook: A wild rootworm burrow near enough the tamed line that the Waykeepers worry and far enough that they do nothing.

places.name: Xanmeer Hold
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 236 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A tribe took a xanmeer's walls and working ancient defences and has lived in them ever since — the strongest fortification in the north.
why.siteAdvantages: A terraced stone mass on firm ground in the channels, with the ancient mechanisms still functional on the lower terraces.
why.occupantsMotive: They live here because the north has been raided by Sul-Xan, Naga and Umbriel within four centuries and the walls have held each time.
why.pressures: Living in stone is a compromise their neighbours notice; their answer is that they did not build it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's refuge of last resort in any real emergency, and the tribe has said as much.

hardConstraints: a standing xanmeer with working defences
places.hook: A xanmeer held as a fort, with the old mechanisms on the lower terraces still working for whoever holds it.

places.name: Thorn
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'thorn' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: The one city with real fields around it: saltrice on temperate grassland, grown first for House Dres and now for whoever holds the title.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm grassland above a delta, with the Tear road out to Morrowind and river access down to the coast — the only place in Argonia where all three meet.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanon governs; the field-owners actually decide; the Dunmer minority holds the trade and remembers who used to hold the people.
why.pressures: Every field title is disputed, the guards look away from the smuggling because the smuggling pays them, and the border tolls fund both sides of the argument.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would tear itself apart if Morrowind ever pressed a claim, and knows it.

places.hook: The field-owners' city: road to Morrowind, river to the coast, and work for anyone who does not ask about the fields.

places.name: Thorn Terraces
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 40 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region.

why.founding: Saltrice is the north's cash crop and the only reason a foreign house ever wanted this ground; the terraces are what four centuries of that wanting built.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow tilt of grassland above the delta, where salt water can be admitted in controlled amounts — saltrice needs both.
why.occupantsMotive: The terraces are worked by the villages and owned, on paper, by whoever last won in Thorn's title court.
why.pressures: The salt gates are the whole system, and three of the eleven are held by a single family who charge for them.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fail as a crop within two seasons if the salt gates were ever lost to a delta shift.

hardConstraints: a tilt of ground above brackish water
places.hook: Saltrice terraces where salt water is let in by hand, and the gate-holders decide the district's year.

places.name: Three-Ways-Over-Water
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 25 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: A smaller junction on the Thorn side where three walkways meet at a single great trunk, using the tree as the platform rather than building one.
why.siteAdvantages: One enormous trunk standing in water at exactly the right place, saving three villages the cost of piles.
why.occupantsMotive: A rope-and-lamp keeper who lives in the trunk's first fork and is paid in food by all three lines.
why.pressures: The tree is alive and growing, and the walkway fixings are being slowly swallowed; every few years an arm has to be re-hung higher.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have to be rebuilt from scratch as a piled platform the day the tree dies, and nobody has costed that.

hardConstraints: one large living trunk in water at a three-way meeting
places.hook: One trunk in the water carries three villages' walkways; cross here or pole a long way round.

places.name: Ties-Four-Ways
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 118 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: Four elevated walkways from four villages meet over open water here, and because nobody would build the junction on anyone's ground, it was built on nobody's — a platform on piles in the middle of a lake.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep enough that no bank claims it; shallow enough to drive piles; equidistant from all four villages to within a few hundred paces.
why.occupantsMotive: A toll-free stall keeper who is tolerated because she is from none of the four, and sells to all of them.
why.pressures: Every plank is maintained by the village whose arm it belongs to, so the junction's condition is a public scoreboard of four villages' diligence.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would collapse into four dead ends the year two of the villages stopped repairing, and one of them has already slipped.

hardConstraints: open water at the meeting of four walkway lines
places.hook: A pile-driven junction of four walkways, equidistant from four villages, and the tolls are argued in the middle.

places.name: Thorn Rat Gallery
places.whySiteWon: ravine in firm lowland (danger band 3), 146 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: An Imperial warden once worked penal labour into these galleries for crystal, promising limited freedom; the gallery outlived the warden, the promise and the Empire.
why.siteAdvantages: The deepest reachable level of the undercity, below the licensed diggings, where the seams the diggers will not risk still run.
why.occupantsMotive: The people down here are working an Owing that has been transferred so many times nobody can name the original creditor.
why.pressures: The gallery floods on a schedule nobody controls, and the licensed diggers above have stopped pretending they don't know.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in a day if the Owing ledgers above it were voided — which is the whole hook.

places.hook: The undercity's deepest reachable level, below the licensed diggings, worked by people who are not counted.

places.name: Waits-For-The-Promise
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 214 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: The An-Xileel promised a clean province and a return of ground; these are the families from three villages the Xit-Xaht took, camped on the boundary of land that was theirs, waiting for the promise to be kept.
why.siteAdvantages: The boundary itself: they are camped exactly on the old line, which is the whole statement, and the ground behind them is worked by somebody else.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody here will move, because moving is the argument lost. Every family present has a claim, a witness and a name, and no court.
why.pressures: It is the fifth year; the camp has built a mud oven and a well, which everybody understands is a defeat.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the day the An-Xileel gave a ruling in either direction, and the camp is more afraid of the ruling than of the wait.

hardConstraints: the disputed ground visible from it
places.hook: A camp sitting exactly on the old boundary line while somebody else works the ground behind them.

places.name: Waits-For-The-Trial
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 292 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Hissmir's Trials cannot take everyone at once, so the overflow camps on the last dry ground before the village and waits — sometimes for a week, occasionally for a season.
why.siteAdvantages: The last firm ground on the pilgrim path, with water, wood and a view of the village that is close enough to be maddening.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilgrims, most of them Hist-less, all of them unwilling to go home; the camp organises itself into an order of arrival that the Root Stewards do not recognise and everybody obeys.
why.pressures: The waiting order is the camp's only law and it is enforced by people with nothing else left, which occasionally goes badly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty overnight if the Stewards ever refused a comer, which canon says they cannot, which is precisely why the camp keeps growing.

hardConstraints: the last dry ground on the pilgrim path
places.hook: Pilgrims camped in sight of the village that has not yet called them in.

places.name: Wolk Market
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 61 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A market grew where the Tear road out of Morrowind meets the marsh tracks and the poled water from the north villages — the district's only hinge. It takes its name from the ruin off the road to the east, shortened, because nobody wanted to name a town after Boethiah and nobody could avoid the landmark either.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground at the hinge, above the flooding that closes the road either side of it for two months a year, with spring water enough for a market but not enough to tempt anyone to build a port here.
why.occupantsMotive: It exists to take a cut of everything moving between the interior, the border city and the smugglers' port, and to be the place where three sets of weights are argued into one.
why.pressures: The vicecanons want its market fees and the river brokers want its warehousing, and the market has spent forty years making sure neither gets a foothold.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be fought over the week any of the three roads mattered militarily, and would have to build the fourth wall it has never had.

hardConstraints: on the road, at a crossing where the marsh tracks join the Tear road
firm ground above the flood line
places.hook: The district's hinge: a three-wedge market where road, track and water meet, with the shunned ruin in plain sight beside it.

places.name: Zuuk
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 939 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A Kothringi settlement that died in 2E 561, one year into the Flu, with its founder's name still on it.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank on the Shadowfen channels — good ground, which is why nobody has taken it and everyone can see it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the neighbouring villages route boats past it without stopping, and have for three hundred years.
why.pressures: It is the best unclaimed landing in the district, and the taboo is the only thing keeping it unclaimed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be resettled within a decade if the north ever grew enough to need the ground.

places.hook: Kothringi work on good ground that nobody will take, in plain sight of everyone who passes.

places.name: The Held Breath
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 292 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged.

why.founding: A maintained air pocket on a flooded root route, kept so the crossing is survivable.
why.siteAdvantages: The midpoint of the longest flooded branch in the region.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; it is maintained by whoever passes. Nobody lives here; it is maintained by whoever passes, on an interior custom that a shelter you use unrepaired is a shelter you have stolen.
why.pressures: The seal leaks and the pocket is smaller each decade. The seal leaks and the pocket is smaller each decade, and the Waykeepers who could reseal it will not work outside a paid line.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing it makes the flooded route impassable. Losing it makes the flooded route impassable and pushes every crossing onto the long root gallery, which is a day and a band of danger worse.

places.hook: Thirty metres down a flooded root gallery there is a room of dry air, and everyone who has rested in it cut their mark in the wall.

places.name: Alten Markmont
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 449 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: An outsider-facing trading station built where the southern water route met the Helstrom approach; the alten- prefix marks it as never Argonian. The kit is Imperial, not Argonian, against the region's own avoid-list: the site is an outsider work and reads wrong in any interior register — that contrast is the point.
why.siteAdvantages: A landing on deep-enough water at the last point outsiders were tolerated.
why.occupantsMotive: A skeleton staff of two factors and whoever is sheltering in the warehouses. The two factors are paid a retainer by a company that no longer trades here, on the theory that a lapsed post is cheaper to hold than to re-license.
why.pressures: The interior tolerates it and does not need it; the trade it was built for stopped. The interior tolerates it and does not need it; the trade it was built for stopped, and the warehouses now shelter people the factors are not allowed to register.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single busy season would refill it — that is the point of keeping it standing. A single busy season would refill it — that is the point of keeping it standing, and the Helstrom assembly has quietly decided it never will be.

places.hook: An Imperial warehouse quarter the marsh has taken back to the knee, with the stock still on the racks nobody dared come back for.

places.name: Thousand-Chimes
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 378 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A craft village that makes the bone and tin chimes through which half the province listens to its Hist.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside a hero Hist whose wind is reliable — the chimes are tuned against the tree that will hang them.
why.occupantsMotive: Chime-makers whose tuning is a religious qualification, not a trade skill. Tuning is examined and licensed by the tree-minders, so a maker who loses the qualification loses the craft and the village at once.
why.pressures: Cheap cast chimes from the cities are undercutting them and, they say, mistranslating the trees. Cheap cast chimes from the cities are undercutting them and, they say, mistranslating the trees — an accusation the tree-minders have declined to rule on for six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority. A ruling that cast chimes are valid would end the village's authority, and the coastal foundries that cast them would take the whole province's trade within a decade.

places.hook: Two hundred hung frames in a field, and the makers will tune a chime to your own tree if you can tell them which one it is.

places.name: The Under-Ring
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 524 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: Barsaebic Ayleid works that predate everything around them and go down rather than up.
why.siteAdvantages: Whatever the Ayleids wanted here is underground now, in rings that fill from beneath every wet season and drain again.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing that talks — but the lower rings are dry, which in this region is enough to explain everything else that lives there.
why.pressures: Antiquarians want in and the interior tribes have no stake either way, so the only obstacle is that nobody with a licence has survived the descent.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dig licence from anywhere would open it, and the Helstrom assembly would then have to decide, for the first time, whether Ayleid stone falls under the Duskfall taboo.

places.hook: Ayleid stone with Argonian root growing through the light-settings, going down instead of up, into water.

places.name: Long-Stride
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 354 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A village that breeds the only animals that can carry a load across the interior's soft ground.
why.siteAdvantages: Wide firm grazing on a flood-high rise with a soft-ground schooling paddock beside it.
why.occupantsMotive: Breeders who supply every interior porter route and price accordingly. Breeders who supply every interior porter route and price accordingly, and who will sell a gelded steed to anyone and a breeding pair to nobody.
why.pressures: Their stock is worth stealing and the roads they supply are raided. Their stock is worth stealing and the roads they supply are raided, so a third of their yearly yield now goes to escorts rather than to buyers.
why.wouldChangeIf: A road built into the interior would end their monopoly overnight. A road built into the interior would end their monopoly overnight — which is one reason the village has never supported a road survey.

places.hook: The only place in the interior that will sell you an animal able to carry a load across soft ground, and teach you to place its feet.

places.name: The Staying Stone
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A shrine where offerings are made to hold back the flood, maintained by four villages jointly.
why.siteAdvantages: The pinch point where the flood enters this basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; four villages take turns. Nobody lives here; four villages take turns, and the turn order is older than any of their current naheesh.
why.pressures: The floods have not obeyed for three years and the villages are blaming each other. The floods have not obeyed for three years and the villages are blaming each other, chiefly the one whose turn fell in the worst year.
why.wouldChangeIf: One more bad year and the shrine will be abandoned or rebuilt bigger. One more bad year and the shrine will be abandoned or rebuilt bigger, and either decision breaks the four-village compact that is the district's only joint institution.

places.hook: Four villages share the ledges here, and which of them has stopped keeping its turn is written in what is rotting on them.

places.name: Keeps-the-Egg
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 128 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: Their Hist was killed in the Imperial century; the tribe recovered the Mnemic Egg and organised itself around keeping it.
why.siteAdvantages: They did not move — the dead trunk is still the centre of the village. They did not move — the dead trunk is still the centre of the village, and the Egg is kept inside it, which is both reliquary and argument.
why.occupantsMotive: Custodians of a memory nobody can currently read.
why.pressures: Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg; one has offered to buy it. Three other tribes claim a share of the Egg; one has offered to buy it, and the offer was made publicly so that refusing it would look like hoarding.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reading the Egg — which the main quest's archivists could — would resolve or destroy them. Reading the Egg — which the main quest's archivists could — would resolve or destroy them, and every claimant tribe knows which outcome it is betting on.

places.hook: A village built around a dead trunk it refuses to leave, keeping a Mnemic Egg that other tribes would pay or kill for.

places.name: The Lit Fen
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 3), 5 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A fen where the water itself lights at night from Hist-flower fall.
why.siteAdvantages: Still water directly downstream of a hero Hist's grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the villages come to look, once a year. Nobody; the villages come to look, once a year, on a night fixed by the Tsoko stones rather than by the fen.
why.pressures: It only lights while the tree above flowers, which is a diagnostic nobody wants to need. It only lights while the tree above flowers, which is a diagnostic nobody wants to need — and this year the light came late and stopped early.
why.wouldChangeIf: The tree failing would put the fen out. The tree failing would put the fen out, and the fen going out is how the district would learn of it, weeks before the grove admitted anything.

places.hook: After dark the water burns red under a black canopy, and how bright it burns is the health of the tree upstream.

places.name: The Raw Hold
places.whySiteWon: island in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 323 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A Blackguard crew hiding in the interior because nowhere else will have them.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep, off every route, with one boat exit.
why.occupantsMotive: Criminals with no ledger and no discipline. Criminals with no ledger and no discipline, most of them three generations out of Blackrose and unable to work anywhere their descent is known.
why.pressures: They cannot resupply and are starting to raid villages they need. They cannot resupply and are starting to raid villages they need, which is the pattern that has finished every raw hold before this one.
why.wouldChangeIf: A village retaliation would finish them within a year. A village retaliation would finish them within a year, and the interior tribes have already agreed among themselves which village would lead it.

places.hook: A Blackguard crew living in the ribs of a barge they could not drag back to the water, with one boat and no friends.

places.name: Many-Ways
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 89 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: A village that grew as a junction of walkways rather than around a centre.
why.siteAdvantages: Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them. Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them — the junction is the village's whole capital.
why.occupantsMotive: Walkway-keepers who charge for maintenance and argue about who owes what.
why.pressures: The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns. The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns, and the keepers have begun charging tolls that the tribes using the arms consider extortion.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing one arm of the junction would strand a whole tribe's route. Losing one arm of the junction would strand a whole tribe's route, and the tribe in question has started surveying its own alternative rather than keep paying.

places.hook: Four walkway routes have to meet somewhere, and the shrine hung under the deck where they cross is the nearest thing here to a town square.

places.name: The Pulled Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 461 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.legendary-deep-medusa-wood (+1.23).

why.founding: A grave-stake field where stakes were pulled by looters, raising what the stakes were holding.
why.siteAdvantages: An old village's burial ground, now cut off from any living village.
why.occupantsMotive: Bog blights, and nothing else. Bog blights, and nothing else — which is why the field has become a training ground the grave-singers send apprentices to, quietly.
why.pressures: The stakes are still being pulled because the grave goods are real. The stakes are still being pulled because the grave goods are real, and the looters are not outsiders but the heirs of the village that abandoned it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking the field would settle it — a deed, not a battle. Restaking the field would settle it — a deed, not a battle — and would settle who the grave goods belong to, which is why nobody local has done it.

places.hook: Looters pulled the grave stakes and what the stakes were holding got up; the stakes are still readable, so you know exactly who is walking at you.

places.name: The Carriers' Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 205 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A staging post on the route by which the bones of Argonians who died away from the Hist are brought back to the dirt.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the river route meets the interior walking route. Where the river route meets the interior walking route, at the last point a bundle can be re-wrapped and re-labelled before the walk.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers, who are a recognised profession and a slightly feared one. Carriers, who are a recognised profession and a slightly feared one, paid by the family and never by the village, so their loyalty is always to the dead.
why.pressures: The 4E produced more distant dead than the route can carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: A backlog is already visible in the racks. A backlog is already visible in the racks, and a second season's backlog would force the carriers to choose which families' dead go first — a power no one wants them to have.

places.hook: A freight office for the dead: racks of wrapped bone waiting for a carrier going the right way, and a delivery board anyone may take work from.

places.name: The Eaten Meer
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 70 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: A xanmeer the forest took: root has replaced stone in about half the structure.
why.siteAdvantages: Nobody defended it and the ground is soft, so the roots won.
