places.hook: Diggers camped over the cairn field, upwind and out of sight of the track, who will buy from you or rob you depending on the hour.

places.name: Twyllbek Crown
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 39 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, sightline, region.

why.founding: The Barsaebic compound at Twyllbek has one block whose upper courses are still sound and whose collapsed stair has left the outside face climbable — so the ruin's real content is not inside it at all.
why.siteAdvantages: The block stands on the compound's high corner, which is enough elevation to clear the scrub and see the Blackwood road for four kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. Treasure-hunters, couriers cutting a corner and one persistent Collections surveyor all use the top for their own reasons.
why.pressures: The climbable face is climbable because it is failing; two courses have gone in the last decade and the route changes each time.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would stop existing as a place at all if the face came down, and the only people who would notice are the couriers.

hardConstraints: a standing ruin block with a failing climbable face
places.hook: The one Ayleid block still standing to its upper courses, and the collapsed stair makes a climb to the top of it.

places.name: Twyllbek Ruins
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 1009 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A Barsaebic Ayleid compound from the exile centuries, close enough to Gideon that the city's antiquities trade starts here.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry terrace over a spring — Ayleid siting logic, and the reason Gideon's diggers keep coming back.
why.occupantsMotive: The diggers want stones with light in them; the Collections chapter wants the same stones back; both are here most months.
why.pressures: Every season of digging takes more of the wall; the Barsaebic layer is being consumed to prove it existed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be protected properly if Gideon's council ever thought a ruin was worth a guard.

places.hook: The Barsaebic compound Gideon's antiquities trade was built on, dug over for a century and still not emptied.

places.name: Culvert Line
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 1787 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, remote.

why.founding: The correction to the embankment: a line of stone culverts cut and dressed on site, then never laid.
why.siteAdvantages: The stone was dressed where it was quarried, next to the line it was meant to serve.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it; squatters took the dressed blocks for foundations until the tribes made stone-taking a quarrel.
why.pressures: Post-Duskfall, building in dead stone is a moral error here, so the blocks sit where they were left.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would vanish in a decade if anyone with a use for stone lived nearby.

hardConstraints: a line of dressed but unlaid stone
places.hook: Culverts cut, dressed and never laid, lying in a line across the plain; they have been lived in ever since.

places.name: Weighed Cart
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 266 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Gideon's council put a tower where the road forks for the clay pits, because the pits' output is the one export it can measure.
why.siteAdvantages: A knoll commanding both forks and the river landing below them.
why.occupantsMotive: The tower's clerk is paid on what he records, so he records everything.
why.pressures: The potters route half their carts round it by night and everyone knows.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pointless if the clay bank moved, which it does every generation.

hardConstraints: a rise with a view of both branches
must overlook a river landing within 60 m of water
places.hook: Every cart off the clay road is weighed under this tower, and the weight decides both the tax and the argument.

places.name: Westfield
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 722 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Argonian villagers took up field agriculture from their Imperial neighbours and now grow it better than they do.
why.siteAdvantages: Temperate grassland on the saddle's western apron: the only large stretch of arable in the west.
why.occupantsMotive: They farm because grain sells in Gideon at whatever price they ask in a bad year.
why.pressures: The fields are held in common and the Imperial grants overlap them on paper; nobody has tested it in court.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would fight, in court or otherwise, the first time somebody did.

places.hook: Argonian villagers who took field farming from their Imperial neighbours and now do it better; the best bread in the west.

places.name: Low Fen House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 298 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, hinterland.

why.founding: The College of Whispers works where nobody watches, and the fen edge is the least watched habitable ground near Gideon.
why.siteAdvantages: A stilt house over standing water, reachable by one pole-punt and no path at all.
why.occupantsMotive: They study Hist-sap chemistry and say they study hydrology.
why.pressures: The village that ferries them has begun to ask what the barrels are for.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be gone overnight, house and all, if the question were ever pressed properly.

hardConstraints: must stand over standing water, reachable only by punt
places.hook: The College of Whispers works where nobody watches, one punt out into the fen, and they are hiring for exactly that reason.

places.name: Xi-Tsei
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 640 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-fringe.the-second-empire-locks (+0.47).

why.founding: The ground where a whole community was killed in 1E 2820, and where the Sul-Xan trace their grievance from. Lore:Xi-Tsei puts the site on the southern strip of Blackwood, which is administered as Cyrodiil; we place it inside our province deliberately, because the border there has moved more than once and the massacre is Argonian history wherever the line currently runs.
why.siteAdvantages: An open flat between two ridges — the only place in the Blackwood where an army could be made to stand and fight.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here; the Sul-Xan come annually and leave marks; the Four Winds come annually and remove them.
why.pressures: Two peoples curate the same field in opposite directions, and both editions are visible.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be settled again only if both traditions lapsed, which neither will.

hardConstraints: an open flat with two ridge flanks
must sit below the rim break, in the lowland fringe, never in the border mountains
places.hook: The ground where a whole community was killed in 1E 2820, and from which every Sul-Xan grievance since is traced.

places.name: The Potentate's Works
places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 2), 252 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, hinterland, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.intact-fort (+0.41).

why.founding: Versidue-Shaie was the Akaviri Potentate, and the works his people left in this basin while building the Rose are not Cyrodilic in any detail.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quarry road between the Robbed City and the Rose — the logistics of a single-day construction, made permanent.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Its stone-handling gear was designed for atronachs and makes no sense for people.
why.pressures: It is the best surviving Akaviri civil work in the province and nobody in the basin knows what it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: An identification would bring outside scholars and their money into a district that wants neither.

places.hook: Lifting sockets sized for something inhumanly strong, and Akaviri tool-marks on every dressed face.

places.name: The Cordon Hearth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 132 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.vampiric-cloud-ground (+1.47).

why.founding: A kept fire on the southern approach, built against one of the cordon stones because that was the only marker on the road.
why.siteAdvantages: At the midpoint of an eight-kilometre stretch with no settlement.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by Rockspring on a rota, badly in winter and well in the trading season.
why.pressures: Travellers who know the district avoid sleeping here because of what the stone next to it means.
why.wouldChangeIf: Moving it two hundred metres would double its use, and nobody will move it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing
places.hook: A kept fire built against a plague cordon stone, using the marker as one wall.

places.name: Basin Swallow
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 276 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.necromantic-dig (+1.47).

why.founding: A collapse in the western feeder country that takes an entire stream underground and does not give it back anywhere anyone has found.
why.siteAdvantages: A genuine rarity in this province — a hole the marsh has not filled in, and the only one in the basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives on the rim. Something lives below the first ledge.
why.pressures: It is almost certainly connected to the Blue Hole, and nobody has proved it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Proving the connection would open a route from the western hills into the lake floor.

hardConstraints: a stream that goes under and does not come back
places.hook: A whole stream pours into this hole and nobody has ever found where it comes out.

places.name: Blackrose
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'blackrose' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Built by the Lilmothiit in a lake where three rivers converge; rebuilt by the Empire after 1E 2837 and held since by whoever holds the island core.
why.siteAdvantages: The hinge of the south: Murkwood's water from the north-east, Oliis Bay from the south, eastern Blackwood from the west, and Bramman's concealed river out to Topal Bay. The lake is a wide fringe marsh with a hard island in it, and the island is the city.
why.occupantsMotive: Toll and transit revenue, and whatever comes out of the Rose. Many have entered its walls; the city keeps the ones who do not leave.
why.pressures: It remembers raising an army against the Third Empire and remembers a battlemage breaking it with a single spell; it distrusts magic and outsiders in that order.
why.wouldChangeIf: Whoever took the island core would take the whole southern route network with it, which is why the core has changed hands four times.

hardConstraints: island in standing water at a confluence
places.hook: Every road and every river in the south ends at the same island, and the island charges for it.

places.name: Speaks-Below-The-Water
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Blackrose's Hist stands in the lake rather than in the city, and the lake rose over it — the register's drowned tree.
why.siteAdvantages: It grew on the island's old shore; three centuries of raised lake level put six metres of water over its crown.
why.occupantsMotive: Tenders dive to it. The city has no other tree and will not plant one, because planting one would be a judgement on this one.
why.pressures: An underwater Hist cannot be communed with in any of the usual ways, and the tenders have improvised a practice nobody else recognises.
why.wouldChangeIf: Lowering the lake would expose it — and it is not agreed whether that would save it or kill it.

hardConstraints: inland of the coast plain, on the Blackrose lake system
places.hook: Blackrose's Hist is alive, whole and six metres under the lake, and its tenders have invented a practice nobody else recognises.

places.name: Blackrose Prison
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 2), 140 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Built by Potentate Versidue-Shaie's battlemage Pelladil Direnni out of the rubble of the ancient Lilmothiit city, by an army of stone atronachs, in a single day, and named for the city whose stone it is made of.
why.siteAdvantages: Marsh on every side and one causeway: the Imperial siting rule for this province, executed perfectly. The ground itself is quiet country — everything dangerous here is either behind the gate or under it.
why.occupantsMotive: Prison-born families three generations deep who hold it as their inheritance, plus exiles and outlaws; they resent being called a prison and have a real argument that they are not one.
why.pressures: Umbriel left something in the lower levels that nobody has cleared; the Chainbreakers want the place opened; Blackrose wants the toll it takes on the south road.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the lower levels would make the Rose a genuine settlement, and everybody who benefits from its reputation knows it.

places.hook: Three generations were born inside these walls, and none of them will tell you what is behind the bricked stair.

places.name: The Refused Vault
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 85 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A vault for the ashes of those the basin's villages refused to stake — blasphemers, oath-breakers and, latterly, anyone who died in the Rose unclaimed.
why.siteAdvantages: Cut into the limestone above the flood, deliberately far from any burial ground.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who accepts urns and refuses to discuss any of them.
why.pressures: The Chainbreakers argue that the prison dead here were refused for the wrong reason and want them out.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling that the prison dead may be staked would empty half the vault.

places.hook: A rock-cut vault of urns, each cut with the one word that explains why the village refused it.

places.name: Bramman's Head
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in deep river corridor (danger band 3), 604 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, danger, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'region-relaxed'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.lake-divers-yard (+1.07).

why.founding: The inland end of the concealed river a First-Era fleet sailed up from the coast: where Bramman's water finally meets the Blackrose lakes.
why.siteAdvantages: A screened lagoon head with just enough depth for a laden hull, and a bank firm enough to tranship on.
why.occupantsMotive: A small permanent crew who keep the head open, charge for the last mile, and have never let the route be charted.
why.pressures: Blackrose's toll authority has walked to within two hundred paces of the head on a fisher's footpath and has still never found the mouth of the river, because the mouth is out in the screen and the head is not.
why.wouldChangeIf: Charting the river would make Blackrose a sea port and destroy the pilots at both ends.

hardConstraints: at the head of a screened lagoon, hidden from the open water
places.hook: The inland end of a river that has never been charted, with a thousand-year-old iron ring for every rope on it.

places.name: Open House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Blackrose Chainbreakers' shelter for people who have come out of the Rose, an Owing, or a toll pit, and have nowhere that will take them; the Freed Rows in the north send them word, not supplies.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the toll line, on water, with two exits and no fixed sign.
why.occupantsMotive: Board, work and legal help; the Chainbreakers' whole practical programme in one building.
why.pressures: Two of the powers they oppose fund half their neighbours, and the shelter is watched constantly.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single violent incident here would let the city close it lawfully.

places.hook: No sign, more doors than rooms, and a wall of bone-tags returned from the Rose.

places.name: Cordon Two, Under-Stores
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 192 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Every cordon post on the Flu line had a ration store cut into the bank behind it, and the stores outlived the posts by sixteen centuries because they were the only dry cellars in the basin.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry vaulted cellars in a levee bank, above every recorded flood, on a line of stones nobody will move.
why.occupantsMotive: The Owing's collectors keep distrained goods here between the taking and the auction, which is a use the stores were built for and a law they are not.
why.pressures: Everything in the cellars belongs to somebody who is still alive and still counting the days.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening the cellars to their owners would break the Owing's whole practice in the south.

hardConstraints: cut into a bank above the flood maximum
places.hook: Everything the Owing has taken in the south is racked in here, tagged and dated, and all of it belongs to somebody.

places.name: Bare Lake
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 5), 329 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.marsh-giant-ground-basin (+0.56).

why.founding: The lake's shallow southern arm empties for six weeks every dry season, exposing four square kilometres of bed that is a metre under water the rest of the year.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide flat arm barely a metre deep, with an outlet that drops below its sill in the dry.
why.occupantsMotive: Everyone. The drawdown is a local event: the whole shore walks out onto the bed and takes what the year has dropped.
why.pressures: Grave-stakes from a drowned burial ground stand exposed during the drawdown, which forces an annual argument about what may be taken.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter cycle would end the drawdown and the whole annual custom with it.

hardConstraints: inland of the coast plain, on the Blackrose lake system
places.hook: For six weeks a year the lake bed is a market; the other forty-six it is a dive.

places.name: The Drowned Gallery
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 491 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Empire tried to drain the Rose's approach with a gallery driven under the levee, worked by gangs small enough to fit it; the lake came in through the face and the gallery has been full ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: Under the levee, below the water table, with its head shaft still open in the lake bed.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing that breathes. The lake-divers know the shaft and will not take work in it.
why.pressures: It runs toward the Rose's foundations, and the necromancers digging from the landward side know it does.
why.wouldChangeIf: Pumping it out would give three separate parties a dry way under the prison.

hardConstraints: under a levee, running toward the Rose
places.hook: A drowned Imperial gallery running under the levee toward the Rose's foundations, with the barrows still on the rail.

places.name: The Windlass Reckoning
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 266 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.rose-outworks (+0.47).

why.founding: The western feeder has a two-hundred-metre sill of rock and old log-jam that no laden hull can pass, so hulls are dragged around it.
why.siteAdvantages: A low saddle beside the narrows where a greased timber slipway can be laid on a workable gradient.
why.occupantsMotive: A drag crew with a windlass, paid by the hull, who also control who goes upstream and when.
why.pressures: The crew's monopoly is total and their maintenance of the slipway is minimal.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the sill would open the western route and end the crew.

hardConstraints: at a shoaling sill in a confined channel
places.hook: A greased slipway, a hand-windlass and a crew who decide how long your day is.

places.name: The Counting Ground
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 11 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where Blackrose buried the Knahaten dead of three peoples, in the order they died and without distinguishing between them.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel terrace above the flood, the only ground in the basin that would take that many graves.
why.occupantsMotive: A memorial rota that includes Argonian grave-singers and nobody else, because nobody else is left to send anyone.
why.pressures: Two of the three peoples buried here are extinct, and the third does their remembering.
why.wouldChangeIf: Any attempt to separate the burials by people would be both impossible and obscene.

places.hook: Three peoples buried in the order they died, in one trench four hundred metres long with a stake at each end.

places.name: Holding Fields, Cordon Three
places.whySiteWon: island in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 546 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon: Lilmothiit refugees fleeing the Knahaten Flu in Murkmire fled inland toward Blackrose, and their fate is unclear. This is where Blackrose stopped them.
why.siteAdvantages: On the southern approach at the last narrows before the lake, where a cordon could actually be held.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody now. It was a village-sized pen with a fence, a gate, a ration store and a burial ground that is larger than the village.
why.pressures: This is the answer to the unclear fate of a whole people, and Blackrose has never once discussed it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Anyone who published the ration ledgers would make the city's founding families answer for it.

hardConstraints: on the road, at the last narrows on the southern cordon out of Blackrose
places.hook: The fence faces inward, the gate furniture is on the outside, and the burial ground is four times the size of the village.

places.name: Fort Cordon
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 334 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.akaviri-works (+0.41).

why.founding: Built to hold the Flu cordon's central narrows and kept in commission long after; abandoned intact when the Empire left.
why.siteAdvantages: Commands the narrows and the road at the one point where both pass together.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty, roofed, and periodically occupied by whoever is currently strongest on the road.
why.pressures: It is the best building in the basin outside the city and everybody knows it is empty.
why.wouldChangeIf: Permanent occupation by any faction would give them the southern road.

hardConstraints: commands something that no longer matters
places.hook: Roof on, gate off, and three different parties' fire-scars in the same courtyard.

places.name: Ash-Hand
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 3), 392 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.rockspring (+0.95).

why.founding: A Kothringi village of the people canon places in the Blackrose region, emptied by the Knahaten Flu in a single season.
why.siteAdvantages: A river terrace with a landing — good ground, which is why it was never resettled by anyone superstitious.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Argonian villages nearby keep its boundary marked and do not cross it.
why.pressures: The Flu is the founding trauma of half the province's demography, and this is what it actually looks like on the ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: Proof that the ground is safe would put a village back on it within a year.

hardConstraints: coastal and riverine — they were sea-going
places.hook: The silver-skinned people's houses, standing to head height, with the flu-year's stores still lidded in the pits.

places.name: Spine
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 43 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.ledgered-blackguards (+0.83).

why.founding: A village built as one continuous boardwalk out from the shore into the lake, extended a house at a time for three centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow shelf that runs eight hundred metres out from the shore before it drops.
why.occupantsMotive: Position on the spine is seniority: the oldest households are at the shore end and the newest are over deep water.
why.pressures: The far end is now over the drop and each new house is more expensive and less safe than the last.
why.wouldChangeIf: A storm surge would take the outer third and reset the village's whole social order.

hardConstraints: crosses water rather than sitting beside it
places.hook: Seniority runs shorewards: the further out you sleep, the newer and poorer you are.

places.name: The Barge Yard
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 110 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.lake-submerged-xanmeer (+0.51).

why.founding: Three centuries of laden barges have gone down in this lake, most of them in the same two places, and someone was always going to work them.
why.siteAdvantages: On the shore nearest the deep hole where the wrecks concentrate, with a crane frame and a drying floor.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews dive for cargo, not hulls; the toll families buy the recovered goods at a discount that reflects who they are.
why.pressures: Some of the sunk cargo was insured, some was smuggled, and the paperwork for both still exists in the city.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rise in the lake would put the wrecks out of free-diving range entirely.

places.hook: A chart of every sinking in the lake, painted on the shed wall by the people who work them.

places.name: Under-Longmont
places.whySiteWon: ford in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 190 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, submerged, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.akaviri-works (+0.81).

why.founding: The village Longmont replaced: the lake level rose across the fourteenth century of the Third Era and the old settlement was rebuilt a kilometre up the shore.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands in five to eight metres of clear cold lake water, complete, because nobody demolished anything — they simply left.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Longmont's households still know which house down there was theirs.
why.pressures: Diving on your own family's drowned house is acceptable; diving on somebody else's is not, and the rule is enforced.
why.wouldChangeIf: A drop in lake level would expose it and force a decision about who owns what.

places.hook: Longmont's older self standing upright under the lake, its street legible and its grave-stakes still in rows.

places.name: The North Stage
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The lake is eleven kilometres across at its widest and the north road ends at a stage rather than going round.
why.siteAdvantages: A short crossing between two headlands where the lake narrows to nine hundred metres.
why.occupantsMotive: A city concession, run efficiently, which is unusual enough here to be remarked on.
why.pressures: It carries the Murkwood-side traffic, which is the traffic nobody wants counted.
why.wouldChangeIf: A crossing further north would bypass the city's count entirely.

hardConstraints: across water too deep or wide to ford
places.hook: Eleven kilometres of open lake, or a stage, a stone slip and a board that lists cargo instead of names.

places.name: Lake Meer
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 280 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'island' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on submerged, parent, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.lake-divers-yard (+0.51).

why.founding: A xanmeer that stood on the lake's old floor before the water rose, now entirely submerged and entirely intact.
why.siteAdvantages: Eighteen metres down in cold clear water, with its terraces stepping up to within six metres of the surface.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing. Its doorways are sealed by silt at the base and open at the third terrace.
why.pressures: It is the deepest reachable structure in the south and the divers who work it treat it as a different profession from lake salvage.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt slump would close the open terrace and seal it entirely.

places.hook: A stone pyramid standing whole on a lake floor, unlooted because eighteen metres of cold water is a better lock than a door.

places.name: The Book House
places.whySiteWon: ford in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 110 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.lake-boardwalk-village (+0.83).

why.founding: The Blackguards' heirs of the Blackrose region run their business like a counting house, because their inheritance from the Rose was a ledger, not a gang.
why.siteAdvantages: An unremarkable water-house on a back channel with three exits and a clear view of the toll quay.
why.occupantsMotive: They broker debt, cargo and silence, and they are better at accounts than the city is.
why.pressures: Their ledger is the most complete record of who owes what in the south, and everyone wants it for different reasons.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the ledger would end them; they have three copies and everybody knows it.

places.hook: The front room keeps proper books; the back room is where the debts are actually settled.

places.name: Robbed City
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 104 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, danger, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.basin-hearth-house (+2.35).

why.founding: The ancient Lilmothiit city Blackrose stands on and was quarried out of: canon says the Rose was built from its rubble in a single day.
why.siteAdvantages: A whole vanished city's stone lying within a day of the site that needed it — which is why the Rose exists at all.
why.occupantsMotive: No inheritors: the Lilmothiit died of the Knahaten Flu. Blackrose's own foundations are its remains.
why.pressures: What is left is a robbed-out ground plan, and every carved block in the district can be matched back to a socket here.
why.wouldChangeIf: A systematic survey would reconstruct a lost people's city from the buildings it was stolen into.

hardConstraints: within 400 m of Blackrose — the city stands on it
places.hook: A vulpine city robbed down to its footings, with every stolen block still matchable to the socket it came out of.

places.name: Longmont
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 219 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.kothringi-ruin-basin (+1.45).

why.founding: Canon-named as Blackrose's south-western neighbour: a lake-shore village on the approach, and the last stop before the city's toll gates.
why.siteAdvantages: A long shallow flat on the lake's south-west shore, poleable all year and outside the city's wall line.
why.occupantsMotive: Everything bound for Blackrose by land is broken to boats here, by people who are not the city and charge less than it.
why.pressures: Blackrose has twice tried to bring Longmont inside its toll regime and twice found the village simply stops handling freight.
why.wouldChangeIf: Absorption into the city's toll regime would move the whole trade to Rockspring in one season.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
inland of the coast plain, on the Blackrose lake system
places.hook: A kilometre of stilt village that will break your cargo to boats for less than the city charges.

places.name: The Water Reckoning
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 88 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tower on the north-east river where the Murkwood water enters the lake system, put there to count hulls.
why.siteAdvantages: On a rock spur the channel must pass within thirty metres of.
why.occupantsMotive: Two counters and a boom; the boom has not been lowered in thirty years and is maintained anyway.
why.pressures: Traffic from the north-east is the least legible and most valuable, and the counters know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Lowering the boom would be an act of policy that would be answered from upriver.

hardConstraints: commands a channel or a road
places.hook: A chain boom that has not been lowered in thirty years, greased and rust-free anyway.

places.name: The Trodden Ground
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 260 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.drawdown-flat (+0.56).

why.founding: A marsh giant's range on the north-east marsh, marked by two centuries of the same paths being walked.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide shallow marsh with reed stands and no human settlement, on the Murkwood side of the lake.
why.occupantsMotive: The animal. Its paths are the only firm walking in eight square kilometres, which is a very tempting trap.
why.pressures: The paths are also the fastest route toward the Murkwood verge, and guides use them anyway.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing will move it; it has been here longer than the city.

places.hook: The only firm walking in eight square kilometres was trodden by the thing you would meet on it.

places.name: Murkwood Verge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 236 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, parent, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.rockspring (+1.00).

why.founding: The forest that ever moves, last located north-east of Blackrose; findable only via the Conclave of Baal at Stormhold reading the Elder Scrolls with an ancient tablet.
why.siteAdvantages: A stretch of deep marsh north-east of the lake where the tree line is wrong on every survey and no two surveys agree. The danger is not in the ground, which is ordinary: it arrived with the forest and it leaves with it.
why.occupantsMotive: Medusas and fellrunners. Nothing that lives here is from anywhere.
why.pressures: The verge is where the forest is *now*; the villages within a day of it keep a tally of where it has been.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its movement is off-screen lore between visits — the verge is a fixed site whose surroundings tell you it has moved.

hardConstraints: north-east of Blackrose, off every road
deep marsh, never firm lowland or coast
places.hook: A wall of forest standing across open marsh with no transition, and a field of drowned stumps a kilometre behind it where it used to stand.

places.name: The Blue Hole
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 176 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A karst shaft in the lake floor that drops well below the lake bed and connects to something else.
why.siteAdvantages: A vertical hole nine metres wide in an otherwise flat lake bottom, with a cold current coming out of it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Two lake-divers have gone down it and one came back.
why.pressures: The current reverses seasonally, which means it goes somewhere and that somewhere fills and empties.
why.wouldChangeIf: Mapping where it surfaces would rewrite the basin's hydrology and open a route.

places.hook: Two lake-divers have gone down the blue hole and one came back up.

places.name: The Quiet Excavation
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 424 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.basin-sinkhole (+1.47).

why.founding: Someone is digging toward the Rose's lower levels from outside, and they are not looking for the living.
why.siteAdvantages: Four hundred metres from the Rose's foundations, on a spoil-hidden rise in the marsh, on the alignment of the flooded tunnel.
why.occupantsMotive: They know exactly what Umbriel left down there and want it, which is a much worse motive than looting.
why.pressures: The Rose's families have not noticed. The Chainbreakers have, and have not decided what to do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Breaking into the lower levels from outside would release what the bricked stair contains.

places.hook: An alignment string running dead straight from a shored shaft toward a prison four hundred metres away.

places.name: The Cordon
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 23 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, bound; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The line Blackrose held during the Flu, marked in stone every hundred paces from the hills to the water.
why.siteAdvantages: It follows the narrows, which is the only line a cordon could hold in this basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody enforces it. Every stone is still standing and nobody has moved one.
why.pressures: Villages on the far side of the line still describe themselves as being outside, sixteen centuries later.
why.wouldChangeIf: Removing the stones would be a civic decision nobody wants to propose.

hardConstraints: uses water as part of the line where it can
places.hook: Six kilometres of hundred-pace marker stones, every one still standing, every one cut with the same three words.

places.name: Third Generation
places.whySiteWon: island in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 291 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Prison-born households who left the Rose and cannot join any village, because none of them has ever been near a Hist.
why.siteAdvantages: An island in the marsh two hours off the causeway: defensible, unclaimed, and nobody else wants it.
why.occupantsMotive: They are building a community from nothing, with no tree, no clan and no funeral rite that anyone recognises.
why.pressures: They will not go back to the Rose and cannot go forward to a village; Hissmir is weeks away and the pilgrimage is talked about the way people talk about an inheritance they will never claim.
why.wouldChangeIf: A village willing to sponsor them into tree-access would dissolve the settlement in a season.

hardConstraints: wherever they were allowed to stop
places.hook: A finished tree-enclosure with nothing planted in it, swept every day, waiting for a cutting nobody will give.

places.name: Welloc's Lines
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 348 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Thrown up around the city when Blackrose rebelled against the Third Empire and raised an army; abandoned when Empress Morihatha's battlemage Welloc broke the rebellion with a spell instead of a siege.
why.siteAdvantages: Sited on the dry ground commanding all three approaches — competent, complete, and never used.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Grazing now, with the ditch profiles perfectly legible from any rise.
why.pressures: A city that remembers raising an army looks at these lines every day.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. The earth stays. That is what makes it a monument.

hardConstraints: dry ground with a view of the target
places.hook: Complete siege lines with sharp unfought ditch profiles, and not one arrowhead anywhere in them.

places.name: Rockspring
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 181 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.kothringi-ruin-basin (+0.95).

why.founding: Canon-named as Blackrose's north-western neighbour, built along a natural levee on the western feeder around the one hard spring in the basin.
why.siteAdvantages: A levee crest a metre above every recorded flood, with a rock spring that runs clean when the whole basin is brown.
why.occupantsMotive: The spring is the asset; in a bad year the village sells water to boats and does not apologise for it.
why.pressures: Longmont's freight trade is the one they want and cannot get, because the feeder is too shallow for laden hulls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dredged feeder would make Rockspring the western freight village and end Longmont's monopoly.

hardConstraints: above the seasonal maximum, beside a channel
places.hook: The one hard spring in the basin, sold by the cup in a bad year and not apologised for.

places.name: Rose Lower Levels
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 229 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: The Rose's lowest levels flooded when the marsh took the foundations, and what Umbriel left in 4E 48 is still down there.
why.siteAdvantages: Below the water table, sealed by a stair the prison-born families bricked up two generations ago.
why.occupantsMotive: The undead, behind a bricked stair that nobody has opened. The families above will confirm nothing, and while the brick holds there is nothing here to fight.
why.pressures: The Chainbreakers' bone claims include people who died down there; the families' claim to legitimacy depends on the stair staying shut.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the lower levels would make the Rose a settlement and end its reputation — which is exactly what the families are frightened of.

hardConstraints: a flooded stair under the prison yard
places.hook: Behind the bricked stair the Rose goes on downward, under the water table, and Umbriel's dead are still standing in it.

places.name: Outworks, Cordon One
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 17 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.feeder-portage (+0.47).

why.founding: A fortress raised in a single day still had to receive people slowly, so the Empire dug holding pits and a ditch line outside the walls and processed arrivals there before the gate ever opened.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground on the causeway side of the marsh, close enough to the Rose to march a chained line in and far enough that the yard never saw it.
why.occupantsMotive: A raw Blackguard crew who found roofed stone pits with locking floors already dug, and use them for exactly what they were dug for.
why.pressures: The prison-born families will not police ground they refuse to be associated with, and Vaunting says it is the prison's business.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the crew out would give the Chainbreakers a receiving house within sight of the causeway.

hardConstraints: on the Rose causeway approach, 300–700 m outside the prison
places.hook: Six numbered Imperial holding pits outside the Rose, with new locks on all of them.

places.name: Vaunting
places.whySiteWon: ford in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 61 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Rose needed feeding for twelve centuries, and the supply town the Empire built for that outlived both the Empire and the prison's official function.
why.siteAdvantages: On the causeway road at the last firm ground before the marsh, with a barge landing and a walled magazine.
why.occupantsMotive: It still supplies the Rose, now on commercial terms, and the arrangement is the town's entire economy.
why.pressures: Half the town is descended from prison staff and half from released prisoners, and the two halves marry but do not forget.
why.wouldChangeIf: Emptying the Rose would end the town within a decade.

hardConstraints: at a crossing or a road
places.hook: The town that fed a prison for twelve centuries and still chalks its ration tally on the magazine door every week.

places.name: Wide-Furrow
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 74 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The basin's saltrice village, on the flood-fed grassland where the eastern feeder spreads out each wet season.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow annual flood over firm ground: the exact condition saltrice needs and almost nothing else tolerates.
why.occupantsMotive: They feed the city, the Rose and Vaunting, and they know the value of that in a basin with three mouths to feed.
why.pressures: The Rose pays late and the city pays in tariff credit, and neither is money.
why.wouldChangeIf: A refusal to supply the Rose would be a political act with immediate consequences.

places.hook: Three mouths to feed in this basin and one village that grows the grain for all of them.

places.name: The Under-Counting
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 186 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A holding pit under a toll counting-house for debtors who could not pay at the gate, in a city that officially has no such practice.
why.siteAdvantages: Beneath the counting quay, dry, private, and eleven steps from where the debt is recorded.
why.occupantsMotive: The toll families use it for days, not years, and consider that an important distinction.
why.pressures: It is currently occupied, and one of the occupants is somebody Blackrose's council would rather were not there.
why.wouldChangeIf: Public exposure would break the toll compact's standing with the city.

places.hook: A hatch in the floor of the room where the tariffs are argued, in a city that officially has no such practice.

places.name: Three Gates
places.whySiteWon: ford in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 106 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Blackrose lives on three-river transit and tolls; the toll town sits at the confluence itself, outside the walls, where all three routes must pass.
why.siteAdvantages: The confluence: no cargo reaches the lake from any direction without passing this point.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian toll-holding families' compact that predates the current city government and has outlasted three of them.
why.pressures: Everyone who trades in the south hates it and pays it; Threewater exists specifically to avoid it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the compact would give the city direct control of its own revenue for the first time.

places.hook: Three rivers, one counting-quay, and a family compact that has outlasted three city governments.

places.name: Given Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 482 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.basin-hearth-house (+1.47).

why.founding: Where Welloc's vampiric cloud displaced the rebels' strength and skill to their opponents, and the Blackrose army stopped being an army in about a minute.
why.siteAdvantages: The open ground north of the city where the rebel army formed up, chosen by them, which is the part nobody has forgiven.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Grave-singers refuse to work it: they say the dead here are not diminished but *emptied*, which is a different problem.
why.pressures: Blackrose's distrust of battlemages is a policy, not a prejudice, and this field is the reason.
why.wouldChangeIf: A grave-singer willing to stake this field would end a two-century-old civic wound.

hardConstraints: where an army could deploy — rare here
places.hook: A field of unstaked dead where the grass still grows in the shape of a formation and nothing has been carried away.

places.name: The Sealed Vault
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 30 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.wisp-lure-basin (+0.56).

why.founding: A vault under a ruined works, sealed by the people who found what had grown in it and left the door welded.
why.siteAdvantages: A stone undercroft with one door and no other opening — which is why sealing it worked.
why.occupantsMotive: The voriplasm. It has been sealed long enough that the seal is now the archaeology.
why.pressures: The sealing party's note is still nailed to the door and is perfectly explicit.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening it would release something the province has a specific and unhappy history with.

places.hook: A stone door with iron welded across it and a nailed board still legible after two hundred years.

places.name: Threewater
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where the western feeder from eastern Blackwood meets the lake system, a market grew for everyone unwilling to pay Blackrose's gate toll.
why.siteAdvantages: A river junction with firm banks on three sides and enough water for laden hulls in every season but the driest.
why.occupantsMotive: It exists to be cheaper than Blackrose, and its whole civic life is organised around staying that way.
why.pressures: Blackrose has twice sent 'inspectors'; the town has twice paid them and continued.
why.wouldChangeIf: An enforced toll here would collapse the market back into the city within two years.

hardConstraints: a junction of navigable waters, or a road crossing
inland of the coast plain, on the Blackrose lake system
places.hook: Everything Blackrose sells, a river junction earlier and a toll cheaper.

places.name: The Lantern Fen
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 225 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.imperial-penal-south.voriplasm-vault (+0.56).

why.founding: A fen on the Rose approach where lights move at night in exactly the pattern of a lit causeway.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly beside the floating road, which is the whole problem.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever makes the lights. It has been doing it for as long as the road has been there.
why.pressures: People walking to the Rose at night have followed them off the road; Vaunting posts a lamp-keeper in the bad months.
why.wouldChangeIf: A properly lit causeway would end the deaths and cost Vaunting money it does not have.

hardConstraints: open standing water on a night route
places.hook: Lights across the fen at night, spaced exactly like the causeway's lamps, moving very slowly.

places.name: The Alessian Hull
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 93 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A First-Era warship from the fleet that chased Red Bramman, lost on the reef and settled upright in eleven metres.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep enough to be intact, shallow enough to dive on one breath at the stern.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody owns it; four Soulrest families dispute that.
why.pressures: Two centuries of salvage have stripped the deck; the hold is silted and nobody has cut into it.
why.wouldChangeIf: One good season of settled water would let a diving team open the hold properly.

hardConstraints: on the reef line, in eight to fifteen metres of salt water
places.hook: A First-Era warship sitting upright in eleven metres, with its holds shut and nobody down there.

places.name: Alten Meerhleel
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 186 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'natural-harbour' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, navigable; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's outsider-facing port north-west of Lilmoth: a working two-culture port below city scale, where an Argonian raft-quarter and an outsiders' warehouse row front the same water. With Lilmoth destroyed for a century and a half the bay's outside trade came here, and enough of it stayed that the quay outgrew the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Slow deep water inside the bar, deep enough for a laden hull to lie off and be worked by lighters, with firm enough margin behind it for a warehouse row — an *alten-* name, meaning outsiders were always the point.
why.occupantsMotive: Lightermen, Argonian raft-quarter families and factors from four ports; the customs presence is one clerk and a tariff shed nobody staffs, which is the entire commercial proposition.
why.pressures: Now that Lilmoth is rebuilt the two ports are direct rivals, and Meerhleel's whole advantage is that it asks nothing — an advantage that Corimont, the province's actual free port, holds far more securely.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Lilmoth's council ever dropped its tariffs, Meerhleel would lose the only reason anyone sails past a real harbour.

hardConstraints: sheltered navigable water off the legal lanes
places.hook: The outsiders' port: you can buy and sell here as a foreigner without asking Lilmoth's permission.

places.name: Ashfield
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 82 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Founded on the ash-enriched firm lowland left by the Great Burn, which turned out to grow food better than the forest had.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry firm ground, deep burn ash, and the coast road for a market.
why.occupantsMotive: Mixed Argonian and Imperial-descended households farming the one soil in the district that improved.
why.pressures: The ash is finite; yields have been falling for three generations and nobody says so out loud.
why.wouldChangeIf: Exhausted soil would empty it within twenty years.

places.hook: Burn-ash fields feed the coast road, and the holders will sell you a bed and a hot meal.

places.name: Ashroot
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 785 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.keshu-grove (+0.50).

why.founding: The nearest Hist village to Soulrest, and the reason the burn country still has Argonians in it at all.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise that the peat fire went around, with its tree's roots reaching water the burn never reached.
why.occupantsMotive: They kept the tree alive through the Burn and consider that the defining fact of their village.
why.pressures: The burn country around it is bad ground and honest about it: the jungle edge here kills people who walk it alone, and the village says so at the gate.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the tree would disperse the village into the city within a generation.

hardConstraints: a rise the peat fire went around, with root-water below it
places.hook: The last Hist between Soulrest and the burn country; they will shelter you and warn you.

places.name: Sees-No-Root
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 132 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village whose Hist died with its mnemic egg unrecovered, and which has organised its entire remaining life around that fact.
why.siteAdvantages: Unchanged good ground — they stayed, which is the unusual decision.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep the empty enclosure, keep the offices, and keep telling the memories aloud because there is nothing left to hold them.
why.pressures: The children are leaving for Lilmoth; the recitation takes six days and fewer people can do it each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A recovered egg would restore the village at a stroke, and every treasure-hunter in Murkmire knows that.

places.hook: A village that lost its tree and kept going; they will pay well for news of the egg.

places.name: Tideward Stage
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 339 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The coast road crosses the river south of Soulrest where it is too deep to ford and too wide to bridge cheaply.
why.siteAdvantages: A narrows with firm banks on both sides and slack water for an hour either side of the turn.
why.occupantsMotive: The ferry family also hire out as guides upriver, which is the more profitable half of the business.
why.pressures: Guides are hired to go upriver far more often than the traffic justifies, and the family does not discuss where.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bridge here would end both trades and has been proposed three times.

hardConstraints: across water too deep or wide to ford
places.hook: The ferry family will take you across for coin, and upriver for rather more, and will not say where.

places.name: Bramman's Screen
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 88 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The seaward mouth of the narrow winding river Red Bramman escaped the Alessian navy through, encased in dense mangrove.
why.siteAdvantages: Four channel mouths open off the same bay; only one carries water at the top of the tide, and only for about ninety minutes.
why.occupantsMotive: The pilots who know the run sell the knowledge and never write it down; a wrong channel strands a hull until the next tide.
why.pressures: It is a hidden route, not a scheduled lane — placing a marked ferry service on it would destroy the thing that makes it worth anything.
why.wouldChangeIf: A silt pulse could close it, or open a second, and the pilots' monopoly would end with it.

hardConstraints: tidal; passable only at low water
places.hook: Four channel mouths, one of them navigable, and only for ninety minutes at the top of the tide.

places.name: Bright-Throat Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 439 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's hospitable, artisan, alliance-brokering tribe, on the mangrove wall above Oliis Bay — the village that knits the region back together after each catastrophe.
why.siteAdvantages: A platform village standing clear of the tide on the mangrove wall, with one stair down to a beach landing: dry, defensible, and watching the whole approach to Lilmoth.
why.occupantsMotive: Diplomacy and craft. Their Listening-Tree and its chimes are why other tribes come to them rather than the reverse.
why.pressures: Everyone in Murkmire wants Bright-Throat's endorsement, which makes neutrality expensive to maintain.
why.wouldChangeIf: Taking a side in the Lilmoth–An-Xileel quarrel would cost them the role they are famous for.

hardConstraints: on the mangrove wall above a beach landing
places.hook: The friendliest door on the bay, and the one tribe that will broker for an outsider.

places.name: Chasepoint
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 38 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Imperial road stage east of Soulrest, canon-named as its neighbour; the Legion built it, the wreck-salvage families kept it.
why.siteAdvantages: Last firm ground before the coast road turns inland; a shingle beach below that catches everything the Southern Sea loses.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage rights are hereditary here and jealously counted; the stage's stable block is now a drying shed for recovered cordage.
why.pressures: No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries; the roof is Argonian thatch on Imperial walls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A revived coast road under a real toll authority would make it a proper town again.

places.hook: A wreck-salvage village on the road bend; whatever the sea lost last week is for sale here.

places.name: Fourth Stage
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 82 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An Imperial road stage counted from Soulrest, still called by its number two centuries after the count stopped mattering.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry rise with a well, at an Imperial day's march from the last one.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian family keeps it and rebuilt the roof in reed; they still use the Imperial numbering.
why.pressures: The well is the only good water for six miles and everyone knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A failed well would end the stage and shift the road's rhythm entirely.

places.hook: A well, a roof and a meal on the coast road, at the price the Legion set two centuries ago.

places.name: Cold Light
places.whySiteWon: islet in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 39 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Imperial harbour works lit the Topal approach for four centuries; the oil contract ended with the province.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest headland on the bay approach, and one of the few structures in the province that breaks the canopy line.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. A Soulrest chandler still bills the council for lamp oil that is never delivered.
why.pressures: The lantern glass is gone; the stair is sound; whoever relights it decides who profits from the bar.
why.wouldChangeIf: Relighting it kills the Long Bar and makes Soulrest's harbour honest.

places.hook: Climb the dead lighthouse and you can see the whole bay approach, including what the wreckers use.

places.name: Lights-From-Under
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 25 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A still fen where the water plants light from below all year, which is why the pilgrim route runs through it at night.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow, warm, flow-free basin — the conditions the glow needs, and rare.
why.occupantsMotive: Gatherers take the plants for lamp-jelly; pilgrims cross at night because the fen lights the way.
why.pressures: Harvesting dims it; the villages ration the take by an argument nobody enjoys having.
why.wouldChangeIf: Over-harvest would end both the trade and the route in the same season.

places.hook: The water lights from below all night, and the pilgrims walk it because of that.

places.name: Four-Hands Crown
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 269 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.inhabited-meer-murkmire (+0.73).

why.founding: A raised hammock's crown given over entirely to the ancestors of the villages around it — the only ground high enough to stay dry in any flood.
why.siteAdvantages: The highest dry ground in a wide floodplain, which makes it the only permanent burial terrace available.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages bury here in four sectors, and the sector boundaries are the oldest agreed lines in the district.
why.pressures: The hammock is running out of terrace and no village will yield an inch of its sector.
why.wouldChangeIf: A flood high enough to reach the crown would be read as a judgement on all four.

hardConstraints: the crown of a raised hammock, with standing water inside 100 m
places.hook: Four villages bury on this one dry crown, and something has been digging at the far end.

places.name: Tzelvei
places.whySiteWon: confluence in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 147 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village on a wooded hammock, reached only by water, with its fields on smaller hammocks around it.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry wooded rise in permanent marsh, with a ring of satellite hammocks at poling distance.
why.occupantsMotive: The hammock gives them the safest ground in the district and the longest journey to market, and they have chosen the former for centuries.
why.pressures: Every child leaves for Lilmoth for a season; roughly half return, and the number is falling.
why.wouldChangeIf: A poling route improvement would connect them to the city and change everything about them.

hardConstraints: a wooded rise in permanent marsh, reached only by water
places.hook: A dry bed and a hot floor in the middle of permanent marsh, if you can pole to it.

places.name: Head of Tide
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 88 m from the nearest route; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon puts a river starting just south of Soulrest and running north-east into the interior; this is the last point a sea-going hull can reach on it.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel sill across the channel: deep water below it, poling water above it, and firm banks for transhipment.
why.occupantsMotive: Everything going inland is broken down into canoe loads here, by people who charge for it.
why.pressures: Whoever controls this sill controls the whole interior trade of the south-west, and four parties know that.
why.wouldChangeIf: Dredging the sill would destroy the transhipment trade and enrich the city.

hardConstraints: a gravel sill where the tide stops, firm banks both sides
south of Soulrest, inside the coast zone
places.hook: Where hulls stop and porters start: hire a carry into the interior, or buy what has just come down it.

places.name: Hereguard Plantation
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 225 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.tempering-ground (+2.35).

why.founding: Canon's rice estate north of Lilmoth and one of the few places Bretons still live in Argonia; rice is the one crop that works here because it wants the flood.
why.siteAdvantages: A flooding river terrace that ruins any other crop and suits this one exactly.
why.occupantsMotive: A Breton family and Argonian tenant households, bound by a share arrangement that both sides describe differently.
why.pressures: Lilmoth depends on Hereguard rice, which gives the tenants more leverage every year and the family less.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tenant refusal at planting would starve the city, and everyone has done that arithmetic.

hardConstraints: controls a crossing or a landing
places.hook: Breton rice farmers who pay in coin and hire outsiders, which nobody else here does.

places.name: High Junction
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 30 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where four elevated walkways meet above the mangrove, a platform grew that is now a place in its own right.
why.siteAdvantages: The one point at which the whole upper network of this district connects, twelve metres above the water.
why.occupantsMotive: A tea-seller, a chime-relay peg board and a toll nobody formally imposes but everybody pays.
why.pressures: The junction's timbers carry more traffic than they were built for and everybody can feel it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would sever the district's upper network into four dead ends.

places.hook: Four walkways meet twelve metres up; whoever runs the deck decides which of them you may use.

places.name: Waits-For-A-Cutting
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 152 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Lilmoth has a Hist but no native tribe, and a fourth of the people who arrive here have no tree at all; the Fringe is where they end up.
why.siteAdvantages: Just outside the wall on ground the city does not tax and the villages will not claim.
why.occupantsMotive: Mutual aid without kinship — the households here are organised by arrival date, not by clan.
why.pressures: Hissmir is two provinces away in practical terms; most people here will never make the pilgrimage and know it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A city grant of tree-access would empty half of it in a month.

hardConstraints: wherever they were allowed to stop
places.hook: Everyone here has no tree and no claim; it is the only place in the south that asks you nothing.

places.name: Root-Sakka
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 673 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.insular-jungle-village (+0.45).

why.founding: A Murkmire village whose tree speaks clearly and often, which makes it the region's arbiter whether it wants to be or not.
why.siteAdvantages: A river terrace on the Keel-Sakka with deep root-water and a defensible bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Their tree-minder is consulted from three days' travel away, which is a burden the village debates constantly.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's tree does not speak to anyone but its minders; this one speaks to everybody, and the comparison is politically loaded.
why.wouldChangeIf: If their tree fell silent the region would lose its only uncontested voice.

hardConstraints: channel bank or spring, always with a landing
places.hook: The tree here answers plainly, so the whole river brings its arguments to this village.

places.name: Chuxeth
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 154 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.hammock-crown-murkmire (+0.73).

why.founding: A tribe that never left its xanmeer, and therefore holds the strongest fortification in southern Murkmire without having built anything.
why.siteAdvantages: Stone walls, a single water approach, and ancient defences that still work — in a region where everything else is timber.
why.occupantsMotive: They are polite, immovable, and entirely uninterested in Lilmoth's politics or the An-Xileel's.
why.pressures: Every faction in the south has wanted their walls at some point; the working defences are why none has taken them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the vakka mechanisms ever failed, the village would be ordinary overnight.

places.hook: A tribe holding a stone fort they never built; get inside and the whole district changes hands.

places.name: Xel-Nahkta
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 471 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.hist-village-keel-sakka (+0.45).

why.founding: A village in the jungle belt that has refused every outside contact since 4E 48 and enforces the refusal at the boundary.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise with one approach, three days from Lilmoth and unreachable by water.
why.occupantsMotive: They lost a village to something that came from outside and have drawn the obvious conclusion.
why.pressures: Their boundary now crosses a route the guides need, and the guides have started going around.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single successful parley would open the shortest route across the belt.

hardConstraints: defensible approach, often a single crossing
places.hook: They shoot at the boundary and always have; there is one thing inside worth the risk.

places.name: Ixtaxh Xanmeer
places.whySiteWon: islet in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 846 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The xanmeer the An-Xileel pumped out room by room and held dry with magicks; with them gone the magicks lapsed and the silt returned.
