why.siteAdvantages: Sits in standing water west of Lilmoth; only the topmost chamber stands above the silt, exactly as canon first found it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody tends it. Divers go in for what the An-Xileel left behind when the water came back fast.
why.pressures: The lower rooms are silt, not water — a diver can enter them and not find the way out.
why.wouldChangeIf: Another pumping effort would reopen it, and there is no faction left with the will or the singing to do it.

places.hook: The An-Xileel held this pumped dry with magic; the silt is back, and so is whatever they were after.

places.name: Keel-Sakka Landing
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 58 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The first village up the Keel-Sakka river from Lilmoth, where the rainforest road meets poling water.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm channel edge with deep water alongside, on the road out of Lilmoth's north gate.
why.occupantsMotive: They take Lilmoth's freight off the road and put it on the river, and charge for the change of medium.
why.pressures: Bright-Throat's chime-relay reaches here and Lilmoth's writ does not, which suits everyone locally.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cart road up the river would end the village's whole function.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
places.hook: The last supplied bed before the river turns to poling water; hire a boat or a poler here.

places.name: Black Fin Grove
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 862 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.ashroot-village (+0.50).

why.founding: A grove kept for Keshu the Black Fin, Murkmire's national hero — a hero-Hist grove is what a village does with a person it cannot let go of.
why.siteAdvantages: A stand of old Hist-kin trees on the ground where the story says she mustered, with a spring at the centre.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by rota from four villages, none of which will concede that the grove is any one of theirs.
why.pressures: The story has four incompatible versions and the rota is how the villages avoid resolving it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A definitive account would give the grove to one village and start a feud.

hardConstraints: spring or still water at the root
places.hook: Murkmire's hero mustered here; the grove keeps what she left, and the keeper decides who sees it.

places.name: Lighter Flotilla
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 6 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon: Lilmoth is built over shallow water and large ships cannot dock, so goods are lightered ashore — and the lighter crews live afloat, between the anchorage and the quay.
why.siteAdvantages: A permanent moored ground in the estuary, half a mile off the quay, out of the tariff line and inside the sheltered water.
why.occupantsMotive: The crews control the only link between deep-water hulls and the city, and they know precisely what that is worth.
why.pressures: A council attempt to license lightering triggered a two-week stoppage that nobody wants to repeat.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dredged deep-water channel would end both the flotilla and the city's leverage over its own trade.

hardConstraints: sheltered saltwater with a reef or bar
places.hook: The crews who move every cargo in the bay live out here, off the tariff and full of talk.

places.name: Lilmoth
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'lilmoth' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
why.siteAdvantages: The one firm shelf at the head of the estuary, with the stilt quarters and the lighter quay stepping down off it into tidal water; big hulls anchor out in Oliis Bay and lighter in, which is the whole economy.
why.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; nobody wants a ruler, and the last party that had one killed the city.
why.pressures: Politically hostile to the An-Xileel successor state; commercially essential to a bay that must trade somewhere; built over its own mass grave.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once — which is why the rules forbid it.

hardConstraints: on the firm shelf at the estuary head, its quays out over tidal water
places.hook: Everything sold in the south crosses this quay, and the city under the floorboards is still full.

places.name: Under-Yard
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 380 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.quinrawl-anchorage (+1.67).

why.founding: Lilmoth stands on a drowned city and salvage from underneath it is a licensed, taxed, entirely respectable trade.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay directly above the deepest of the sunken villas, with a stair down to a landing at water level.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews work the drowned quarter by permit, in pairs, and hand everything to the yard for valuation.
why.pressures: Some of what comes up belongs to families still living, and the yard has to decide that daily.
why.wouldChangeIf: A find of An-Xileel material would turn a trade into a political incident.

places.hook: Licensed diving into the drowned city: buy air, sell salvage, hear which villa is not yet stripped.

places.name: Long Bar
places.whySiteWon: headland in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 411 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A shoal bar off the salvage coast where a false light has been shown for longer than anyone will admit.
why.siteAdvantages: Two miles of breaking bar on the Southern Sea approach, with a beach behind it that no road overlooks and no village can see.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage families who decided that waiting for wrecks was inefficient; they take the low-profile Southern Sea traders nobody reports missing.
why.pressures: Khajiit crews keep the same lane and have begun to notice; the Soulrest harbour office would have to act if it were ever proved.
why.wouldChangeIf: A working lighthouse on the headland would end it in one season.

hardConstraints: no settlement in sight of the beach
places.hook: Someone has been showing a false light here for a century, and the beach is the proof.

places.name: Moonmarch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 368 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Khajiit moon-sugar landing on the Murkmire coast — the province gazetteer's only Khajiiti place-name, and it is here for a reason.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered landing far enough west of Lilmoth to be outside its tariff and close enough to sell into it.
why.occupantsMotive: Two families left of a dozen; the sugar still lands, in less of it and less often.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's rebuilt council taxes what Moonmarch used to handle untaxed; the trade has moved to Alten Meerhleel.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tariff rise at Lilmoth would refill Moonmarch in a season.

hardConstraints: a landing at the water’s edge, outside Lilmoth’s tariff line
places.hook: The province's one Khajiit landing: moon-sugar, Southern Sea rumour, and no questions about your cargo.

places.name: Mudfoot
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 170 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A fishing and cockle village on the Topal tidal flat, close enough to Soulrest to sell into it daily.
why.siteAdvantages: A tide that covers the cockle flat and uncovers it twice a day; stilts keep the floors dry and the flat is walkable at low water.
why.occupantsMotive: Sell fresh to the city, sell salted to the coast road, and never owe the council anything.
why.pressures: The city's price is set by buyers who all know each other; the village's answer is to sell early and low.
why.wouldChangeIf: A harbour road extension would turn it into a suburb.

hardConstraints: built over water at the highest seasonal level, piled to the bed
places.hook: Cockles, a dry floor and a walkable flat at low water; the cheapest bed on Topal Bay.

places.name: Xul-Hakka
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 142 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.keshu-grove (+0.78).

why.founding: A Naga village on the inner channels that raids the Lilmoth road in the dry season and trades with it in the wet.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep channel water on three sides, one poled approach, and reach to both the Lilmoth road and the estuary channels.
why.occupantsMotive: Raiding here is seasonal economics, not war; the same households trade with the people they robbed four months earlier.
why.pressures: Lilmoth's council has started paying for road escorts, which changes the arithmetic for the first time in a century.
why.wouldChangeIf: A permanent armed escort would force the village into either full trade or full war.

places.hook: Naga who raid the road in the dry season and trade on it in the wet; the season decides which.

places.name: Xul-Vaat
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 39 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village whose whole trade is the dead: staking, tending, reading and repatriating for the whole southern coast.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm peat that holds a stake, central to a dozen villages, and far enough from all of them.
why.occupantsMotive: Every household here holds a grave-office; children learn to read stakes before they learn anything else.
why.pressures: The Owing's dead, Umbriel's dead and White Rose's dead all arrive here eventually, and the ground is filling.
why.wouldChangeIf: A refusal to accept more dead would force a dozen villages to solve the problem themselves.

hardConstraints: soft ground that holds a stake, downwind of everyone
places.hook: The coast brings its dead here; the stake-carvers will read yours, for a price.

places.name: Breathing-Stone
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A maintained air chamber on the submerged route between the estuary and the inner channels — somebody built the bench in it.
why.siteAdvantages: Halfway along a flooded passage too long to swim in one breath, in a natural dome that holds air.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by the divers who use the route: a bench, a slate, a lamp bracket and a rule about leaving oil.
why.pressures: The air is finite and shared; the slate records who is currently below.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the chamber would close the route to everyone but the very best swimmers.

places.hook: A bench and a dry breath halfway along a swim no one can do in one lungful.

places.name: Walks-The-Mangrove
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A mangrove village that grew as a walkway first and a settlement second: the path came, then the houses hung off it.
why.siteAdvantages: A mangrove belt too soft to build on and too dense to boat through, where a raised deck is the only viable form.
why.occupantsMotive: Every household maintains its own span of deck, and the village's shape is the record of who has been diligent.
why.pressures: Three spans are failing and their households have left; the village is branching around the gaps rather than repairing them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A concerted repair would reconnect two halves that are drifting into separate villages.

hardConstraints: crosses water rather than sitting beside it
places.hook: A village that is really a two-mile walkway; it is the dry way through the mangrove.

places.name: The Drake Hole
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 392 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on danger, parent, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.sealed-meer-murkmire (+0.74).

why.founding: A drowned sinkhole in the bay floor, forty metres deep and occupied by something the fishers will not name at sea.
why.siteAdvantages: The one deep hole in an otherwise shallow bay: cold, dark and permanent.
why.occupantsMotive: The occupant. The fishers work around it in a circle you can see on any chart of their nets.
why.pressures: The hole is directly on the natural lighterage line and every hull crosses it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing anybody here is willing to attempt.

places.hook: Forty metres down in the bay floor is a hole the fishers will not name, and it is occupied.

places.name: Estuary Stage
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 28 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The estuary is half a mile wide at the road crossing and the ferry is older than the rebuilt city.
why.siteAdvantages: A narrows with hard landings on both sides and slack water twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: A council concession, farmed out annually to the highest bidder, which explains the fare.
why.pressures: The fare rises every year and the boats do not improve.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rival free crossing upstream would break the concession and the council's revenue with it.

hardConstraints: at a water narrows the coast road must cross
places.hook: The only way across the estuary without a two-day walk, and the ferry holders know it.

places.name: The Cut Reef
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 39 m from the nearest route; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A reef harvested for lime, lacquer shell and building aggregate rather than for pearl — Lilmoth's stilts need footings.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow enough to work by free-diving, close enough to barge the take straight to the city.
why.occupantsMotive: Cutters take by permit from the council, which is the only harvest in the bay anyone actually licenses.
why.pressures: The reef is visibly smaller than it was in living memory and the permit count has not fallen.
why.wouldChangeIf: Closing it would raise the cost of every new platform in Lilmoth.

hardConstraints: clear water over a worked bed
places.hook: Lilmoth's stilts stand on lime cut from this reef, and the cutters are always short of divers.

places.name: Xal-Meht
places.whySiteWon: flood high in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 20 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A xanmeer with no surviving clan, tended instead by the pilgrims who pass it on the way to the Teeth of Sithis.
why.siteAdvantages: On the pilgrim line, with a spring at its foot — the reason the route goes this way at all.
why.occupantsMotive: Maintenance as devotion: each party clears one terrace and moves on.
why.pressures: Pilgrim tending is uneven and sentimental; the terraces nobody likes are being lost.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rerouted pilgrimage would leave it to the forest within thirty years.

places.hook: A xanmeer with no clan left, kept open by the pilgrims who pass it; the lower rooms are not kept.

places.name: Quin'rawl Anchorage
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 2), 55 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, hinterland, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.lilmoth-divers-yard (+1.67).

why.founding: Southern Sea crews — a large share of them Khajiit — keep a low profile to avoid Altmer and Maormer warships, so they anchor where no state looks.
why.siteAdvantages: A deep cove behind a headland with two exits, sand holding ground and a freshwater run at its head.
why.occupantsMotive: Half the hulls here carry a Soulrest charter, and all of them carry cargo the charter does not mention.
why.pressures: Soulrest's council both licenses and disowns them, which is a stable arrangement everyone resents.
why.wouldChangeIf: A Dominion sweep of the Southern Sea would scatter it to the mangroves in a week.

hardConstraints: a deep cove on open salt water behind a headland
places.hook: Crews who hide from two navies anchor here; they will trade, and they will not be followed.

places.name: Rockpark
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 167 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.white-rose-prison (+0.69).

why.founding: Canon empties Rockpark of every business and guild through pestilence, plague and a curse; nobody returned because its Hist died.
why.siteAdvantages: Good firm ground on the north-east road out of Lilmoth — which is why its emptiness is so conspicuous.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Unearthed Equipment Store still blocks the palace gate and the palace still holds what the royal family became.
why.pressures: It is a day's walk from a living city and stocked with five centuries of untouched goods, and still nobody goes in.
why.wouldChangeIf: A confirmed cure for whatever is in the palace would strip the town in a week.

places.hook: Canon says plague emptied it and nobody came back; the houses were left with everything in them.

places.name: Under-Root
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 420 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on landform, remote, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A walkable gallery under a great root mass, dry above the flood, and occupied by people who wanted somewhere no one would look.
why.siteAdvantages: Two hundred metres of natural passage with three entrances and a permanent air flow.
why.occupantsMotive: Whoever is currently in it — the tenancy changes and the fittings do not.
why.pressures: The gallery floods to chest height in the deep wet season, on about a week's notice.
why.wouldChangeIf: A root collapse would close the middle and split it into two dead ends.

hardConstraints: water at the gallery's low points; some branches fully flooded
places.hook: Two hundred metres of dry passage under the roots, and the people using it chose it for that.

places.name: Customs Suburb
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Imperial customs suburb outside Lilmoth's north gate, looted by the An-Xileel when they took the city from the Empire.
why.siteAdvantages: Astride the north road where every cargo had to pass, which is why it was built and why it was sacked.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody rebuilt it; Lilmoth's rebuilt council collects at the quay instead and prefers not to be reminded.
why.pressures: Its record room survived the fire and nobody has read it in two centuries.
why.wouldChangeIf: The records would establish who owned what before 4E 48, which several families would prefer stayed unknown.

hardConstraints: in a port or a city
places.hook: The Empire's customs quarter, looted in a night and never cleared; the cellars are still sealed.

places.name: Screen-Watch
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in tidal delta (danger band 3), 275 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village of the people who pilot Bramman's river, built inside the mangrove wall a mile above its mouth.
why.siteAdvantages: Invisible from the bay; every house sits on the channel it watches; the mangrove is both wall and roof.
why.occupantsMotive: Piloting fees, and a strict internal rule that no two families ever teach the same reach of the river.
why.pressures: Blackguards want the river as a road, Soulrest wants it as a customs problem, and the village wants it to stay a rumour.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the channel were ever charted publicly the village would have no reason to exist.

places.hook: The pilots who know Bramman's river live in here, and they are the only ones who do.

places.name: Shut-From-Within
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 538 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.oliis-drake-deep (+0.74).

why.founding: Sealed by its own people when its Hist chamber was emptied, so that whatever remains inside stays inside.
why.siteAdvantages: A low xanmeer on a rise, unremarkable except that its door was closed from within.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing tends it. Its traps are intact and its Hist chamber is not empty in the way the sealers believed.
why.pressures: Two villages disagree about which of them did the sealing, and therefore about who may open it.
why.wouldChangeIf: An agreement between the two villages would open it legitimately for the first time in centuries.

places.hook: It was shut from the inside. The mechanisms still work, which is the problem.

places.name: The Slaughter Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 50 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where Lilmoth buried the dead of 4E 48 — its own residents, killed first, by their own city's tree and its party.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the rebuilt wall on the only firm ground large enough, because inside the wall is the mass grave the city stands on.
why.occupantsMotive: A rotating vigil, maintained by the same rule as the tree-minders': never one faction, never one person.
why.pressures: The An-Xileel successor state denies the causation; Lilmoth's whole civic identity depends on it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A reconciliation with the successor state would require abandoning the inscription, and it will not happen.

places.hook: Lilmoth's own dead of 4E 48, and the city would rather you did not read the stones.

places.name: Soulrest
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'soulrest' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Third-Era provincial capital at the one sheltered deep-water landfall where Topal Bay meets the Southern Sea.
why.siteAdvantages: Peninsula wrapping the bay; a river mouth just south opening a route north-east into the interior; islands screening the approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Four powers hold pieces of it: a merchant council, an orphaned Imperial apparatus, interior tribes, and the river interests who control Bramman's water.
why.pressures: Its gold-and-timber hinterland was burned by the tribes in 3E 427 and never rebuilt; the capital moved; the offices remain, administering nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the mines reopened, or if one of the four claimants finally won, the city would stop being a stalemate and start being a capital again.

hardConstraints: bay port at a concealed river's mouth
places.hook: The old capital still keeps the province's best harbour, and three factions are quietly arguing over who owns it.

places.name: Breaking Hard
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in tidal delta (danger band 2), 110 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on bound, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Where the Expeditionary Force's transports were cut up for their iron when the Empire stopped paying for them.
why.siteAdvantages: A hard shingle slope inside the mole with deep water at its foot — the only place on the coast a hull can be laid over.
why.occupantsMotive: Breakers who make more from Imperial fastenings than any local trade makes from anything.
why.pressures: The supply of Imperial hulls is finite and nearly finished; the yard has started buying wrecks off the Long Bar and asking nothing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Soulrest ever built ships again, the same slope would serve.

places.hook: Hulls are cut up here for iron; anything off a ship can be bought, and some of it is not scrap.

places.name: Long Table
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 25 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The quayside house where cargo is contracted, crews are hired and the council's tariffs are argued about.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay, between the harbour office and the divers' yard.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper sells information at the same table as beer and considers both a single trade.
why.pressures: Everyone who matters in the port drinks here, which makes it the least private room in the city.
why.wouldChangeIf: A council monopoly on brokerage would empty it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing
places.hook: Contracts, crews and the tariff argument: whatever is happening on this coast is said here first.

places.name: Ganthil's Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 641 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Umbriel passed over this village on its way from Lilmoth in 4E 48 and took everyone in it; what stood up afterwards is still standing.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly under the recorded track of the shadow, on ground that was good enough to hold a village and is now avoided entirely.
why.occupantsMotive: The dead here do not leave the village bounds, which is the only reason it is not a regional catastrophe.
why.pressures: It sits between two working villages and forces every journey between them to take an extra half-day.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would restore a road that has been broken for a hundred and fifty years.

places.hook: Umbriel took everyone here in a night; the houses stand, furnished, with the doors shut.

places.name: Sunkfoot
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 82 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A shore hamlet that subsided when the salt pans changed the drainage behind it; the sea came in over a decade.
why.siteAdvantages: It had firm ground once. It does not now, and that is the whole story.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty at low water; the grave-stakes were moved but not all of them.
why.pressures: The pan-holders have never accepted that the pans did it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing brings it back; a second subsidence would take the pans too.

places.hook: A whole hamlet went under in a decade, and the roofs are still on it.

places.name: Teeba-Enoo Court
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 1), 39 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon: the tribes tolerate Alten Meerhleel because of its Teeba-Enoo court — the ball game is the price the port pays for existing.
why.siteAdvantages: A floored court on the landward margin of the port, where tribal parties can come without entering the trading water.
why.occupantsMotive: The port fields a team and loses politely; the tribes take the result seriously and the trade continues.
why.pressures: A port team that won convincingly would create a diplomatic problem nobody wants.
why.wouldChangeIf: Ending the games would end the tolerance, and the port knows exactly what that costs.

places.hook: The ball game the port pays to keep the tribes friendly; win a place on a side and doors open.

places.name: The Teeth of Sithis
places.whySiteWon: summit in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 593 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's largest Sithis temple in Murkmire, tended by the Clutch of Nisswo though it no longer serves its original purpose.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep in the marsh at the end of a pilgrim route, with a natural rock formation the temple was built to frame.
why.occupantsMotive: The Clutch maintain it precisely and preach that its loss of purpose is the sermon.
why.pressures: Nobody can now say what the original purpose was, and at least one faction claims to have found out.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rediscovery of the temple's function would split the Clutch.

places.hook: The largest Sithis temple in Murkmire, and the Nisswo will take an outsider in if you bring the right thing.

places.name: Tempers-The-Young
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 88 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, hinterland, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.hereguard-plantation (+2.35).

why.founding: Canon: in Lilmoth people look to their elders, including retired Shadowscales — and retired Shadowscales trained somewhere.
why.siteAdvantages: An enclosed water-and-root ground an hour outside the city, with three approaches and no sightline into it.
why.occupantsMotive: Two retired scales still keep the ground and still take the occasional sign-born child, which is now illegal in every sense.
why.pressures: The Cheydinhal succession wants the tradition back; Lilmoth's council would rather it did not exist near their walls.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single public execution of a trainee here would force the council to act.

places.hook: Retired Shadowscales train here, and they are the only people in the south who will teach you this.

places.name: White Fields
places.whySiteWon: natural harbour in ocean (danger band 0), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Salt is the one export the burning of the mines did not touch, and the bay's shore evaporates well.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide, gently shelving salt-marsh shore with a dry season long enough to crystallise.
why.occupantsMotive: Pan-holders who pay Soulrest a share and sell the rest to fish-curers along the whole south coast.
why.pressures: A wet-season overtop ruins a year; the sea walls are rebuilt by owed labour every spring.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Owing gangs stopped coming, the pans would silt in three years.

hardConstraints: tidal salt water, sun and wind
places.hook: Salt is the one export the burn did not touch; the salters buy labour and sell in bulk.

places.name: The Villa Cellars
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 31 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'any-shallow-marsh' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, submerged, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Imperial villas outside the rebuilt wall sank with their cellars intact, and the cellars are connected.
why.siteAdvantages: A continuous flooded undercroft running two hundred metres, entered from three collapsed floors.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvage crews work the near end under permit; the far end is beyond the permit line and not empty.
why.pressures: The passage is head-height, silt-floored and disorients completely; there is no natural light after the second room.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse at the middle would cut the far cellars off for good.

places.hook: Two hundred metres of connected Imperial cellars under the water, and the divers have not reached the end.

places.name: White Rose Prison
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 4), 71 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.mercantile-coast.rockpark (+0.69).

why.founding: One of the prisons canon says the Empire built after 1E 2837, sited by the Imperial rule for this province: put it where the marsh is the wall. It stands off the Bogmother causeway, the road the Legion already had.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground with marsh water on every side and one causeway in, a short haul from the Bogmother road that brought the convicts and took the ore out.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty of the living. Full of Argonian dead who died away from their Hist and whose bones were never brought to the dirt.
why.pressures: The Blackrose Chainbreakers want the dead repatriated; the structure is sound enough that somebody will eventually want it back.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reoccupation by any armed party would make the repatriation impossible and the grievance permanent.

hardConstraints: firm ground ringed by marsh water, one causeway in
within 400 m of the Bogmother causeway
places.hook: An Imperial prison the marsh sealed; the cordon cellars below it were never emptied.

places.name: Whitebone Reef
places.whySiteWon: cove in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 202 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The bar that made the salvage economy: a coral and shell reef lying a foot under at high water across the bay mouth.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly on the natural sailing line into Topal Bay, which is exactly the problem.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives here but the reef; three centuries of hulls do.
why.pressures: Silt from the burn-country rivers is killing the living head and turning it to rubble, which makes it more dangerous, not less.
why.wouldChangeIf: A lit mark on the headland would render it merely scenery.

places.hook: The reef that made the salvage trade: a foot under at high water, with the wrecks still on it.

places.name: The Wraxu Frieze
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 204 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Sithite work-and-unmake ground where the local xanmeer carvings of the extinct wraxu are copied in clay and destroyed each year.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered clay bank under a xanmeer face that carries the original wraxu etchings canon records here.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo and their students make an exact copy of the frieze, exhibit it for one night, and break it before dawn.
why.pressures: Outsiders keep trying to buy the copy; the Clutch keeps having to explain that the destruction is the work.
why.wouldChangeIf: A copy surviving a year would be a theological crisis, and someone is trying to arrange one.

places.hook: The Sithites copy the extinct birds in clay each year and break them; the original carving is underneath.

places.name: Wraxu Stacks
places.whySiteWon: islet in fringe marsh (danger band 2), 44 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Named for the extinct wraxu birds whose colonies canon puts on this coast; the birds that nest here now are not them.
why.siteAdvantages: Vertical sea stacks off the islands, unclimbable from three sides, thick with guano and eggs.
why.occupantsMotive: Egg-takers come twice a year by rope and take the ledges in a fixed order.
why.pressures: Everyone here knows what happened to the wraxu, and the taking rules are stricter than any law Soulrest ever wrote.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single greedy season would be remembered for a century.

hardConstraints: sea stacks standing out of salt water
places.hook: Egg-takers climb these stacks for a living; there is a sea cave at the base nobody works.

places.name: Xinchei-Konu Monument
places.whySiteWon: summit in firm lowland (danger band 2), 377 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's ancient calendar in the lowlands east of Lilmoth, with a hereditary keeper — a jekka-wass — and a function: it is called a catalyst of change and can alter the weather.
why.siteAdvantages: An open lowland with a clean southern horizon, because the instrument needs one.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper's whole office is not to use it, and to explain that to everyone who arrives wanting it used.
why.pressures: Every party with a weather problem eventually comes here; the keeper has refused emperors' agents and antiquarians alike.
why.wouldChangeIf: A successful use would be the largest single event in the province's recent history, which is the argument for and against.

places.hook: A working ancient calendar with a hereditary keeper, and canon says it can turn the weather.

places.name: The Poler's Breath
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 218 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A maintained air pocket on the flooded shortcut under the narrows.
why.siteAdvantages: The midpoint of a dive that cannot be made on one breath.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; maintained by the guides who use it. The guides keep it because a pocket nobody maintains is a pocket that drowns the guild's next apprentice, so the upkeep is charged into every crossing fee whether the client uses the pocket or not.
why.pressures: Silt is filling the pocket from below. Two guiding families disagree about who is responsible for clearing it, and each has spent a decade waiting for the other to admit the duty.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its loss would close the shortcut and add two hours to every crossing. Its loss would also break the guides' price against the portage crews, who would take the traffic within a season.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
water at least 6 m deep within 100 m
places.hook: Half way through a dive nobody survives on one breath, there is a room full of air, and the guides charge you for it whether you use it or not.

places.name: The Unmaking Yard
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 395 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A ground where Nisswo commission works of art and destroy them as the sermon.
why.siteAdvantages: A clearing above the flood with one landing, so patrons can attend, watch a work destroyed, and leave the same night.
why.occupantsMotive: A resident maker and a rotating congregation. The maker is paid to make well and then watch it burn; the fee is for the making, and a maker who flinches at the destruction is not commissioned again.
why.pressures: Foreign collectors have begun buying the works before the destruction, which is heresy and lucrative. The buyers pay in coastal coin the congregation has learned to want, so the heresy is funding the rite that condemns it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single sale being made public would split the congregation. A split would put a second, tolerant unmaking-yard on the coast within a year, and this one would become the strict house by contrast.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
places.hook: The Nisswo pay for beautiful things and then break them in front of you, and they will let you commission one.

places.name: Teeth-Pens
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 216 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that keeps crocodiles — for hide, for meat, and because a penned ring of them is the cheapest wall in the swamp.
why.siteAdvantages: A creek that can be gated at both ends to make the pens.
why.occupantsMotive: Keepers whose stock is also their defence. Keeping is hereditary because the stock knows its keepers by scent, and a village that sold its line of keepers would have to kill its wall and start again.
why.pressures: The pens have failed twice and the village rebuilt them larger. Larger pens need more meat than the creek yields, so the village now buys fish it used to sell, and the wall is quietly eating the economy it protects.
why.wouldChangeIf: A pen failure in the wet season would be catastrophic. A wet-season failure would not just cost the herd: the loose stock would take the surrounding reaches for a decade and cut the village off from its own landings.

places.hook: You cross a bridge over hungry stock to reach the houses, and the same stock is why nothing has ever raided this village.

places.name: Since-The-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in seasonal floodplain (danger band 4), 449 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, ring; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village whose Hist was killed during the Umbriel passage and which has stayed put ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: Their ground is good and their reason for staying is that leaving would be a second death. Their ground also carries the stump, which is a relic and a grave and the only thing they own that no neighbour will contest.
why.occupantsMotive: People with no hatching, no naming and no soul-return, keeping a village going anyway.
why.pressures: Their young are Hist-less by birth — a whole generation the province has no category for. The neighbouring tribes will trade with them and will not marry them, so each generation is smaller than the last while the village itself is unchanged.
why.wouldChangeIf: Adoption by a neighbouring tree would dissolve them into someone else's tribe, which they have refused twice. A hero Hist consenting to hatch their young without taking their name would solve it, and no tree has ever been asked to do that.

places.hook: Their tree was killed under Umbriel and they made the stump into the table they eat off, and they will sit you at it.

places.name: Nine-Stakes Field
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 93 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A grave-stake field that rose after a flood disturbed it, not after a theft.
why.siteAdvantages: Low ground beside a channel that changed course.
why.occupantsMotive: Blights that were not raised by anyone's fault. Because no theft raised them, the risen have no wrongdoer to blame, which in local law makes them the whole village's debt rather than one family's.
why.pressures: The village that owns the field cannot afford to restake it and cannot afford not to. The stake-setters price by the night and the village pays in rice, and the two rates have drifted so far apart that the work has stopped mid-field.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking would settle it; the labour is the obstacle, not the danger. Restaking would settle it; the labour is the obstacle, not the danger, and any outsider who supplies the labour buys a permanent claim on the village.

places.hook: The stakes are all still standing and correct; the water carried the dead out from under them, and there is no rite for that.

places.name: The Old Cordon
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 255 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.naga-village-settled (+1.97).

why.founding: A plague cordon's burial line that was never staked at all, because the buriers were foreign.
why.siteAdvantages: The line of an Imperial-era cordon across the zone's neck.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever a century of unstaked burial produces. Nobody inherits the duty because nobody inherited the burial: the Legion dug the line, the Legion left, and the ground has been legally ownerless since.
why.pressures: The route the cordon guarded is the route people still use. The route the cordon guarded is the route people still use, and each generation's accidents are blamed on the last generation's cowardice.
why.wouldChangeIf: Staking the line would take a season and end a century of accidents. Staking the line would take a season and end a century of accidents — and would also settle, publicly, that the plague dead here were Argonian and not Kothringi.

places.hook: A dead-straight Imperial burial trench cut across two kilometres of swamp, dug deep, dug wrong, and open at both ends.

places.name: The Carriers' Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 143 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.poacher-camp-egg (+0.43).

why.founding: A seasonal camp of bone-carriers gathering the zone's distant dead for the walk inland.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the poling routes converge and the walking route inland begins; the last point a laden carrier can be resupplied by boat.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers, in season. Carrying is a debt-work: most carriers are repaying a family's unreturned dead rather than earning, which is why the season is worked to exhaustion.
why.pressures: The Umbriel-era backlog reaches this camp too, and it is visible in the stacks. The Umbriel-era backlog reaches this camp too, and it is visible in the stacks — bundles labelled for villages that no longer exist and cannot receive them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A carriers' strike would leave a season's dead unreturned.

places.hook: They are waiting to carry the dead inland, and the oldest bundle in the stack has been rewrapped so many times it is mostly wrapping.

places.name: Dead-Water Village
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 633 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.voriplasm-chamber-breached (+2.22).

why.founding: The Naga-Kur's seat: the tribe built for surviving the worst thing in the swamp, around the tree that made them.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise in the inner swamps with black water on every side and one poling approach. The single poling approach is also the tribe's toll: nothing reaches the inner swamp's eastern reaches without being counted here first.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe whose whole discipline — grave rite, watch, blight-craft — is organised around the dead not staying down.
why.pressures: Umbriel's legacy is exactly their enemy, and they have not stopped preparing; their kin on the roads are tribeless and their reputation suffers for it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the blight pressure stopped, the tribe would have no reason for the discipline that defines it. If the blight pressure stopped, the tribe would have no reason for the discipline that defines it — and the stake-setters, the night necropolis and three subordinate villages would lose their trade with it.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
black standing water on three sides, one poling approach
places.hook: The Naga-Kur seat, under the one Hist in the province that flowers blue, and nothing goes east without being counted here first.

places.name: Deepmire, the Refuge
places.whySiteWon: flood high in interior swamp (danger band 4), 568 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon's shelter of last resort: an all-but-inaccessible plateau in the north-north-east that even the tribes avoid, where the presence of Sithis is said to be strong, holding pre-Duskfall xanmeers and the skeletons of swamp leviathans. It is not to be visited except to shelter, and it is tended by a caretaker few.
why.siteAdvantages: High, dry, defensible ground in a province that has almost none, with one approach that can be walked and no approach that can be poled.
why.occupantsMotive: The caretakers do not live here so much as keep it fit to be lived in — stores turned, shelters re-roofed, the memorial swept — against a need they hope never comes.
why.pressures: In 4E 48 the need did come: Murkmire's survivors fled up onto the plateau while Umbriel passed overhead, and the caretakers have been feeding that memory ever since. The Umbriel Witness Society wants the memorial catalogued, the Nisswo want it let go, and the caretakers want it left exactly as it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the argument over the memorial is settled by anyone but the caretakers, the plateau stops being a refuge and becomes a destination — which is the one thing its whole custom exists to prevent.

hardConstraints: upland ground above the flood by 40m+
places.hook: The last dry ground in the province, kept ready for a night that has not come again; you may shelter here and you may not stay.

places.name: The Chimney
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 4), 380 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on region, submerged, landform; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A natural shaft from the swamp floor into the root layer.
why.siteAdvantages: Where a root gallery's roof gave way under standing water, deep in the swamp and a long way from anywhere.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever uses a vertical connection between two systems. Whatever uses a vertical connection between two systems uses it in both directions, which is why the villages date their worst years by what came up it.
why.pressures: Divers use it as a shortcut and it does not always let them back. Divers use it as a shortcut and it does not always let them back; the guides charge double to name it and will not enter it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would seal the connection. A collapse would seal the connection and add half a day to every stake-field circuit on this side of the zone.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
standing water at least 8 m deep at the mouth
places.hook: A silt plume rises out of the swamp floor for no visible reason, and it is the only way down into the root layer from here.

places.name: The Moving Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 361 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village on rafts that moves with the season, because in the inner swamp no ground is reliable for a decade.
why.siteAdvantages: Whichever mooring the year requires; the village site is a route, not a point, and the moorings are chosen for what is spawning rather than for what is safe.
why.occupantsMotive: People who own no land and consider that a strength.
why.pressures: Every fixed village disputes their fishing and their claim to anything. Every fixed village disputes their fishing and their claim to anything, and the settled Naga have begun charging them for water they used to take freely.
why.wouldChangeIf: A land grant would end the practice and probably the culture. A land grant would end the practice and probably the culture, and the tribes that want them settled want it precisely for that reason.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
sited as a mooring SET (3-4 alternates), not a point — quests 20 fixed-alternative-mooring pattern
places.hook: It is never where the last traveller said it was, and you find three empty moorings before you find the village.

places.name: Under-Piles
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.raft-village-lashed (+0.79).

why.founding: A stilt village drowned when the channel changed and the water rose two metres in a season.
why.siteAdvantages: It was correctly sited for the water level of the time, which is the standing local argument against building on any firm-looking flat.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; fish, and salvage divers.
why.pressures: The families who left are three villages away and still claim the goods in it. The families who left are three villages away and still claim the goods in it, and have hired divers twice rather than let the dredgers take it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A drawdown would expose it and start a legal fight. A drawdown would expose it and start a legal fight that three villages have quietly agreed to hope never happens.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
standing water at least 4 m deep over the roofs
places.hook: The houses are still furnished under the water, because the rise was slow enough to walk away from and too slow to carry anything.

places.name: The Gate Narrows
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 8 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.necropolis-nightbound (+0.80).

why.founding: A flood-pulse pinch in deep marsh where the whole zone's outflow squeezes through in the hours after rain.
why.siteAdvantages: The single outlet of the inner swamp, held between two root walls rather than rock.
why.occupantsMotive: None; a timing post is kept by the nearest village. The timing post is manned by whichever village most recently lost a boat, a rota that guarantees the keeper takes it seriously and never lasts.
why.pressures: Boats that mistime it are lost, and the village profits from salvage, so the gauge post has never been improved and the drawdown timings are memorised rather than written.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cut second channel would end both the danger and the salvage income. A cut second channel would end both the danger and the salvage income, which is why the village has twice blocked the survey.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
places.hook: A painted gauge post tells you how long the window is, and a salvage board beside it lists what the last mistiming produced.

places.name: The Hire Stage
places.whySiteWon: island in interior swamp (danger band 2), 151 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The stage where outsiders hire a poler, because the inner swamp cannot be navigated without one.
why.siteAdvantages: The last point reachable without local knowledge.
why.occupantsMotive: Polers, a broker, and a price list that is not the real price list. The broker is not a poler and takes a cut of every hire, which the polers resent and tolerate because he is the one who deals with foreigners.
why.pressures: Unguided travellers go in anyway and their craft come back empty. Unguided travellers go in anyway and their craft come back empty, and each such loss is used to justify the next rise in the hire price.
why.wouldChangeIf: A published chart would destroy the trade, which is why none exists. A published chart would destroy the trade, which is why none exists — and why the two surveyors who tried were poled home very slowly.

hardConstraints: the last landing reachable without a local poler
places.hook: Past this landing you do not go without a poler, and the wall of recovered boat-nameplates is the argument.

places.name: The Sunk Corridor
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 516 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, remote, submerged; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A xanmeer service corridor now full to the ceiling.
why.siteAdvantages: It connects two parts of a ruin that are otherwise a day apart. It connects two parts of a ruin that are otherwise a day apart, and the far half is the half the looters never reached.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing. Nothing lives in it; the silt is undisturbed, which is how the divers know nobody has been through in years.
why.pressures: It is the only connection and it is a hundred metres long.
why.wouldChangeIf: A drawdown year makes it walkable and everyone waits for one. A drawdown year makes it walkable and everyone waits for one — including the tending clan, who intend to be first through and have said so.

places.hook: A hundred metres of dead straight flooded corridor with the far end a coin of light, and the far half is the half the looters never reached.

places.name: The Polers' Camp
places.whySiteWon: islet in interior swamp (danger band 4), 72 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A night camp for poling guides crossing the inner swamp.
why.siteAdvantages: The one rise at the midpoint of the longest crossing, high enough to sleep on and small enough to defend.
why.occupantsMotive: Guides and their clients, overnight only. Guides sleep between their clients and the water, a courtesy that is also a guard against clients who decide at midnight that they can find their own way.
why.pressures: The rise is small and the crossings have got busier. The rise is small and the crossings have got busier, so arrival order now decides who sleeps dry, and the older guides arrive early on principle.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second rise would have to be built, and building it is a project nobody owns. A second rise would have to be built, and building it is a project nobody owns — the guides are rivals, and no village claims ground this far out.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
the one rise on the longest crossing
places.hook: Lamps at water level on the only high ground you have seen all day, and a strict arrival order the guides enforce on each other.

places.name: The Held Tree
places.whySiteWon: flood high in interior swamp (danger band 4), 151 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, route; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Hist held by a crew who feed it, tend it, and will not let its tribe near it.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise with sixty metres of black water between the tree and the tribe that owns it, and only one landing on the crew's side.
why.occupantsMotive: Occupiers who claim they are protecting it and may believe it. They tap it, and what they draw is worth more than anything else in the zone, which is the part of the protection story they do not tell.
why.pressures: The tribe camps within sight and has done for eleven years. The tribe camps within sight and has done for eleven years, feeding a standoff that the surrounding villages now depend on: while it holds, nobody else can claim the holding.
why.wouldChangeIf: Either party breaking the standoff resolves it violently. Either party breaking the standoff resolves it violently, and the tree itself is the likeliest casualty of the resolution.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
on a channel bank with a village on the opposite bank
places.hook: A crew has taken a tribe's Hist and feeds it well, and the tribe is camped in sight of their own empty houses.

places.name: The Horwalli Cut
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 51 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'confluence' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.umbriel-stripped-undead (+1.51).

why.founding: Waterworks built by a vanished people who managed this swamp instead of living with it.
why.siteAdvantages: The zone's natural drainage pinch, where two channels are close enough that cut stone could join them and pay for itself.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the works run themselves, badly. Nobody; the works run themselves, badly, and the villages downstream have built their calendars around its faults rather than its intent.
why.pressures: The half-working sluices still divert water, and two modern villages flood because of a decision made by a dead civilisation. The half-working sluices still divert water, and two modern villages flood because of a decision made by a dead civilisation — which each village blames on the other's failure to clear its own channel.
why.wouldChangeIf: Repairing or breaking the works would redraw the zone's hydrology. Repairing or breaking the works would redraw the zone's hydrology, making one village's rice ground and drowning another's, so any repair is a political act before it is an engineering one.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
places.hook: Sluices that still open and close on the season, unattended, and the villages downstream have organised their year around a machine nobody understands.

places.name: The Feather Deep
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 609 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'box-canyon' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.naga-village-raiding (+2.05).

why.founding: The deepest hole in the inner swamps, named in the tribes' recitation and entered by nobody.
why.siteAdvantages: A drowned sinkhole in the swamp floor, far deeper than anything around it. A drowned sinkhole in the swamp floor, far deeper than anything around it — the only place in the zone where the root layer does not close overhead.
why.occupantsMotive: Something the recitation names and does not describe. Something the recitation names and does not describe, and the omission is deliberate: the naming tribes hold that describing it is an invitation.
why.pressures: Divers who go for the treasure at the lip do not go past it. Divers who go for the treasure at the lip do not go past it, and the lip has been picked over often enough that the good salvage now starts below the point where people stop.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
standing water at least 20 m deep — the deepest hole in the zone
places.hook: A disc of true black in olive water, named in the tribes' recitation and entered by nobody.

places.name: The Nine Ribs
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 143 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Canon says swamp-leviathan skeletons litter Deepmire; this is the largest of them, and a bone-and-hide works grew up beside it because the material is free, enormous and already dead.
why.siteAdvantages: Beached in shallow water at a channel bend, so the carcass could be worked from boats and the ribs stayed standing while the rest went.
why.occupantsMotive: A handful of bone-cutters and one family living inside the rib cage, who regard the arrangement as ordinary.
why.pressures: The cause of death is still legible in the skull, and it was not old age; whatever did it has not been seen since, which the neighbours find less reassuring than the cutters do.
why.wouldChangeIf: The bone runs out in a generation, and the works has already started arguing about the second skeleton downstream.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
shallow water a hull can work from
standing ribs that break the canopy line
places.hook: A house built inside the rib cage with the ribs left uncut, and everything under the carcass has moved in with it.

places.name: The Kaju Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 645 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.sealed-xanmeer-vakka-deeps (+1.20).

why.founding: The trial by which the deep-swamp young take an adult name: a kill, alone, in water.
why.siteAdvantages: A reach that reliably holds the right animal. A reach that reliably holds the right animal, and shallow enough at the margins that the families can watch without being able to help.
why.occupantsMotive: Trial-keepers and, in season, the candidates' families waiting at the bank.
why.pressures: The animal population is down and the trial is getting harder, which some read as a judgement. The animal population is down and the trial is getting harder, which some read as a judgement, and which has already pushed two families to send their young to the coastal trials instead.
why.wouldChangeIf: A failed season would force a change to a rite nobody wants to change. A failed season would force a change to a rite nobody wants to change, and the deep-swamp tribes would rather import animals than admit the reach is finished.

places.hook: Take an adult name the way the deep swamp does: one kill, alone, in the water, with the families watching from the shallows.

places.name: The Open Ward
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 335 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A miregaunt standing in open water with nothing behind it to guard.
why.siteAdvantages: Open shallow water on no route to anywhere. Open shallow water on no route to anywhere — which is itself the evidence, because a ward implies the route existed once.
why.occupantsMotive: One miregaunt, guarding nothing anybody can find.
why.pressures: Its presence implies something here worth guarding, and nobody has found it. Its presence implies something here worth guarding, and nobody has found it; the standing theory is that the ward outlived a Horwalli work now under the silt.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing. It returns. Nothing. It returns — and it returns to the same stance and the same bearing, which is the detail scholars pay for.

places.hook: It has been guarding a patch of open water since before the villages existed, and under the water there is a way down to what it is guarding.

places.name: The North Cut Camp
places.whySiteWon: ford in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 8 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A tribeless Naga camp working the northern poling route.
why.siteAdvantages: A blind bend where craft must slow.
why.occupantsMotive: Tribeless Naga who take cargo and rarely lives. Tribeless Naga who take cargo and rarely lives, on the calculation that a robbed poler comes back next season and a dead one brings his tribe.
why.pressures: The settled tribes are blamed for them, which suits nobody. The settled tribes are blamed for them, which suits nobody, and the settled hold has begun paying the camp not to work its stretch — a fact that would ruin it if known.
why.wouldChangeIf: A settlement between settled and tribeless would end the camp. A settlement between settled and tribeless would end the camp, and the province's toll rates would fall with it.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
on a blind bend of a poling route
places.hook: A rope across the channel at chest height, and a scratched tally-stick receipt for whatever they take off you.

places.name: The Reed Gate Camp
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 69 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.raft-village-lashed (+1.26).

why.founding: A second camp working the southern route, run by a group that has fallen out with the northern one.
why.siteAdvantages: A reed narrows with two exits. A reed narrows with two exits, so a boat that flees one exit is met at the other; the crew's whole method is the geometry.
why.occupantsMotive: A crew who are worse than their northern rivals and know it.
why.pressures: The two camps are raiding each other's takings. The two camps are raiding each other's takings, and the southern crew has started killing where the northern would not, which is losing them the route's silence.
why.wouldChangeIf: A merger or a war would resolve it. A merger or a war would resolve it, and either outcome would double the pressure on the ferry stage that feeds both routes.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
a reed narrows with two exits
at least 3 km from The North Cut Camp
places.hook: A boat that flees one exit of the reed narrows is met at the other; the crew's whole method is the geometry.

places.name: Cut-Rope
places.whySiteWon: cove in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 514 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on hinterland, parent, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.legendary-deep-feather-serpent (+2.05).

why.founding: A Naga village that took up the roads openly and now lives on them.
why.siteAdvantages: A creek head in shallow marsh that reaches three poling routes and hides a fleet of craft, none of which can be counted from the water.
why.occupantsMotive: Raiders who consider it work, and their families, who consider it income.
why.pressures: The settled tribes have disowned them; the province's tolls have doubled because of them. The settled tribes have disowned them; the province's tolls have doubled because of them, and the coastal brokers who buy the takings are the same brokers the settled tribes sell rice to.
why.wouldChangeIf: A season of failed raids would starve or scatter them. A season of failed raids would starve or scatter them, and scattering is the outcome the settled Naga fear most — a hundred tribeless families with no village to negotiate with.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
a creek head with three poling routes inside an hour
places.hook: The boat sheds hold more craft than the village has people, all taken, all repainted with the same mark.

places.name: Long-Water Hold
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 135 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.bog-blight-ground-old-cordon (+1.97).

why.founding: A settled Naga tribe with a tended Hist, villages, fields and a quarrel with their own tribeless relatives.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground on the inner swamp's main poling route, with a landing deep enough for laden craft, which is the reason they can trade at all.
why.occupantsMotive: People who want the road trade and are undermined by kin who rob it.
why.pressures: Every outsider arrives assuming they are brigands, which is exhausting and occasionally fatal. Every outsider arrives assuming they are brigands, which is exhausting and occasionally fatal, and the hold now pays the northern camp for quiet rather than fight a war it would win and could not afford.
why.wouldChangeIf: A settlement with the tribeless would change how the whole southern interior travels. A settlement with the tribeless would change how the whole southern interior travels, and would cost the coastal escort trade its best market.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
firm ground with a landing deep enough for laden craft
places.hook: Everything is built a size too large, so a normal visitor is physically a child here, and they trade with anyone who can pay the toll.

places.name: The Staking Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 399 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.drowning-narrows-tidal-gate (+0.80).

why.founding: A village that services the grave-stake fields of the deep swamp and works them only after dark, when the blights are readable.
why.siteAdvantages: Central to nine fields, on the one rise that stays dry. Central to nine fields, on the one rise that stays dry — which also makes it the only place in the zone that can store stakes in quantity.
why.occupantsMotive: Stake-setters who work nights and sleep through the day.
why.pressures: Since Umbriel there is more work than there are setters, and the backlog is measurable in risings. Since Umbriel there is more work than there are setters, and the backlog is measurable in risings; villages now bid against each other for a night's work and the poorest fields go unstaked.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing a generation of setters would let the fields go. Losing a generation of setters would let the fields go, and the Naga-Kur's whole grave discipline runs through this village's rota.

places.hook: Arrive in daylight and you will think it abandoned; they work the stake fields at midnight because that is when the blights are readable.

places.name: The Egg Camp
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.bone-carriers-camp-deeps (+0.43).

why.founding: Egg-poachers working the zone's nesting grounds for a coastal buyer.
why.siteAdvantages: Between three nesting sites, on a creek with a fast exit.
why.occupantsMotive: Poachers who take clutches the villages are counting. Poachers who take clutches the villages are counting, working for a coastal buyer who sells the eggs as a delicacy and never sees the marsh.
why.pressures: Taking eggs here reads as close to taking children, and the villages respond accordingly. Taking eggs here reads as close to taking children, and the villages respond accordingly; two poachers have been staked alive and the practice has not stopped.
why.wouldChangeIf: One caught crew would end the trade for a season. One caught crew would end the trade for a season, and would give the villages a name to send to the coast — which is the outcome the buyer has paid to prevent.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
inside an hour of three nesting grounds
places.hook: The crates are stacked in the open because eggs must be kept warm, and one crate is labelled with a species no village here permits to be taken.

places.name: The Drag
