places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 85 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'waterfall' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A slipway where craft are dragged past the narrows rather than run them.
why.siteAdvantages: The shortest firm crossing of the neck between two channels, which is why the rollers have been here for two centuries.
why.occupantsMotive: A drag crew who charge by the hull and keep the rollers greased with fish oil they buy from the drawdown village they are competing with.
why.pressures: The crew and the drawdown village compete for the same traffic, and each has an interest in the other's accidents being talked about.
why.wouldChangeIf: A cut channel would end both trades. A cut channel would end both trades, which is why the two rivals have twice sent a joint delegation against the survey.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
a neck of firm ground under 300 m between two navigable channels
places.hook: Two centuries of hulls have worn a groove in the bog-oak rollers, and the crew charge by how deep your keel sits in it.

places.name: The Lashing
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 214 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.naga-highway-camp-active-south (+1.26).

why.founding: Households who lash their rafts together for the wet season and separate for the dry.
why.siteAdvantages: A sheltered backwater with no current. A sheltered backwater with no current, and no owner — the water is too poor for a fixed village to have claimed it.
why.occupantsMotive: Families who are neighbours six months a year and strangers the other six.
why.pressures: Every year the lashing order is renegotiated and every year it causes a row. Every year the lashing order is renegotiated and every year it causes a row, because the outer rafts take the weather and the inner ones take the smell.
why.wouldChangeIf: A permanent lashing would make them a village and they have voted against it twice. A permanent lashing would make them a village and they have voted against it twice, chiefly because a village can be taxed and a raft cannot be found.

places.hook: Their constitution is a knotted cord, and in the dry season there is nothing here at all.

places.name: The Raided Camp
places.whySiteWon: island in interior swamp (danger band 3), 342 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A village that ran from the raiding Naga and has not gone back.
why.siteAdvantages: The first defensible ground they reached. The first defensible ground they reached, which is nobody's ground, which is why no tribe has had to decide what they are.
why.occupantsMotive: People waiting to hear whether their village still stands.
why.pressures: It has been two years and the camp is becoming a settlement nobody will admit to founding. It has been two years and the camp is becoming a settlement nobody will admit to founding; the children have started calling it by a name the adults refuse to use.
why.wouldChangeIf: News either way ends the camp. News either way ends the camp — and the news exists: a poler has seen the village and has been paid by two different parties not to say what he saw.

places.hook: They have pitched the tents in the exact street plan of the village they ran from, house for house.

places.name: The Warren
places.whySiteWon: flood high in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 544 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A gallery beneath a burial ground.
why.siteAdvantages: The roots reach the graves, which is the whole problem. The roots reach the graves, which is the whole problem: the gallery is fed by the burial ground it undermines.
why.occupantsMotive: Bog blights, in numbers, working steadily upward. Bog blights, in numbers, working steadily upward — and, unusually, staying below by day, which is the only reason the village above still exists.
why.pressures: The village above is driving a stake ring and losing ground each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing and restaking it is the zone's defining deed. Clearing and restaking it is the zone's defining deed, and the Naga-Kur would owe whoever did it a standing that no amount of trade buys.

places.hook: A mouth in the middle of a stake field with fresh stakes driven in a ring around it, because the risen went down and followed the roots back toward the village.

places.name: Root-Whisper Village
places.whySiteWon: flood high in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 491 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleids destroyed the tribe here and harvested its souls into the Remnant of Argon; the Hist did not die but slept, and was called the Dreaming Tree for as long as it slept. At the end of the Second Era the souls were returned and the village was re-founded on its own ground, between the twin xanmeers Xul-Thuxis and Vakka-Bok.
why.siteAdvantages: East Deepmire ground the tribe never technically left, held between two pre-Duskfall xanmeers that mark it from a distance and keep the approach to one line.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe rebuilt out of returned souls, living on the exact ground it was killed on, because the tree is here and the tree is the only reason any of them exist.
why.pressures: The Hist is elder in years and young in voice — it speaks like a hatchling and is treated by its own tree-minder as convalescent — and Cyrodilic Collections, which helped resurrect the tribe, has never quite stopped treating the village as its find.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Dreaming Tree failed a second time there would be no second Remnant; the tribe knows this and organises its whole year around not finding out.

places.hook: A Hist with a hatchling's voice and an elder's trunk, in a village whose souls the Ayleids took and something gave back.

places.name: The Shut Meer
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 525 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.maturity-trial-kaju-kill (+1.20).

why.founding: A xanmeer whose vakka mechanisms have never stopped working.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise in black water with no approach that is not overlooked by the building.
why.occupantsMotive: The defences. The defences, and nothing else: no squatters, no scavengers, no den — the one xanmeer in the zone with no living tenant at all.
why.pressures: Four expeditions in fifty years, no returns; the count is kept by the nearest village. Four expeditions in fifty years, no returns; the count is kept by the nearest village, who charge to recite it and consider the recitation a public service.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing short of the mechanisms failing. Nothing short of the mechanisms failing — and the vakka stones that drive them are worth more than the contents to every broker on the coast.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
a rise in black water with no approach the building does not command
places.hook: A xanmeer whose vakka mechanisms have never stopped, and no approach to it is out of the building's sight.

places.name: The Adder Banks
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 252 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: Moon adders den along a stretch of bank that catches what little moonlight the zone gets.
why.siteAdvantages: Open banks with a clear sky line — rare here.
why.occupantsMotive: Adders, and the venom-takers who work them for the daril trade. The venom-takers work at moonrise because the adders come to the open bank then; the whole trade is timed to the one thing the zone's canopy allows.
why.pressures: The takers are unlicensed and the village nearby wants a cut. The takers are unlicensed and the village nearby wants a cut, and has begun burning the bank margin to drive the adders onto its own ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: A licence deal would make it a works site instead of a lair. A licence deal would make it a works site instead of a lair, and would put the daril trade of three regions behind one village's gate.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
open bank with a clear sky line — rare in this zone
places.hook: The one open bank in the zone that catches moonlight, which is exactly why the adders den in it.

places.name: The Black Eye
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 427 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A collapse in the root layer, drowned, in the middle of a reed flat.
why.siteAdvantages: A rare hole the swamp has flooded rather than filled — one of only a handful in the province, so the thing itself is a landmark.
why.occupantsMotive: Divers, occasionally. Divers, occasionally, and always the same three, who will not take passengers and will not say what they bring up.
why.pressures: It goes into the root layer and nobody has mapped where it comes out. It goes into the root layer and nobody has mapped where it comes out, though a body put in here has twice surfaced two zones away.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry cycle would expose the rim and make it enterable on foot.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
a round hole of open black water in a reed flat
places.hook: A perfectly round hole of black water in a reed flat, with the reeds stopping dead at the edge as if cut.

places.name: The Emptying House
places.whySiteWon: flood high in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 719 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A Sithis temple in the deep swamp where the doctrine is practised at its least metaphorical.
why.siteAdvantages: Black water on all sides and no neighbour close enough to object. Black water on all sides and no neighbour close enough to object, and one landing that can be watched from the house itself.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo who preach a sermon the coastal Nisswo will not repeat.
why.pressures: The interior tribes tolerate it and do not attend; the settled Naga forbid their young to go. The interior tribes tolerate it and do not attend; the settled Naga forbid their young to go, and the forbidding has made attendance a way for the young to make a point.
why.wouldChangeIf: A closure would need someone with authority nobody in the deep swamp recognises. A closure would need someone with authority nobody in the deep swamp recognises — and the coastal Nisswo who could claim that authority will not come this far in.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
raised ground with one watched landing
places.hook: The building is beautifully kept, which is the disturbing part; the sanctuary floor drains to one hole and everything the temple has done goes down it.

places.name: The Still-Walking Village
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 181 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, parent; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.horwalli-waterworks-deeps (+1.51).

why.founding: A village under the Umbriel track whose dead did not lie down afterwards.
why.siteAdvantages: Directly on the shadow's path, which nobody could have chosen. Directly on the shadow's path, which nobody could have chosen, and on ground that was the best rice land in the zone before it.
why.occupantsMotive: The village's own dead, still in their own houses.
why.pressures: This is precisely the enemy the Naga-Kur's discipline was built for, and they have contained rather than cleared it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it is a deed the Naga-Kur would owe the player for permanently. Clearing it is a deed the Naga-Kur would owe the player for permanently — and would free the rice ground, which four neighbouring villages have already privately divided.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
places.hook: The Naga-Kur have staked a containment ring a kilometre out rather than go in, and the ring is dated and being pushed slowly inward.

places.name: The Split Cistern
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 517 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'sinkhole' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none); site exchanged in the swap pass with place.naga-kur-deeps.dead-water-village (+2.22).

why.founding: A sealed cistern that a subsidence cracked open twelve years ago.
why.siteAdvantages: Under a xanmeer floor, in ground that is still moving, so any seal put back would have to be built to shift with it.
why.occupantsMotive: What was sealed in it, now not sealed in it.
why.pressures: It is spreading through the flooded lower halls and out into the swamp. It is spreading through the flooded lower halls and out into the swamp, and the dredgers working two channels away have started finding it in their spoil.
why.wouldChangeIf: Sealing it again is possible and nobody has the nerve. Sealing it again is possible and nobody has the nerve; the tending clan has priced the work three times and each price has been higher than the last.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
inside or under a xanmeer floor
places.hook: A hand's-width crack in a sealed cistern, and successive visitors have charted the spread from it on the wall outside.

places.name: The Standing Charge
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 309 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An adult wamasu holds a pond on the zone's main poling route.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep still water a few hundred metres off the main poling line, close enough that the detour poles run past it for its whole length.
why.occupantsMotive: One adult, resident for years. One adult, resident for years, and the villages have begun leaving offerings at the bank in the old Shadowfen manner rather than treat it as vermin.
why.pressures: Traffic detours two hours around it and the detour is itself dangerous. Traffic detours two hours around it and the detour is itself dangerous, running past the reed narrows where the southern camp works.
why.wouldChangeIf: Killing it reopens the route and the tribes disagree about whether it should be killed. Killing it reopens the route and the tribes disagree about whether it should be killed — the offering-makers hold that a wamasu on a route is a toll, not a problem.

places.hook: A marked detour whose poles have stood so long they have grown roots, and the thing they route you around has not moved either.

places.name: The Withdrawn Tree
places.whySiteWon: island in interior swamp (danger band 4), 639 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on remote, landform, region; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: A wild Hist that has cut itself off from the collective — the rare, catastrophic condition, visible in one place.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep swamp, no tribe, no witnesses to argue about it. Deep swamp, no tribe, no witnesses to argue about it — which is also why it has been left alone long enough to be studied.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing speaks for it and nothing tends it. Nothing speaks for it and nothing tends it; the nearest tribe sends no one and will not explain the omission to outsiders.
why.pressures: It is the physical demonstration of the main quest's premise, standing in the world before the quest names it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Reconnection is possible in principle and nobody knows how. Reconnection is possible in principle and nobody knows how, and the tribes that could try are the same tribes that will not go near it.

places.hook: White light where there should be blue: a Hist that has cut itself off from the rest, and the tribes will not go near it.

places.name: The Sunk Barge
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: An Imperial-era cargo barge that went down in the narrows with its load aboard.
why.siteAdvantages: It sank in the deep of the bend and has never shifted, so the hull is intact and the holds are still closed.
why.occupantsMotive: Fish, and divers who take a little at a time. Fish, and divers who take a little at a time, on the reasoning that a wreck emptied all at once is a wreck somebody comes to look at.
why.pressures: The cargo is bonded goods and a company that no longer exists still legally owns them. The cargo is bonded goods and a company that no longer exists still legally owns them, which makes selling any of it on the coast a question rather than a sale.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry cycle would expose the deck and end the slow looting.

hardConstraints: at least 12 km inland — this is the deep interior
in navigable water at least 4 m deep, on the outside of a bend
places.hook: Her cargo seals are intact and legible, which makes everything you take off her provably stolen from a company that has not existed for a century.

places.name: Alten Corimont
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'alten-corimont' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: A river port ESE of the Hatching Pools that grew into a small town by being institutionally neutral about cargo: it sits on the northern trunk between Stormhold and Thorn, on water deep enough for a laden hull and far enough from any customs regime that both of them use it.
why.siteAdvantages: The last reach of navigable river below the northern rim, with an oxbow that makes a natural basin, firm banks for warehousing and a rim road behind it that crosses to Morrowind without passing a post.
why.occupantsMotive: A captain of the port whose only law is a nailed-up price list, freeholder crews with no tribe and no tree, Dunmer factors from the Morrowind trade and Nord hands off the northern hulls.
why.pressures: There is no Hist here — the register is explicit — so nothing binds anyone to anything except the list; Stormhold's vicecanons would like the trade and cannot reach it; Rockpoint downriver still resents losing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If either Stormhold or Thorn made the port lawful, its whole reason to exist is gone; if the river silted below the oxbow, the town is a village in five years.

hardConstraints: navigable water for a laden hull
sheltered basin off the legal lanes
no Hist within the settlement — canon
places.hook: The free port: everything here is for sale at a price nailed up in public, including the passage out.

places.name: Bundle Racks
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 72 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Argonians who die away from a Hist can still return if their bones are brought to the dirt — and this zone has no Hist at all, so every death here starts a journey south.
why.siteAdvantages: On the trunk route at the point where the southbound road and the river both leave the freeholds.
why.occupantsMotive: Bone-carriers who take the dead of a town that cannot bury them, for a fee they are ashamed of.
why.pressures: The house is always full, because the freeholds produce more Hist-less dead than any comparable ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Hist were ever planted at the free port, this house closes and the carriers lose a trade.

places.hook: Bundled bones waiting on racks for someone travelling the right way upriver, and a keeper who will pay you to be that someone.

places.name: The Hard
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 73 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger.

why.founding: Foreign keeled hulls come this far up the river and have to be laid over and scraped somewhere the owner is not watching.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm shelving bank inside the basin, with a hard bottom that will take a hull's weight at low water.
why.occupantsMotive: Boatwrights who build canoes beautifully and repair Nord hulls badly, on purpose, for money.
why.pressures: Hull identities change here: a name is planed off and another painted on, and everybody knows the going rate.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port were ever inspected, the hard is the first thing that would have to disappear.

places.hook: Hulls laid over and scraped where the owner cannot see, by boatwrights who will change a boat's name for a price.

places.name: Short Rope
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 517 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: The free port sells to everyone and therefore protects no one, so the crews that will not keep to the price list anchor a reach away and take what the list would have made them pay for.
why.siteAdvantages: A blind reach with a cut bank, out of sight of the port and above the last mooring anybody legal uses.
why.occupantsMotive: A Salt-Teeth crew working the reach between the port and the head of navigation, keeping their prizes in the bank until they can be sold as salvage.
why.pressures: The port halls will tolerate them exactly as long as the price list is not undercut in public.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the port ever set a rate for salvage, the crew would come in and pay it, and hate it.

hardConstraints: at least 800 m from Alten Corimont
out of sight of the free port
places.hook: A crew that will not pay the port's prices keeps its prizes in a hole in the bank, and will kill you for looking at them.

places.name: Chasecreek
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 158 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent.

why.founding: A fishing hamlet on the one rise the creek does not reach, which found that a boat can wait out of the channel here while the free port is being watched, and has lived off that ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: A rise of firm ground well above the water, with a creek behind it deep enough to lie a hull in and shallow enough that nobody follows.
why.occupantsMotive: Fisher households who are also, on about four nights a month, a lay-by with a fee.
why.pressures: The lay-by trade is worth more than the fish, everyone under sixteen already knows it, and the port road runs close enough that being discreet is work.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port's list ever covered waiting time, Chasecreek loses its niche and becomes a fishing hamlet again.

hardConstraints: ground that stays above the flood
a creek mouth deep enough to lie in
the mooring screened from the main channel
places.hook: A fishing hamlet that makes most of its money letting other people's boats wait where nobody is looking.

places.name: Crosstrees
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 43 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The free port is built around a hull that was dragged up the bank and never floated again. Its masts were left standing because they were useful, and the crosstrees became the port's lookout: the one place in the freehold you can see over the roofs and the canopy at once.
why.siteAdvantages: The beached hull sits on the highest firm ground in the basin, and the canopy is cut back around it so the lookout can work.
why.occupantsMotive: The port's lookout watches for hulls coming up the reach, and charges nothing, because everybody benefits from knowing early.
why.pressures: The rigging is sixty years past its rope; the ladder is rebuilt every wet season and rebuilt worse.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the hull finally goes over, the freehold loses the only high ground it has and starts posting watchers on the water instead.

hardConstraints: a clear line north-west down the reach and west along the road
places.hook: Climb the old hull's masts and the lookout will name everything you can see from up there, including the boat that leaves for the capital.

places.name: The Hiring Yard
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 78 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Debts bought at the gambling house become owings, and owings become gangs — the yard is where the people who lost their ground wait to be told where they are working.
why.siteAdvantages: A hard standing beside the porter yard, on the only road out of the free port.
why.occupantsMotive: Households whose owing was called in, and a broker's clerk with a ledger.
why.pressures: Nobody here is chained and nobody here can leave, and the difference is legally important and practically nil.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Chainbreaker cell reached the yard, the free port's labour supply stops on the same day.

hardConstraints: on the road out of a settlement
a hard standing and a ledger office
places.hook: The yard where an owing turns into a work gang, and the ledger is read aloud so everyone hears the months go on.

places.name: No-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 412 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent.

why.founding: The register is explicit that the free port has no Hist, and that is not an omission — it is the reason the freeholds exist. Everyone here is Hist-less by choice or by accident, and the camp on the town's edge is where that is admitted out loud.
why.siteAdvantages: The town's landward fringe, on ground the port does not administer.
why.occupantsMotive: Argonians with no tree to return to, plus outsiders who find that easier to be around.
why.pressures: The tribal villages upriver will not visit; Hissmir's reconnection rite is a two-week journey and a hard conversation.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Hist cutting were successfully planted here, the free port stops being a freehold and starts being a town.

places.hook: A village with a planting circle kept swept for sixty years and nothing in it, and people who will tell you exactly why.

places.name: The Low Store
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 270 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.trunk-toll-bridge (+1.44).

why.founding: A bonded store was cut into the channel bank when the water sat two feet lower. The water came back, the owner stopped paying the port, and the doors were left to whoever wanted them.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry-ish cellar under a wet bank, on the water but out of sight of the quay.
why.occupantsMotive: Three of the port's less useful hands sleep here between jobs and take what floats past.
why.pressures: It floods to the knee on a high river and to the chest twice a year.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the port ever enforced its own bond seals, the store would be emptied in a morning.

hardConstraints: a cut bank on the channel
places.hook: A flooded store under the bank with three idlers living in it, and whatever the last owner never came back for.

places.name: The Quay Room
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 71 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A port whose social hall is a beached hull still needs somewhere you can pay for a bed and a locked door.
why.siteAdvantages: On the basin front, one door from the hull hall and two from the gambling house.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who sells beds and rents silence.
why.pressures: Four languages in one room, and the guest book is worth more than the takings.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port were made lawful, the guest book becomes evidence and the keeper burns it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a mooring
places.hook: A bed, a door that locks, and a guest book in four scripts that is worth more than the takings.

places.name: The Old Pens
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 183 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: House Dres took Argonians out of this river country for centuries, and the pens they used to hold and count them are still standing on the bank they loaded from.
why.siteAdvantages: A river landing with hard standing, sited for loading rather than living.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody above ground. Something has been getting into the flooded cells below, and the free port will not use the ground and will not explain why to outsiders.
why.pressures: It is the one thing in this zone nobody makes a joke about.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Dunmer factors in town were ever formally associated with it, the freehold's trade with Morrowind ends overnight.

hardConstraints: a river landing built for loading
places.hook: The Dres loading pens, still standing, count-marks still cut in the gatepost, and something living in the cells below.

places.name: Andrano Hold
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 341 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.veterans-holding (+1.13).

why.founding: A House holding left over from the Dres trade, now a Dunmer village on the wrong side of the border that stayed because going home was worse.
why.siteAdvantages: A defensible upland shelf on the pass road, with its own water and a walled core.
why.occupantsMotive: Dunmer families three centuries settled, who factor for the free port and are not liked for it.
why.pressures: They are the largest concentration of the zone's 22% Dunmer minority and they live beside the pens their ancestors filled.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Morrowind reasserted a claim here, the free port's northern trade becomes a diplomatic asset instead of a crime.

places.hook: The last Andrano still holding a Morrowind house on the wrong side of the border, with cellars nobody has opened in two hundred years.

places.name: Five-Sixty Field
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 90 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.rockpoint (+0.95).

why.founding: The people who died in the Flu here were not Argonian and had no Hist to go to, so they were cairned where they fell, by whoever was left.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm dry ground above the village, with loose stone to hand.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; the cairns are re-stacked by passing travellers, which is a custom nobody can explain.
why.pressures: It is the largest visible evidence in the zone that a whole people used to live here.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a scholar counted them properly, the district's population history changes.

places.hook: Five hundred and sixty stakes in one field, and one cairn that was opened from the inside.

places.name: The Open Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 598 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.freehold-naga-camp (+0.47).

why.founding: The price list has to be applied somewhere, and the stall row under the list board is where the zone's economy actually happens.
why.siteAdvantages: Level ground below the list board, one street up from the basin and not on the water itself.
why.occupantsMotive: Traders working in septims, Dunmer coin, barter and obligation at adjacent stalls.
why.pressures: The board is a public document that names contraband, which makes it the province's best commercial intelligence.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the list were withdrawn, the row would still meet and nobody would know what anything was worth.

hardConstraints: inside the free port, under the list board
places.hook: Four provinces' goods under one board that prices contraband by grade, in three currencies that disagree.

places.name: Nine Mile
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 224 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.freehold-market (+0.47).

why.founding: A Naga band works the trunk road where it runs closest to the marsh, because the freeholds' cargo is worth taking and nobody polices the road.
why.siteAdvantages: Cover within a spear's throw of the road at a point where it cannot be left.
why.occupantsMotive: Eight or so, mobile, who move camp after every taking.
why.pressures: The free port pays escorts rather than fight them, which is cheaper and everyone knows it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the reoccupied fort extended its patrols, the band moves to the river and takes boats instead.

hardConstraints: cover within a spear's throw of the trunk road
at least 1.2 km from Alten Corimont
a point where the road cannot be left
places.hook: A Naga band camped a spear's throw off the trunk road, at the point where you cannot leave it.

places.name: Bellet's
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 76 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.kothringi-river-ruin (+0.85).

why.founding: A port that takes anyone's cargo takes everyone's sickness, and a town with no temple needs somewhere to put the sick.
why.siteAdvantages: Downwind and downstream of the free port, on its own ground.
why.occupantsMotive: Two keepers with no formal training and four hundred years of accumulated local practice.
why.pressures: It is funded out of the price list, which is the only public spending in the zone.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the list stopped funding it, the port would find out very quickly why it did.

hardConstraints: downwind and downstream of the settlement
places.hook: The only place in the freehold that will take you in without asking what you can pay.

places.name: The Anomaly
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 86 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.freehold-pest-house (+1.69).

why.founding: A province with almost no metalworking has one here, because a free port that steals fastenings needs somewhere to reuse them.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the careening hard inside the port, on the only ground in the zone with a permanent forge on it.
why.occupantsMotive: A Nord smith who came off a hull twenty years ago and never re-embarked.
why.pressures: His stock is entirely other people's ship iron and everyone pretends not to know.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the fastening supply were cut, the forge goes cold and the boatwrights lose their hulls.

hardConstraints: inside Alten Corimont, within 250 m of the basin
places.hook: The only forge in the province, worked by a Nord who came off a hull, stocked entirely with other people's ship iron.

places.name: Long Water
places.whySiteWon: spring head in border mountains (danger band 3), 496 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on hinterland, parent, route; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.reach-wreck (+1.50).

why.founding: Half the crews on this water hold a charter from somebody, and none of them will say from whom. Long Water is where they lie up between charters, and the port treats it as a berth rather than a problem.
why.siteAdvantages: A long straight reach with deep water on one bank, room for four hulls and a clear run out in either direction.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews resting, refitting and hiring, and a broker who sells passage to anyone who does not ask what else the hull is carrying.
why.pressures: One bad prize and the port halls withdraw the berth, and the whole anchorage becomes Short Rope.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the League of Open Water ever chartered these crews properly, the freehold would have a navy and stop being a freehold.

hardConstraints: on navigable water deep enough for a laden hull
places.hook: Four crews lying up between charters, and a broker on the middle hull who will sell you passage and not ask why you want it.

places.name: Slack Bend
places.whySiteWon: gorge in firm lowland (danger band 3), 66 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on region, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.freehold-pest-house (+0.85).

why.founding: The Kothringi held river country like this and the Knahaten Flu ended them in 2E 560; their village on the bend was never reoccupied because nobody would.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bend site with a landing — the same reasons a village would be built there today.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The free port's crews will not tie up here and will not say it is superstition.
why.pressures: It is the best unoccupied river frontage in the zone and it has been empty for six hundred years.
why.wouldChangeIf: If somebody built here and did not die, the whole taboo collapses and the zone gains a settlement site.

hardConstraints: a river bend with a landing
places.hook: The best empty river frontage in the zone, and six hundred years of crews refusing to tie up at it.

places.name: The Roll
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 77 m from the nearest route; no free 'any-channel-bank' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on sightline, region, parent.

why.founding: The free port pays for its channel to stay open, and the cheapest way to keep it open is a dredging gang that owes money. The barge is where the gang lives, and where a new hand is read onto the roll.
why.siteAdvantages: Moored in the channel off the port, close enough to work the reach and far enough that the port does not have to look at it.
why.occupantsMotive: A broker's detail, a handful of overseers and thirty people who owe months; two of them are visibly washed out from years away from their Hist.
why.pressures: The ledger is read aloud at every intake, with the months added for food, and nobody argues because arguing costs months.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the port stopped paying for the dredging, the owings would be sold on to an estate upriver and the barge would be broken for planking.

hardConstraints: shallow water and reed cover on the far side for the escape
places.hook: Where the game starts: a dredging barge, a ledger with your months on it, and a night that ends with the deck on fire.

places.name: Gang Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 56 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: A gang that works a channel has to sleep somewhere on land, and the families follow the gang. The camp is forty years old and has never been called anything but the ground the gang is on.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm bank opposite the barge's mooring, with a hatching shed set back from the water where the ground stays dry.
why.occupantsMotive: Families whose people are on the roll, keeping a life going within walking distance of it.
why.pressures: The camp has a Hist a day upriver and no claim on it, and the clutch in the shed is the argument for staying.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the clutch is lost, the camp has no reason to be here and every reason to go somewhere the ledger cannot follow.

hardConstraints: on the bank opposite the work barge, within 200 m of it
dry ground for a hatching shed
places.hook: The gang's families live here, and the shed at the back holds the eggs that die on the first night of the game.

places.name: Sixty Tun Salt
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 23 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.half-chartered-anchorage (+1.50).

why.founding: A laden river hull that failed to hold the line above the bar and went down in the deep of the confluence.
why.siteAdvantages: It lies in the confluence hole at -6.5 m, out of the current but under a lot of water.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing; the salvage yard has stripped everything above the silt line.
why.pressures: The hold is under silt and the yard has decided it is not worth the drowning.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the river dropped in a hard dry season, the hold would be reachable and the yard would work it in a week.

places.hook: Sixty tun of salt on the bottom of the confluence hole, and a hold the salvage yard decided was not worth drowning for.

places.name: Gorrey's Fort
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 309 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: An intact Imperial fort on the trunk road, abandoned two hundred years ago, into which somebody moved and started charging.
why.siteAdvantages: It commands the trunk where the road cannot go around it — which is why the Legion built there.
why.occupantsMotive: A toll-taking outfit with a claim, a garrison of thirty and no legal standing whatsoever.
why.pressures: They are the free port's only rival for the road trade, and the port would rather they existed than the state did.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the state ever garrisoned it properly, the whole zone's economy is enclosed in a season.

places.hook: An intact Imperial fort with somebody else's flag on it, charging the road toll it has no right to charge.

places.name: Nine Sockets
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 307 m from the nearest route; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, danger; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleids left keystone mechanisms across the fringe of this country, and one of them is cut into the rim rock above the river.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry chamber in the ravine wall, above the flood and below the snow.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living; the mechanism is the occupant.
why.pressures: The sockets are empty and the keystones are elsewhere, which is exactly the problem the type poses.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the keystones were returned, whatever the chamber does would start doing it again.

places.hook: Nine sockets cut for keystones nobody has ever found, and whatever moved in once the cutting stopped.

places.name: The Snowline Stage
places.whySiteWon: saddle in border mountains (danger band 3), 424 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The one legal crossing of the northern rim needs a staged shelter, because the pass is above the snowline for part of the year and people die on it.
why.siteAdvantages: The saddle at 226 m: the lowest crossing of the wall for many kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who is nominally the state's and is paid by the free port, which he does not advertise.
why.pressures: The pass closes seasonally, and when it closes the ledge trade doubles.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the state funded it properly the rim would be policed and this zone's economy would change entirely.

hardConstraints: at the lowest crossing of the rim
places.hook: The last roofed room before the pass into Morrowind, and the only place to ask what the road is like today.

places.name: The North Traverse
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 233 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The free port's cargo has to leave the province somehow, and the legal crossings into Morrowind are few — so the illegal ones are the rim itself.
why.siteAdvantages: A cliff bench two-thirds of the way up the border wall, out of sight from below and from the pass, with a traverse line rather than a path.
why.occupantsMotive: Two or three men who move consignments and mark which side each one is going.
why.pressures: It is a four-hour climb with a load and the weather on the rim turns without warning.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the pass station below were properly manned, the ledge becomes the only route and the price triples.

hardConstraints: a rim ledge out of sight of the pass
no water — this is the dry route
places.hook: A staffed ledge where goods cross the border without passing a post, held by people who would rather you had not seen it.

places.name: Exile's Roof
places.whySiteWon: summit in border mountains (danger band 3), 604 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Somebody was put out of an order and went as high as there is to go in this province, which is the northern rim.
why.siteAdvantages: Above the snowline on the border wall, with a spring that does not freeze.
why.occupantsMotive: One or two, keeping an observance nobody else keeps.
why.pressures: It is the coldest inhabited place in Argonia and reaching it is a genuine expedition.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the order that exiled them collapsed, the observance here becomes the only surviving version of it.

hardConstraints: a spring that does not freeze
on the rim above the Corimont pass, inside the freehold's own reach
places.hook: Snow on an inhabited roof in Argonia, a day's climb up, kept by one exile with an observance nobody else keeps.

places.name: Rockpoint
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 306 m from the nearest route; no free 'cliff-bench' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, danger, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.flu-cairn-field (+0.95).

why.founding: A rival landing founded downriver to undercut Alten Corimont's list, which lost — because the river bar below it will not take a laden hull and the list will not be undercut.
why.siteAdvantages: A stone-footed landing, a warehouse shell and a defensible bank, all standing, on ground nobody now claims.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The bar that killed it also keeps casual squatters away, and Alten Corimont makes sure the story of why it failed is well told.
why.pressures: It is intact, empty, freehold ground with a river frontage — which in this zone is the most valuable unowned thing there is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If anyone repaired the landing and dredged the bar, Alten Corimont would have a competitor again, and would act.

hardConstraints: a standing landing and at least one roofed shell
downstream of the free port, below a bar
places.hook: A derelict steading with its own landing, empty since the port outgrew it, and yours if you can make the roof hold.

places.name: The Trunk Span
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 37 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'water-narrows' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.corimont-low-store (+1.44).

why.founding: The road from the free port to Stormhold has to cross the channel, and the crossing has an owner, as every crossing here does.
why.siteAdvantages: The narrowest hard-banked crossing on the Alten Corimont to Stormhold road.
why.occupantsMotive: Four toll-takers working for a freehold syndicate that bought the span outright.
why.pressures: The Owing operates at this crossing, as it does at every tolled crossing in the route graph, and the ledger is kept in the open.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port bought the span outright, Stormhold's road trade would be paying Alten Corimont directly, which is why it has not happened.

hardConstraints: spans the channel at its narrowest
on the Alten Corimont to Stormhold road
places.hook: The span the road has to cross, owned outright, with a board that prices people in a column of their own.

places.name: Blacklight Holding
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in border mountains (danger band 3), 453 m from the nearest route; no free 'ridge-end' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.pirate-freeholds.dunmer-frontier-holding (+1.13).

why.founding: Argonians who went north into Morrowind in the 4E came back and would not settle in ordinary villages, so they made their own holding on the border they had crossed.
why.siteAdvantages: High firm ground on the flank above the pass, chosen for the sightline rather than the soil.
why.occupantsMotive: Veterans and their children, armed, organised, and not answerable to the free port.
why.pressures: They are the only armed force in the zone and everyone is careful about what they are asked to do.
why.wouldChangeIf: If they were ever hired by the port, the freeholds become a power rather than a market.

hardConstraints: a view of the border crossing
places.hook: Argonians who fought in Morrowind and came home armed, holding their own ground above the pass and answering to nobody.

places.name: Archon
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'archon' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: A deep, sheltered estuary mouth on the Padomaic was the one place on this coast a foreign hull could lie safely, so the Second Empire and then the East Empire Company built a stone quay here and the Saxhleel town grew landward of it.
why.siteAdvantages: Estuary with a landable stone shore, a river road into the interior, and the only stretch of the east coast where the mangrove wall breaks for more than a kilometre.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian-majority harbour population who work the water as amphibians and run the port authority out of dead Company offices, alongside state customs and a long-settled Dunmer merchant minority from the Morrowind trade.
why.pressures: The lawful port is the province's only functioning customs choke, so everything that wants to avoid it goes round it: half-chartered hulls land on the Oliis shore and wreckers work the Padomaic beaches south of the city. The mangrove and jungle behind the city is D4 within a kilometre of the gate, and the sealed Shadowscale sanctuary is a thing nobody will discuss and everybody knows about.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Archon-Lilmoth-Soulrest-Tear line stopped running, or if the harbour authority lost its claim to the Company buildings, Archon would become a large fishing town in a month.

hardConstraints: deep water at the quay line at the highest seasonal level
places.hook: The one harbour on this coast where a foreign hull can tie up legally, and the one desk in the province that can tell you where a cargo went.

places.name: Reaches-The-Low-Branch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 51 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, bound, parent.

why.founding: The register fixes a small Hist landward of the harbour — the city's own tree rather than a grove capital's, planted or tended where the salt does not reach.
why.siteAdvantages: The first freshwater ground behind the estuary: a low rise inside the cleared apron that the tide never covers, with jungle closing on three sides of it.
why.occupantsMotive: Tree-minders keep it; dockworkers touch it going out and coming in; the Dunmer quarter does not.
why.pressures: Salt intrusion is rising with the quay works, and the tree is smaller than it was a century ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the estuary silts or the harbour cuts a deeper channel, this Hist dies and Archon becomes a Hist-less city with a port.

places.hook: The city's own Hist stands ten minutes from the quay, and its minders keep the one account of Archon nobody has edited.

places.name: The Closed Sanctuary
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 313 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, region, parent.

why.founding: Children born under the Shadow were given up to the Dark Brotherhood here under the old compact; the compact lapsed and the sanctuary was closed by order in 4E 187.
why.siteAdvantages: Deliberately unremarkable ground within an hour of the city, off both boat lanes and out of sight of the river road — near enough to walk from the hatchery, far enough that nobody passes it by accident.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. A watcher is paid to sit where he can see the path, by someone who has not visited in fourteen years.
why.pressures: The Cheydinhal Listener wanted it back; the harbour authority would rather it stopped existing; the birth-sign roll inside names living adults who do not know what they were promised to.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the roll were made public, or if the door were opened, half the Shadowscale line's premise collapses at once.

hardConstraints: concealed approach — no sightline from any route
places.hook: The Shadowscale school Archon closed, sealed and never emptied — and the Brotherhood in Cheydinhal wants it reopened.

places.name: The Ashen Towers
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 275 m from the nearest route; no free 'headland' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, parent, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.deep-bank (+1.72).

why.founding: Cantemiric Velothi — elven dissidents out of Morrowind — built towers on the highest ground they could hold above the eastern shore, and the marsh took the lower half back.
why.siteAdvantages: High, drained ground with fresh water and a neck one wall could close, chosen for the reason Velothi always chose: it faces east, toward home.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The Dunmer families in Archon know the house mark and will not discuss it.
why.pressures: Salt has eaten the render for two thousand years; the ancestor niches are empty and the reason is not recorded.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a living House claimed descent, the Archon Dunmer quarter's standing in the city changes overnight.

hardConstraints: high ground on the eastern seaboard with open water in sight
a narrow neck that can be walled
places.hook: Velothi towers standing above the canopy with half their floors under water, and nobody living within a day's walk to explain them.

places.name: Two-Marks-One-Rope
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 25 m from the nearest route; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Productive open water lying exactly between two villages that both claim it.
why.siteAdvantages: A shelf inside the mangrove channels where cold water rises: reliably full of fish, and reliably indefensible.
why.occupantsMotive: Both fleets work it, on alternate days when relations are good.
why.pressures: Claim buoys carry two marks on the same rope; gear has been cut adrift twice this year.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Archon's harbour authority licensed it, both villages would unite against the licence.

places.hook: Two crews claim this shelf and both are on it today; you can fish it, broker it or take it.

places.name: Nine Fathom
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 307 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'natural-harbour' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.cantemir-headland (+1.72).

why.founding: A deeper bank out on the lane, worked by whoever has the hull to reach it.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep water off the lagoon mouth, no shelter, a long run from any shore — which is why only Argonian lungs work it.
why.occupantsMotive: Crews from three settlements who do not meet ashore.
why.pressures: It is a day's sail from help and the weather here turns fast.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a storm shelter existed on the nearest islet the bank would be worked twice as hard.

places.hook: Deep enough that only an Argonian can reach the bottom, and something down there feeds on what the nets miss.

places.name: The Dusk Island
places.whySiteWon: islet in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 60 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A low island in the lagoon where an enormous number of birds roost, worked for eggs and down under a rota.
why.siteAdvantages: An island with no predators, ringed by water too shallow for boats at low tide.
why.occupantsMotive: Egg-harvesters from two villages under a rota that limits the take.
why.pressures: The rota exists because they emptied it once; the harvesting frames are older than anyone using them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the rota broke, the column stops and the coast loses its one living landmark.

hardConstraints: island or stand surrounded by water
places.hook: An islet of nesting birds that will mob anything that lands, and eggs and feathers worth the bruises.

places.name: The Estuary Mouth Station
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 143 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The Pass-1 transport compile already puts a rootworm terminus on the east estuary; this record fixes it as a real place with a reason — the coast's only fast link inland, at the one point where the root layer reaches tidewater.
why.siteAdvantages: Where a rootland arm runs out under firm ground within a short walk of the estuary landing, so a passenger can step off a boat and into the root.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers who read the worms' movement and sell passage they cannot guarantee.
why.pressures: The worms are alive and seasonal; a standing station is a claim, not a timetable.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the root arm died back, the coast loses its only fast transit and Archon becomes a week from the interior.

places.hook: Pay the waykeepers and the root will carry you to Helstrom in a day, in the dark, with no idea what you passed.

places.name: Carves-All-Winter
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 85 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, hinterland.

why.founding: Somebody has to keep the estuary marks lit and the stake lines cut, and that somebody has to sleep near the water.
why.siteAdvantages: The only firm hummock on the estuary's north shore, dry at the highest seasonal level and one boat-length from the channel.
why.occupantsMotive: Four generations of one family, contractually stuck with it and quietly expert.
why.pressures: The fuel account is paid late, every year, and the family has learned to hoard.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the light were automated or abandoned, the family would still be here, keeping nothing.

hardConstraints: dry ground at the highest seasonal level
a landing on the estuary channel
places.hook: The keeper knows every mark, every wreck and every hull that passed at night, and will trade none of it for coin.

places.name: Takes-The-Wrong-Gap
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, submerged, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.shell-beast-shallows (+0.26).

why.founding: A shallow bar across otherwise navigable water with one buoyed gap through it; hulls that read the buoys wrong end on the bar, and the bar keeps them.
why.siteAdvantages: Broken water over a shallow bar with a single marked gap, close enough to the lane that a pilot's mistake is cheap to reach.
why.occupantsMotive: Divers work the harvest lots; the wrecks on it are worked by everyone.
why.pressures: Whoever moves the buoys decides where the next hull ends up, and somebody has been moving them.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the lighthouse went dark, the count would be four within a season.

places.hook: Three hulls on one bar, still holding their cargo, reachable only on a held breath.

places.name: Eleven-Berth
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 0), 12 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A second shelter on the lagoon crossing, because the crossing is two hours and the squalls are shorter than that.
why.siteAdvantages: A low islet in the mangrove crossing with the only firm standing between the two shores.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; boat crews waiting out weather.
why.pressures: It floods in the worst storms, which is the joke everyone makes about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were raised a metre it would be the safest place on the lagoon.

places.hook: Eleven berths, a dry floor and a bar across the door: the one place to sit out a squall on the crossing.

places.name: The Standing Corner
places.whySiteWon: island in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 418 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, submerged; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: The terraces were built dry; the water came later, and came to stay.
why.siteAdvantages: A drowned lagoon deep enough to swallow six terraces and clear enough to read the geometry from a boat above it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives in it that anybody has come back to describe.
why.pressures: It is a tended monument that can no longer be tended, which the nearest village finds unbearable.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water dropped a metre the tribe would reclaim it and it would stop being a dungeon.

hardConstraints: fully submerged but for one chamber
clear enough water to read the geometry
places.hook: Six terraces of xanmeer under still water, entered head-down through the top of a tower.

places.name: One-Chest
places.whySiteWon: cove in lake & standing water (danger band 3), 225 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Somebody furnished a trapped air space inside a flooded structure, and whoever they are they chose this.
why.siteAdvantages: Enclosed by water on all sides; the only approach is a dive of about twenty metres.
why.occupantsMotive: One or two occupants, or their belongings.
why.pressures: Everything in it is too heavy to swim out with, which is deliberate.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water level fell the room becomes an ordinary cellar and worthless.

places.hook: A dry room with a chest in it, twenty metres down and no way in but a held breath.

places.name: Black-Cut Teeth
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in tidal delta (danger band 3), 402 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, route.

why.founding: Where the mangrove wall meets open water a shell bar has built up and been farmed for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow, sheltered mangrove reef, walkable at the lowest tides and picked over daily by anyone with a basket.
why.occupantsMotive: Two villages work alternate lots by an agreement nobody has written down.
why.pressures: The agreement is one bad season from being a fight.
why.wouldChangeIf: If either village lost its boats, the other would take the whole bar in a month.

places.hook: The coast's larder: shellfish, crab and reef weed a beginner can gather at low tide without drowning.

places.name: Lands-It-After-Dark
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 82 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Archon's customs desk is the only one on the coast that works, so the Oliis run grew a last stop short of it: a channel mouth where a hull can lie a night, break a cargo down and send it in by canoe in daylight, declared as something else.
why.siteAdvantages: A mangrove channel deep enough for a keeled hull, screened from the lane, within a night's paddle of the Archon quay.
why.occupantsMotive: Half-chartered crews out of the Oliis coast whose letters of marque cover the hull but not the hold, and factors in the city who prefer their goods undated.
why.pressures: The harbour authority sweeps the channels twice a season and always finds the wrong one; the League of Open Water tolerates the trade and taxes it privately.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Archon's customs stopped functioning the lay-by would be pointless and the trade would go straight to the quay.

hardConstraints: water deep enough for a keeled hull at any tide
no sightline from the Lilmoth-Archon lane
places.hook: The last stop before Archon customs, where a cargo becomes a different cargo — and where a broker will pay you to carry the difference.

places.name: Lost-The-Ospreye
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 318 m from the nearest route; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The outer bar the shipping lane keeps clear of, which is why it is still alive.
why.siteAdvantages: Clear water over a healthy reef in the outer mangrove channels, far enough out that nobody works it daily.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Divers come out for a day and go home.
why.pressures: It is the healthiest thing on the coast and the least defended.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the harvest lots moved out here, it would look like the Gap in fifteen years.

places.hook: Pearl beds under a living reef, and a flooded cut in the reef wall that only Argonian lungs will reach.

places.name: Shows-The-Wrong-Light
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 187 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Archon is the only lawful landing on this coast, so a hull that misses the estuary in weather looks for any light it can see. A shore gang worked out that a light in the wrong place is worth more than a light in the right one.
why.siteAdvantages: A shelving beach south of the estuary with a bar offshore and no settlement within sight of the fire.
why.occupantsMotive: Landless coast households who lost their fishing ground and found that a cargo comes ashore whether or not the crew does.
why.pressures: The harbour authority knows the beach exists and cannot prove which fire is which; the pilots of Portdun Mont lose a hull a season to it and want it burnt out.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the estuary marks were kept properly lit the gang would have nothing to imitate, and would go back to fishing or go to Alten Corimont.

hardConstraints: a shelving beach a laden hull can ground on
no settlement in line of sight of the fire
places.hook: The light on this beach is not the estuary light, and the cargo stacked behind it came off the last hull that believed it was.

places.name: Portdun Mont
places.whySiteWon: flood high in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 229 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The village grew on the rise behind the pilots' watch, above the beach landing and below the ridge line.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground above the flood, a clear view down the whole estuary approach, and a beach landing at the foot of the stair.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilot families who take fees to bring hulls in, and who remember when the fee was collected differently.
why.pressures: Archon's authority stops at the headland; the pilots' monopoly is customary, not legal, and the anchorage below the cliff has a past.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the harbour authority licensed its own pilots, Portdun Mont would be a fishing hamlet in a year.

hardConstraints: a bench above water with a landing below
places.hook: Every hull bound for Archon takes a pilot here first, so the village hears the coast's news before the city does.

places.name: The Three Tongues
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in tidal delta (danger band 2), 62 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A port needs paid lodging with a fire, a bed and a room full of people who know things.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay front, one door from the mooring line.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who trades in information as her actual business.
why.pressures: Three languages in one room and two of them are lying.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the port trade fell away this becomes a village inn and the coast loses its densest hook node.

hardConstraints: on a route with a landing
places.hook: Three languages in one room, a contract board on the wall, and a keeper whose actual trade is what she overhears.

places.name: Seafalls
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A drop in the river stops laden hulls dead, so everything going inland is unloaded, carried past the fall and loaded again — and a town grew on the carry.
why.siteAdvantages: The furthest point upriver a laden boat can reach, with landings above and below the drop and firm ground between them.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters, transfer clerks and hauliers whose entire livelihood is that the falls exist.
why.pressures: The navigable limit moves with the season and this year's board does not match last year's; the porters price accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the portage slipway above the falls were ever mechanised, the town's whole labour economy evaporates.

hardConstraints: landings above and below the drop
places.hook: Everything going inland is carried past the fall on somebody's back, and everyone who carries it knows what is in it.

places.name: Seven-Terrace
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 657 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: Deliberately closed by its own people, with its traps live and its vakka-stone mechanisms intact.
why.siteAdvantages: Seven terraces of dressed stone standing in D4 jungle with no tending path to them, which is why nobody reopened it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living; the mechanisms count as occupants.
why.pressures: The tending clan a valley away knows the door and will not open it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were opened, whatever it was closed against becomes everyone's problem.

places.hook: The only way in is up: seven terraces of climbable wall and a trapdoor on the top one.

places.name: Haj-Mota Wallow
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.gap-reef (+0.26).

why.founding: The animals that supply the shell trade have to live somewhere, and they live where the mud is deep and the water shallow.
why.siteAdvantages: Churned shallow mud at the delta edge, warm and food-rich.
why.occupantsMotive: A small number of very large animals and one abandoned set of cutter's tools.
why.pressures: The yard needs them and the villages fear them, in the same week.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the wallow were worked out the shell yard closes and the district's shields become imports.

places.hook: A haj-mota wallow at the delta edge: shell, bone and eggs, guarded by the thing that made the mud.

places.name: Climbs-The-Long-Back
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 444 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Above the flood line the ground rises in a long shelf, and a village that wanted to be above the wet season built along it rather than across it.
why.siteAdvantages: Drained firm ground with a spring head above it and one approach that four people can hold.
why.occupantsMotive: Households who grow on terraces and trade downhill.
why.pressures: The spring is the whole settlement and it is one collapse from failing.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the spring failed, the village would be on the coast within a season.

places.hook: The last dry beds before the deep jungle, kept by a village that will sell you rope and will not sell you a guide.

places.name: The Two-Hour Flat
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 85 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A delta flat that shortens the coast journey and is crossable only while the basin's tidal amplitude leaves it dry - in practice a short morning, and not the same morning twice.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm sand under shallow water at low tide, marked by a stake line laid generations ago.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on it; six people are usually waiting at the head.
why.pressures: The tide does not negotiate, the window is never the same length twice, and the body count is carved on the waiting shelter's post.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a causeway were ever built here, the whole district's travel times change and the shelter dies.

hardConstraints: firm bed under the marked line
places.hook: Two hours of firm sand twice a day; miss the window and the crossing is a swim in a running channel.

places.name: Four-Eight
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 3), 56 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Umbriel crossed this coast in 4E 48 and the bodies it left had to go somewhere the Hist could not be blamed for.
why.siteAdvantages: A tidal flat above the village line where the ground could be opened quickly and in quantity.
why.occupantsMotive: Bone-carriers still call here on the way south; nobody else does.
why.pressures: The dead here were stripped, so there is nothing to repatriate, which is the whole grievance.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a way were found to return even one of them, the Umbriel Witness Society gains its first real relic.

hardConstraints: ground that can be opened in quantity
places.hook: Four thousand eight hundred names cut into a tidal flat, and a cut in the ground you can still open.

places.name: Still-Water Sleeping-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 154 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The Hist opened a break in the canopy on a firm rise at the marsh edge, and the village that answered it has never moved.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm rise where the fringe marsh meets the jungle wall, with fresh water and a canopy break the Hist made itself.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe who trade with Archon and have no interest in living there.
why.pressures: The port wants their timber and their labour; the village supplies exactly as much as it chooses.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Hist stopped speaking, the village disperses and Archon gains a hundred Hist-less households.

hardConstraints: a living Hist with a canopy break
places.hook: A Hist village that still answers its tree, and the nearest bed to Archon that owes the city nothing.
